# C-UI-KIT (@adhamaa/ui-kit) v0.9.1

> Shared, themeable React 19 UI kit for INFRACIVIC apps, built on ui-sdk (behaviour and accessibility) with the kit's own CSS. Install `@adhamaa/ui-kit` only; it brings ui-sdk, so never install `@ui-sdk/*`. `@adhamaa/ui-kit/table` (DataTable) also needs `ag-grid-community` and `ag-grid-react`; `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form` (react-hook-form fields) needs `react-hook-form`. Load `@adhamaa/ui-kit/styles.css` once and wrap the app in `UIKitProvider`.

# INFRACIVIC UI Kit

`@adhamaa/ui-kit` is a set of basic React components shared by every INFRACIVIC app. It covers:

- **Form fields:** text, number, password, textarea, select, multi-select, autocomplete, infinite select, checkbox, switch, radio, chip, segmented control, date, month, time, file and colour.
- **react-hook-form bindings** for every field, plus `FormFields` and `FormDialog` for config-driven forms.
- **DataTable**, built on AG Grid Community, with a toolbar, row actions, number formatting and client or server pagination.
- **Overlays:** `Dialog`, `ConfirmDialog`, `modals.open()`, `ActionMenu` (flat, or grouped under headings with descriptions), `Popover`, `toast()`.
- **Display:** `Badge`, `Card`, `Breadcrumb`, `EmptyState`, `Timeline`, `ImagePreviewer`, `Pagination`, `Loader`, `Avatar`, `Skeleton`, `LoadingOverlay`.
- **Navigation and disclosure:** `Tabs`, `Accordion`, `Tooltip`, `ScrollArea`.

The behaviour (keyboard handling, focus, ARIA) comes from [ui-sdk](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ui-sdk/react). The kit adds a consistent look and simple, prop-based APIs on top.

## Built to be themed

Every colour, radius and font comes from CSS variables. Each app applies its own brand with `defineTheme()` or a few lines of CSS, and every component follows it, the data table included. Use the **Theme** and **Scheme** switches in the toolbar above to see the same components as SWIFTO, or in dark mode.

## Where to go next

- **Getting started:** install the package, load the styles, add the provider.
- **Theming:** brand colours, dark mode and the AG Grid theme.
- **Forms with react-hook-form:** the `RHF*` fields and config-driven forms.
- **Migrating from SWIFTO:** how the old Mantine components map onto the kit.
- **Components:** every component, with live controls and a props table.

## Requirements

- React 19 or newer (a ui-sdk requirement).
- `react-hook-form` 7.50 or newer, only for `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form`.
- `ag-grid-community` and `ag-grid-react` 35 or 36, only for `@adhamaa/ui-kit/table`.
- Any framework: Next.js (App or Pages router), Vite or anything else. Every component is a client component.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/introduction--docs

---

# Getting started

## 1. Let npm find the package

The kit is a private package on GitHub Packages. Add this line to your app's `.npmrc`, next to `package.json`. It holds no secret, so commit it:

```ini
@adhamaa:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
```

Then give your own machine a token, once:

1. On GitHub, open **Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic)**.
2. Create a token with only the **`read:packages`** scope. GitHub's npm registry doesn't accept fine-grained tokens.
3. Add it to the `.npmrc` in your **home folder** (`~/.npmrc`, or `C:\Users\<you>\.npmrc` on Windows), never the project's:

```ini
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=ghp_your_token_here
```

**Deploy servers** (QA, prod, and the Docker build host) need the same line in their `~/.npmrc`. Use a token from a bot or machine account so deploys don't depend on one person. See *Server setup* in the repository README.

## 2. Install

```bash
yarn add @adhamaa/ui-kit
```

That's all most apps need. ui-sdk comes with the kit, so don't install `@ui-sdk/*` yourself: a second copy would split its React context. Requires React 19 or newer.

### Optional: tables and react-hook-form

Two parts of the kit live in their own entry points and need a library the kit doesn't install for you. Add one only if your app imports that entry point:

| If you import | Install |
| --- | --- |
| `@adhamaa/ui-kit/table` (`DataTable`) | `yarn add ag-grid-community ag-grid-react` (35 or 36) |
| `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form` (`RHF*` fields, `FormFields`, `FormDialog`) | `yarn add react-hook-form` (7.50 or newer) |

If you import one of these without its library, the build fails with a "module not found" error naming the package to add.

## 3. Load the styles once

**With Tailwind CSS v4**, at the top of your global stylesheet:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@adhamaa/ui-kit/styles.css" layer(components);
```

The kit's stylesheet already includes ui-sdk's base styles. Putting it in Tailwind's `components` layer keeps Tailwind's base reset from undoing them, while utility classes still win. So `className="mt-4"` on any kit component works.

**Without Tailwind**, import it once at your app's entry, such as `app/layout.tsx` or `main.tsx`:

```ts
import '@adhamaa/ui-kit/styles.css'
```

## 4. Add the provider

```tsx
import { UIKitProvider, swiftoTheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

export default function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <UIKitProvider theme={swiftoTheme} defaultColorScheme="light">
      {children}
    </UIKitProvider>
  )
}
```

The provider applies the theme and hosts the toast region and the modal stack. In a Next.js App Router project, put it in a `'use client'` providers file and render that from `app/layout.tsx`.

## 5. Use components

```tsx
import { Button, TextInput, toast } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
import { DataTable } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/table'
import { RHFTextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'
```

The package has three entry points, so an app that never uses tables or react-hook-form doesn't load them:

| Import from | Contains | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `…/ui-kit` | Theme, fields, overlays, display | (ui-sdk is included) |
| `…/ui-kit/form` | `RHF*` fields, `FormFields`, `FormDialog` | react-hook-form |
| `…/ui-kit/table` | `DataTable`, AG Grid theme, cell editors | AG Grid |

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/getting-started--docs

---

# Theming

Every component reads its colours, radius and fonts from CSS variables. The colours that ui-sdk already defines keep its names (`--ui-primary`, `--ui-border`, …). The kit adds a few of its own (`--kit-success`, `--kit-table-header`, …).

## Use a preset

```tsx
import { UIKitProvider, neutralTheme, swiftoTheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

<UIKitProvider theme={swiftoTheme}>…</UIKitProvider>
```

- `neutralTheme`: slate greys with a blue primary. It's the default.
- `swiftoTheme`: SWIFTO's gold and slate palette, Helvetica / Noto Sans.

## Define your app's theme

```ts
import { defineTheme, extendTheme, neutralTheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

// From scratch: anything left out keeps the default.
export const claimsTheme = defineTheme({
  name: 'claims',
  colors: {
    primary: ['oklch(0.55 0.2 260)', 'oklch(0.7 0.15 260)'], // [light, dark]
    primaryForeground: 'white',                               // same in both
    primarySoft: ['oklch(0.96 0.03 260)', 'oklch(0.3 0.06 260)'],
  },
  scalars: { radius: '0.5rem', fontSans: '"Inter", sans-serif' },
})

// Or start from a preset.
export const myTheme = extendTheme(neutralTheme, { colors: { primary: '#0f766e' } })
```

A colour is a single CSS colour, or a `[light, dark]` pair. Pairs compile to CSS `light-dark()`, so changing scheme needs no re-render.

### Colour tokens

| Token | Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` / `foreground` | `--ui-background` / `--ui-foreground` | Page and text |
| `muted` / `mutedForeground` | `--ui-muted` / `--ui-muted-foreground` | Quiet surfaces, secondary text |
| `border` / `input` | `--ui-border` / `--ui-input` | Dividers / field borders |
| `ring` / `ringBorder` | `--ui-ring` / `--ui-ring-border` | Focus glow / focused border |
| `primary` / `primaryForeground` | `--ui-primary` / `--ui-primary-foreground` | Filled buttons, checked controls |
| `primarySoft` / `primarySoftForeground` | `--kit-primary-soft` / `…-foreground` | Light buttons, selected options, current page |
| `destructive` / `destructiveForeground` | `--ui-destructive` / `--kit-destructive-foreground` | Errors, danger buttons |
| `success`, `warning`, `info` (+ `…Foreground`) | `--kit-success`, … | Badges, toasts, timeline |
| `surface` / `surfaceRaised` | `--kit-surface` / `--kit-surface-raised` | Dropzones / dialogs, cards, popovers |
| `tableHeader` / `tableHeaderForeground` / `tableRowHover` | `--kit-table-*` | DataTable |

### Scalar tokens

`radius`, `radiusSm`, `radiusLg`, `fontSans`, `fontMono`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `spacing`, `shadow`, `shadowLg`.

## Theme with CSS only

You don't need the provider's theme. Pass `theme={null}` and set the variables in your own CSS:

```css
:root {
  --ui-primary: light-dark(#0f766e, #2dd4bf);
  --ui-primary-foreground: white;
  --ui-radius: 0.5rem;
}
```

To read a token in JavaScript, like for a chart, use `tokenVar('primary')`, which returns `'var(--ui-primary)'`.

Disabled and read-only fields have their own optional variables, so an app can give them a plain look without changing `--ui-muted` everywhere:

```css
:root {
  --kit-disabled-bg: #f8fafc;       /* default: var(--ui-muted) */
  --kit-disabled-border: transparent; /* default: var(--ui-input) */
  --kit-disabled-fg: #64748b;       /* default: var(--ui-muted-foreground) */
}
```

## Light and dark

```tsx
<UIKitProvider defaultColorScheme="auto">  {/* follows the OS */}
```

```tsx
import { useColorScheme, ColorSchemeToggle } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

const { colorScheme, setColorScheme, toggleColorScheme } = useColorScheme()
<ColorSchemeToggle />
```

The scheme sets `color-scheme` on `<html>`, plus `data-theme="dark"` and the `dark` class, so Tailwind's `dark:` variant works too. The user's choice is remembered in localStorage; turn that off with `persistColorScheme={false}`.

## The data table follows the theme

`DataTable` uses `createAgGridTheme()`, which is AG Grid's Quartz theme wired to the same variables. To use AG Grid directly elsewhere with the same look:

```tsx
import { createAgGridTheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/table'

const gridTheme = createAgGridTheme({ rowVerticalPaddingScale: 0.8 })
<AgGridReact theme={gridTheme} … />
```

## Override one component

Every component accepts `className`, and form fields accept `classNames` per part (`root`, `label`, `control`, `description`, `error`):

```tsx
<TextInput label="Code" classNames={{ label: 'uppercase tracking-wide', control: 'bg-amber-50' }} />
```

The kit's styles live in the `ui-kit` cascade layer, so your classes win without `!important`.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/theming--docs

---

# Forms with react-hook-form

Import from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form`. Every kit field has an `RHF` version that takes the field's own props plus:

| Prop | |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The form field. Required. |
| `rules` | Validation rules, as in `register`. `required` also shows the asterisk. |
| `defaultValue` | The field's default, if the form has none. |
| `control` | Only when the field isn't inside `<FormProvider>`. |

```tsx
import { useForm, FormProvider } from 'react-hook-form'
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'
import { RHFTextInput, RHFSelect, RHFDatePicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

const methods = useForm({ resolver: zodResolver(schema) })

<FormProvider {...methods}>
  <form onSubmit={methods.handleSubmit(save)}>
    <RHFTextInput name="package_name" label="Package name" />
    <RHFSelect name="state" label="State" data={states} />
    <RHFDatePicker name="start_date" label="Start date" />
  </form>
</FormProvider>
```

The kit doesn't depend on zod or any other schema library; use whichever resolver your app has.

## Available fields

`RHFTextInput`, `RHFPasswordInput`, `RHFTextarea`, `RHFNumberInput`, `RHFSelect`, `RHFMultiSelect`, `RHFAutocomplete`, `RHFInfiniteSelect`, `RHFCheckbox`, `RHFSwitch`, `RHFRadioGroup`, `RHFChip`, `RHFSegmentedControl`, `RHFDatePicker`, `RHFMonthPicker`, `RHFTimeInput`, `RHFFileInput`, `RHFColorInput`.

## Value types

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Text, password, textarea, autocomplete | `string` |
| Number | `number \| null` |
| Select, radio, segmented | `string \| null` |
| Multi-select | `string[]` |
| Checkbox, switch, chip | `boolean` |
| Date | `'YYYY-MM-DD' \| null` |
| Time | `'HH:mm' \| null` |
| File | `File \| null`, or `File[]` with `multiple` |
| Colour | CSS colour string |

## Error messages

A failed rule shows its own message (`rules={{ required: 'Enter a name' }}`). A rule without one shows the default, *This field is required*. Change the default for a whole subtree:

```tsx
<RHFFieldDefaults requiredMessage="Wajib diisi">…</RHFFieldDefaults>
```

## Infinite and server-searched selects

`InfiniteSelect` and `RHFInfiniteSelect` take one function that fetches a page. They debounce search, load more on scroll, cancel stale requests and remember labels of selected values:

```tsx
<RHFInfiniteSelect
  name="contractor_uuid"
  label="Contractor"
  initialOptions={record ? [{ value: record.contractor_uuid, label: record.contractor_name }] : []}
  loadOptions={async ({ search, page, signal }) => {
    const res = await services.contractors.list({ search, page: page + 1, per_page: 20 }, { signal })
    return {
      options: res.data.map((c) => ({ value: c.uuid, label: c.name })),
      hasMore: res.meta.current_page < res.meta.last_page,
    }
  }}
/>
```

It doesn't depend on TanStack Query. If your data already comes from `useInfiniteQuery`, pass it to a plain `Select` or `MultiSelect` with `data`, `hasMore`, `onLoadMore`, `loading` and `onSearchChange`.

## Config-driven forms

`FormFields` renders fields from an array, and `FormDialog` wraps that in a dialog with Cancel and Submit:

```tsx
import { FormDialog, openFormDialog } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

openFormDialog({
  title: 'Add item',
  fields: [
    { name: 'item_name', label: 'Item name', type: 'text', required: true },
    { group: [
      { name: 'unit', label: 'Unit', type: 'select', options: ['m', 'm²'] },
      { name: 'rate', label: 'Rate', type: 'number' },
    ] },
    { name: 'photo', label: 'Photo', type: 'custom', render: () => <MyUploader /> },
  ],
  onSubmit: (values) => createItem.mutateAsync(values), // stays open, pending, until it resolves
})
```

Field `type`s: `text`, `email`, `number`, `password`, `textarea`, `select`, `multiselect`, `radio`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `date`, `time`, `file`, `custom`. Pass any other prop of the underlying component through `props`.

## Binding your own component

```tsx
import { createRHFField } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

const RHFRating = createRHFField(Rating, ({ field }) => ({
  value: field.value ?? 0,
  onChange: field.onChange,
}))
```

The component receives `name`, `ref`, `error` (the message) and `withAsterisk` automatically.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/forms-with-react-hook-form--docs

---

# Migrating from SWIFTO's components

The kit started as SWIFTO's `src/components/ui`, rebuilt on ui-sdk instead of Mantine. Prop names were kept where they made sense, so most changes are a new import.

## Component map

| SWIFTO | Kit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AgGridTable` | `DataTable` (`/table`) | Same props. Set `tableSettings.autoFormatColumns` to keep the old column formatting by name, and pass `renderIcon` for Iconify string icons. |
| `swiftoAgGridTheme` | `createAgGridTheme()` | Follows the kit theme instead of fixed colours. |
| `Forms/RHFTextInput` … | `RHFTextInput` … (`/form`) | Same `name`, `rules`, `defaultValue`. |
| `RHFComboSelect` | `RHFSelect` with async props, or `RHFInfiniteSelect` | |
| `RHFComboMultiSelect`, `RHFMultiSelect` | `RHFMultiSelect` | `creatable` + `onCreateOption` kept. |
| `RHFDatePickerInput`, `RHFDateInput` | `RHFDatePicker` | Values are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, as in Mantine 8; other date strings (like `Sat, 21 Nov 2026 06:21:58 GMT`) are read too. Mantine's `valueFormat="DD MMMM YYYY"` becomes `displayFormat={{ day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }}` with `locale="en-GB"`, which also makes the field a press-to-pick button like Mantine's. |
| Mantine `MonthPickerInput` | `MonthPicker` / `RHFMonthPicker` | Values are `YYYY-MM` strings; `toMonthString()` converts a `Date`. |
| Mantine `Menu` with `Menu.Label` sections | `ActionMenu` with `{ type: 'group', label, items }` | Items take `description` and `activeIcon`. |
| `RHFFieldDefaults` | `RHFFieldDefaults` | Unchanged. |
| `Modal.confirm` | `modals.confirm()` | |
| `Modal.form` | `openFormDialog()` / `FormDialog` | Field config is close; see below. |
| `Modal.table` | `modals.open({ children: <DataTable … /> })` | |
| `Modal.imagePreview` | `ImagePreviewer` | |
| `Modal.comingSoon`, `ComingSoon` | `EmptyState`, or `modals.open` with one | |
| `Toast.success/warning/error` | `toast.success/warning/error` | Also `info`, `loading`, actions and updates. |
| `Timeline`, `StatusTimeline`, `ActivityTimeline` | `Timeline` | `variant="status" \| "activity"`. For SWIFTO's look add `appearance="card"`, plus `alternating` for stages (SWIFTO's default). Events take `dateTime`/`time` instead of `timestamp`; `date`, `actor`, `department`, `stage`, `reason`, `sentFrom` and `metadata` keep their names. |
| `BreadcrumbsSection` | `Breadcrumb` | Pass `items` and `linkComponent={Link}`. Route-data logic stays in the app. |
| `StaggeredDotsLoader` | `Loader` | |
| `ColorSchemeSwitcher` | `ColorSchemeToggle` | |
| Mantine `AppShell` (`header`, `navbar`, `AppShell.Main`) | `AppShell` | Parts `Header`, `Sidebar`, `Main`, `Footer`. `navbar.width` becomes `sidebarWidth={{ full, mini }}`, `navbar.breakpoint` becomes `breakpoint`, and `layout="alt"` is the kit's default `layout="sidebar"`. The collapsed state is `sidebarState` (`full`, `mini`, `hidden`); save it yourself. Below the breakpoint the sidebar is a drawer that `AppShell.MenuButton` opens. |

**Not in the kit**, and they stay in the app: `Header`, `Navigation`, `UserButton`, `Logo`, `AppMain` (the frame itself is the kit's `AppShell`), domain icons, `ProcessStage`, `DetailHeaderActions`, `PublishedBadge`, `CoordinateInput*`, `GoogleMaps`, `RHFDropzoneWithPublishToAtm`, `SessionDebugger`, and the RHF-backed cell editors (`TextCellEditor`, `NumberCellEditor` and `ImageCellEditor` read and write form context by row uuid). The kit's own `TextCellEditor` and `NumberCellEditor` are plain AG Grid editors.

## Mantine props

| Mantine | Kit |
| --- | --- |
| `withAsterisk` | `withAsterisk`, or `required` |
| `error` | `error` |
| `leftSection` / `rightSection` | Same |
| `classNames={{ input }}` | `classNames={{ control }}` |
| `size="xs" … "xl"` | `xs` … `lg` |
| `data` on Select | Same shape: strings, `{ value, label }`, `{ group, items }` |
| `onChange(event)` on TextInput | Same, plus `onValueChange(value)` |
| `onChange(value)` on NumberInput | `onChange(number \| null)`. It never gives a string. |
| `autosize`, `minRows`, `maxRows` on Textarea | Same |
| `styles={…}` | Not supported. Use `className`/`classNames` or theme tokens. |
| `variant="filled"` etc. on Button | `filled`, `light`, `outline`, `subtle`, `default`, `danger` |

## Style overrides

SWIFTO overrides like `classNames={{ root: '!bg-[var(--color-swifto-brand-200)]' }}` exist to brand Mantine. With `swiftoTheme` applied the kit is already branded, so drop them rather than port them.

## Gradual migration

During the move, SWIFTO keeps `src/components/ui/*` as thin re-exports of the kit, so imports don't change all at once. Each later PR removes one folder's shim and points imports at the package directly.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/migrating-from-swifto--docs

---

# Use with AI

AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex…) can read these docs, so they suggest the kit's real components and props instead of guessing. There are two ways to give them the docs, and both are free and need nothing installed in your app.

## MCP server (recommended)

Connect your assistant to the kit's MCP server. It's served by [GitMCP](https://gitmcp.io), a free service that reads the docs published on this site.

```
https://adhamaa.gitmcp.io/C-UI-KIT-docs
```

**Claude Code**, from your app's folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http c-ui-kit https://adhamaa.gitmcp.io/C-UI-KIT-docs
```

**Cursor**: add to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your app:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "c-ui-kit": { "url": "https://adhamaa.gitmcp.io/C-UI-KIT-docs" }
  }
}
```

**VS Code (Copilot)**: add to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "c-ui-kit": { "type": "http", "url": "https://adhamaa.gitmcp.io/C-UI-KIT-docs" }
  }
}
```

**Codex**: add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.c-ui-kit]
url = "https://adhamaa.gitmcp.io/C-UI-KIT-docs"
```

Check it works by asking: *"Using the c-ui-kit MCP, list the kit's components."*

### What the assistant can do with it

| Tool | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch_C_UI_KIT_docs_documentation` | Reads the index: every component and guide, with a one-line summary and a link |
| `fetch_generic_url_content` | Reads one page from the index, like `…/llms/components/multi-select.md`: props table, examples and usage notes |
| `search_C_UI_KIT_docs_docs` | Searches the docs. It may return the index until GitMCP has indexed the site |

Assistants usually read the index first, then the page for the component they need.

## Plain text, without MCP

For tools that don't support MCP, point them at these files:

| File | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| [`llms.txt`](https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/llms.txt) | The index, following the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/llms-full.txt) | Every page in one file (about 270 KB) |
| `llms/components/<name>.md` | One page per component, like [`select.md`](https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/llms/components/select.md) |

## Tell the assistant about the kit

Paste this into your app's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, so the assistant uses the kit without being asked each time:

```md
## UI components

- Build UI with `@adhamaa/ui-kit` (C-UI-KIT). Look up components and props with the
  `c-ui-kit` MCP server, or https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/llms.txt.
- Import components from `@adhamaa/ui-kit`, the DataTable from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/table`,
  and react-hook-form fields (`RHF*`, `FormFields`, `FormDialog`) from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form`.
- Never install or import `@ui-sdk/*`: the kit brings it.
- Style with the theme tokens (`var(--ui-primary)`, `tokenVar('border')`…), not hard-coded colours.
```

## How it stays current

Every `yarn deploy-docs` regenerates the text files from the same JSDoc, stories and docs pages as this site, so the MCP server always describes the latest published version. If your app is on an older version, check its changelog for props that were added since.

The docs are only as good as their source. When you add or change a component, write its JSDoc and docs page for someone, or something, that has never seen it. See **Contributing**.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/use-with-ai--docs

---

# UIKitProvider

Applies a theme and hosts the toast region and modal stack. Place it once, near the root of the app. Every page of these docs is rendered inside one.

```tsx
import { UIKitProvider } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
import '@adhamaa/ui-kit/styles.css'
import { UIKitProvider, swiftoTheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

export function Root() {
  return (
    <UIKitProvider theme={swiftoTheme} defaultColorScheme="light">
      <App />
    </UIKitProvider>
  )
}
```

## What it does

- **Theme:** injects a `<style>` tag with the theme's CSS variables. Pass a preset (`neutralTheme`, default, or `swiftoTheme`) or your own from `defineTheme()` / `extendTheme()`. Pass `null` when the app sets the CSS variables itself.
- **Colour scheme:** starts in `defaultColorScheme` (`auto` follows the operating system), and remembers the user's choice in localStorage unless `persistColorScheme={false}`.
- **Toasts:** renders the `Toaster`, so `toast()` works anywhere. Turn it off with `withToaster={false}` if you place `<Toaster />` yourself.
- **Modals:** renders the stack for `modals.open()` and `modals.confirm()`. Turn it off with `withModals={false}`.

With a Content Security Policy, pass `nonce` so the injected style tag is allowed.

## Next.js

The provider uses state and effects, so render it from a client component:

```tsx
// app/providers.tsx
'use client'
import { UIKitProvider } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <UIKitProvider>{children}</UIKitProvider>
}
```

## Props

See the props of `UIKitProvider` on the docs page or in its TypeScript types.

## Related

- **Theming** and **Tokens**: defining a theme and what each token does.
- **ColorSchemeToggle** and `useColorScheme`: changing the scheme.
- **Toast** and **Dialog** (`modals`): what the provider hosts.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-theming-uikitprovider--docs

---

# Contributing

How to add a component to the kit, and how to document it so its page matches the rest. **Button**, **Select** and **Dialog** are the reference pages: copy one when you start.

## Where things live

```
packages/ui-kit/src/components/<Name>/<Name>.tsx   the component, with JSDoc on every prop
packages/ui-kit/src/styles/<area>.css             its styles, in @layer ui-kit
apps/docs/src/stories/<Category>/<Name>.stories.tsx   its stories
apps/docs/src/stories/<Category>/<Name>.mdx           its docs page
```

Categories, in sidebar order: **Buttons**, **Inputs**, **Combobox**, **Dates**, **Overlays**, **Feedback**, **Data display**, **Navigation**, **Theming**, **Table**. The story `title` is `Components/<Category>/<Name>`.

## 1. Write JSDoc on the component

The props table is generated from it, so this is where most of the reference docs come from.

```tsx
export type BadgeProps = {
  /** @default 'light' */
  variant?: 'light' | 'filled' | 'outline' | 'dot'
  /** Content before the label, usually an icon. */
  leftSection?: React.ReactNode
}

/**
 * A short label for a status or a count.
 *
 * @example
 * <Badge color="success">Approved</Badge>
 */
export function Badge(props: BadgeProps) { … }
```

- One line per prop that says what it does, not what type it is.
- Add `@default` for every prop with a default.
- Give the component a summary and an `@example`.

## 2. Write the stories

One `.stories.tsx` file per component.

```tsx
const meta = {
  title: 'Components/Data display/Badge',
  component: Badge,
  tags: ['!autodocs'],          // the .mdx file is the docs page
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
  args: { children: 'Approved' },
  argTypes: {
    variant: { control: 'inline-radio', options: ['light', 'filled', 'outline', 'dot'] },
  },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Badge>

export const Playground: Story = {}
export const Variants: Story = { render: (args) => … }
```

- Start with a `Playground` story with no args of its own, so the Controls drive it.
- Spread `args` into `render` stories (`<Badge {...args} variant="dot" />`), so toolbar changes reach them.
- Use `fn()` from `storybook/test` for callbacks, so calls show in the Actions panel.
- Use realistic INFRACIVIC data: packages, routes, contractors, states. Avoid "foo" and "Lorem ipsum".
- For components with real interaction (pickers, overlays, tables), add `play` tests: open it, pick something with the mouse, do the same with the keyboard, and check focus. See `Select.stories.tsx` and `Dialog.stories.tsx`.

## 3. Write the docs page

Copy this template to `<Name>.mdx` and fill it in. Sections marked *(complex only)* are required for form controls, overlays and data display, and optional for small components.

````mdx
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Badge.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Badge

One or two sentences: what it does and when to reach for it.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Badge } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Variants} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Variants
### Sizes
### …one heading per story, each with a sentence and a <Canvas>

## Composition            ← only if it has parts or sub-components

## Use with react-hook-form   ← only if an RHF* version exists

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling                ← (complex only) kit-* classes, data-* attributes, tokens

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk <Name>](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/<name>).
A keyboard table, plus anything the kit adds or changes.

## Usage guidelines       ← (complex only) Do / Don't

## Related                ← (complex only)
````

## Writing style

- Write for an app developer who has never seen the component.
- Use short sentences and the second person: "Pass `value` to control it."
- Lead each example with what it's for, then show it.
- Link to ui-sdk for behaviour the kit doesn't change. Only spell out what the kit adds.
- Show code people can copy: real imports, real prop names.

## Before you open a PR

- [ ] Every prop has JSDoc, with `@default` where it has one.
- [ ] Stories cover each variant, size and state.
- [ ] The docs page follows the template and renders with no errors.
- [ ] The **Accessibility** panel shows no violations on any story.
- [ ] `play` tests pass in the **Interactions** panel (if any).
- [ ] Both themes and both schemes look right (toolbar switches).
- [ ] `yarn lint`, `yarn type-check` and `yarn build-storybook` pass.
- [ ] A changeset if the package changed (`yarn changeset`).

## Publishing the docs

The docs are published to GitHub Pages at https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/, from the public repo `adhamaa/C-UI-KIT-docs`. Until the org's GitHub Actions work again, publish by hand after a release or a docs fix:

```sh
yarn deploy-docs
```

It builds Storybook, generates the AI-readable text (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a Markdown page per component, from the Storybook manifests), and pushes `apps/docs/storybook-static` to the `gh-pages` branch of the docs repo. You need push access to that repo. Set `DOCS_REPO` to publish somewhere else, for example a fork.

The kit's MCP server (see **Use with AI**) reads that text, so your JSDoc, stories and docs pages are what AI assistants learn from. Keep them complete, and run `yarn build-storybook && yarn build-llms` to preview the output in `apps/docs/storybook-static/llms/`.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/contributing--docs

---

# Tokens

Every component reads its colours, radius, shadows, fonts and heights from CSS variables. The swatches below show the live values. Use the **Theme** and **Scheme** switches in the toolbar to see them change.

To change a token for your app, use `defineTheme()` or `extendTheme()`. See **Theming**. To use one in your own code, read the variable, or call `tokenVar()` in JavaScript:

```tsx
import { tokenVar } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

<div style={{ color: tokenVar('mutedForeground') }} />   // var(--ui-muted-foreground)
```

```css
.my-panel {
  background: var(--kit-surface-raised);
  border: 1px solid var(--ui-border);
  border-radius: var(--ui-radius);
}
```

## Colours

Variables named `--ui-*` are shared with ui-sdk. Variables named `--kit-*` are the kit's own. Each colour has a light and a dark value.

```tsx
const Colors = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 24 }}>
    {colorGroups.map((group) => (
      <section key={group.title}>
        <h3 style={{ margin: '0 0 8px', fontSize: 14 }}>{group.title}</h3>
        <div
          style={{
            display: 'grid',
            gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fill, minmax(180px, 1fr))',
            gap: 12,
          }}
        >
          {group.tokens.map((token) => (
            <div key={token} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6 }}>
              <div
                style={{
                  height: 56,
                  borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
                  background: `var(${colorTokenVars[token]})`,
                  border: '1px solid var(--ui-border)',
                }}
              />
              <span style={label}>{token}</span>
              <span style={code}>{colorTokenVars[token]}</span>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </section>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

Pair each background token with its `…Foreground` token for text on it, so the contrast holds in both schemes.

## Radius

`radius` is the default for fields and buttons. `radiusSm` is for small inner parts like list items and chips. `radiusLg` is for floating layers and containers like dropdown lists, cards and dialogs.

```tsx
const Radius = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 24, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
    {radii.map((token) => (
      <div key={token} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6 }}>
        <div
          style={{
            width: 96,
            height: 64,
            background: 'var(--kit-primary-soft)',
            border: '1px solid var(--ui-primary)',
            borderRadius: `var(${scalarTokenVars[token]})`,
          }}
        />
        <span style={label}>{token}</span>
        <span style={code}>{scalarTokenVars[token]}</span>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Shadows

`shadow` is for slightly raised elements. `shadowLg` is for floating layers like dropdown lists, menus and dialogs.

```tsx
const Shadows = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 32, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
    {shadows.map((token) => (
      <div key={token} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6 }}>
        <div
          style={{
            width: 140,
            height: 80,
            background: 'var(--kit-surface-raised)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
            boxShadow: `var(${scalarTokenVars[token]})`,
          }}
        />
        <span style={label}>{token}</span>
        <span style={code}>{scalarTokenVars[token]}</span>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Typography

`fontSans` is the interface font. `fontMono` is for codes, IDs and numbers that should line up. `fontSize` and `lineHeight` set the base text size.

```tsx
const Typography = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <div>
      <div style={{ fontFamily: 'var(--ui-font-sans)', fontSize: 20 }}>
        The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 0123456789
      </div>
      <span style={label}>fontSans</span>{' '}
      <span style={code}>--ui-font-sans</span>
    </div>
    <div>
      <div style={{ fontFamily: 'var(--ui-font-mono)', fontSize: 16 }}>
        PKG-004 · 12,480.50 · {'{ status: "draft" }'}
      </div>
      <span style={label}>fontMono</span>{' '}
      <span style={code}>--ui-font-mono</span>
    </div>
  </div>
);
```

## Control heights

Buttons, inputs and selects of the same `size` share a height, so they line up in a row. These variables aren't part of the theme API. Override them in CSS if you need to.

```tsx
const ControlHeights = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 16, alignItems: 'flex-end' }}>
    {heights.map((size) => (
      <div
        key={size}
        style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6, justifyItems: 'center' }}
      >
        <div
          style={{
            width: 64,
            height: `var(--kit-h-${size})`,
            background: 'var(--kit-primary-soft)',
            border: '1px solid var(--ui-primary)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--kit-radius-sm)',
          }}
        />
        <span style={label}>{size}</span>
        <span style={code}>--kit-h-{size}</span>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/tokens--docs

# Button

Import: `import { Button } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Runs an action. It comes in six variants and four sizes, takes icons on either side, and stays pending while an async `onClick` runs, so a form can't be submitted twice.

```tsx
import { Button, IconButton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Variants = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
    {variants.map((variant) => (
      <Button key={variant} {...args} variant={variant}>
        {variant === 'danger'
          ? 'Delete'
          : variant[0].toUpperCase() + variant.slice(1)}
      </Button>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Playground

Change the props below to see every combination.

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Button variant="filled" size="md" onClick={() => {}}>Save package</Button>;
```

## Examples

### Variants

| Variant | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `filled` (default) | The main action on a page or in a dialog. Use one per view. |
| `light` | A secondary action that should still stand out. |
| `outline` | A secondary action next to a filled button. |
| `subtle` | Low-emphasis actions in toolbars, table rows and cards. |
| `default` | Neutral actions like Cancel or Back. |
| `danger` | Destructive actions like Delete. Pair it with a confirmation. |

The preview at the top of the page shows all six.

### Sizes

`size` sets the height from the `--kit-h-*` tokens: `xs` 28px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px (default), `lg` 44px. Form fields use the same scale, so a button and a field of the same size line up.

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    {sizes.map((size) => (
      <Button key={size} {...args} size={size}>
        Size {size}
      </Button>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### With icons

`leftSection` and `rightSection` take any node, usually one of the kit's `icons`. Put a forward-pointing icon on the right and an add or action icon on the left.

```tsx
const WithIcons = () => <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12 }}>
    <Button
        variant="filled"
        size="md"
        onClick={() => {}}
        leftSection={<icons.PlusIcon />}>Add package
              </Button>
    <Button
        size="md"
        onClick={() => {}}
        variant="default"
        rightSection={<icons.ChevronRightIcon />}>Next
              </Button>
</div>;
```

### Icon only

Use `IconButton` for a button with no visible text. It is square, defaults to the `subtle` variant, and **requires `aria-label`**, which TypeScript enforces.

```tsx
const IconOnly = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    <IconButton aria-label="Refresh">
      <icons.RefreshIcon />
    </IconButton>
    <IconButton aria-label="More actions" variant="default">
      <icons.DotsVerticalIcon />
    </IconButton>
    <IconButton aria-label="Add" variant="filled" size="lg">
      <icons.PlusIcon />
    </IconButton>
  </div>
);
```

### Loading

`loading` shows a spinner in place of the left section and blocks presses. The button stays focusable, so keyboard users don't lose their place.

```tsx
const Loading = () => <Button variant="filled" size="md" onClick={() => {}} loading>Saving</Button>;
```

### Async click

Return a Promise from `onClick` and the button becomes pending until it settles: it gets `aria-busy`, ignores more presses and, if the action takes longer than a second, tells screen readers it's loading. You don't need a `loading` state of your own for this.

```tsx
const AsyncClick = () => <Button
    variant="filled"
    size="md"
    onClick={fn(() => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000)))}>Submit (1s)</Button>;
```

```tsx
<Button onClick={() => api.savePackage(values)}>Save</Button>
```

This tracks the Promise from the button's own `onClick`. For a form's async `onSubmit`, keep a pending flag and pass it to `loading` instead.

### Disabled and full width

```tsx
const Disabled = () => <Button variant="filled" size="md" onClick={() => {}} disabled>Save package</Button>;
```
```tsx
const FullWidth = () => <Button variant="filled" size="md" onClick={() => {}} fullWidth>Save package</Button>;
```

## Props

### Button

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Styles, or a function of the part's state that returns them. |
| `onClick` | `((event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>, details: ActionDetails) => unknown)` |  | Runs when the button is pressed. Return a Promise to make the button pending until it settles: it gets `aria-busy`, `aria-disabled` and `data-pending`, keeps focus, ignores presses meanwhile, so a form can't submit twice, and says `pendingAnnouncement` after a second. The event's element is whatever `render` renders, like a link. `details.source` says how it was pressed, for changes made after an `await`. |
| `type` | `enum` | `button` | What a native button does in a form: `"submit"` submits it and `"reset"` resets it. Ignored when the button renders as something else. @defaultValue "button" |
| `render` | `RenderProp<ButtonState>` |  | Renders your own element: one that receives the part's props, or a function of the props and the state. |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Keeps a disabled button in the tab order with `aria-disabled` instead of the native attribute, so it can hold focus while it becomes disabled and host a tooltip that says why. Presses still do nothing. @defaultValue false |
| `pendingAnnouncement` | `string` |  | What screen readers hear once the button has been pending for a second, so a slow action doesn't pass in silence. Set it in the page's language. An empty string says nothing. @defaultValue "Loading" |
| `debug` | `boolean` |  | Logs every state change with its reason to the console, in development builds. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `subtle` |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` |  |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content before the label, usually an icon. |
| `rightSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content after the label. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and blocks presses. A Promise returned from `onClick` does this on its own. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Stretch to the container's width. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Button also accepts the props of ui-sdk's Button, such as `type`, `onClick` and `focusableWhenDisabled`. `type` defaults to `'button'`, so set `type="submit"` to submit a form.

### IconButton

See the props of `IconButton` on the docs page or in its TypeScript types.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button` | The button, for both Button and IconButton |
| `.kit-icon-button` | Added on IconButton |
| `.kit-button--full` | Added with `fullWidth` |
| `.kit-button__section` | The left or right section, and the loading spinner |
| `.kit-button__label` | The text |
| `[data-variant]`, `[data-size]` | The current variant and size |
| `[data-loading]` | Present while `loading` is set |
| `[data-pending]` | Present while an async `onClick` runs (from ui-sdk) |
| `[data-disabled]` | Present while disabled (from ui-sdk) |

Colours come from the theme tokens: `primary` and `primaryForeground` for `filled`, `primarySoft` for `light`, `destructive` for `danger`. See **Tokens** for the full list. To restyle one button, pass `className`. The kit's rules sit in `@layer ui-kit`, so your unlayered CSS wins without `!important`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Button](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/button), which renders a native `<button>`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | Presses the focused button |

- Give every button a text label that says what it does: "Save package", not "OK".
- `IconButton` must have an `aria-label`. Add a `Tooltip` with the same text for sighted mouse users.
- While pending, the button sets `aria-busy="true"` and `aria-disabled="true"` and keeps focus.
- Use `focusableWhenDisabled` when a disabled button should still be reachable, for example to show a tooltip explaining why it's disabled.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep one `filled` button per view, for the main action.
- Start labels with a verb: "Add package", "Export report".
- Put Cancel (`default`) before the primary action in dialog footers.

**Don't**

- Don't use a button to go to another page. Use a link.
- Don't change the label to "Saving…" while pending. The spinner and the screen reader announcement already say it's working, and a changing label shifts the button's width.
- Don't use `danger` for actions that can be undone.

## Related

- **Dialog** and **ConfirmDialog**: footers built from buttons.
- **Tooltip**: names an `IconButton` for mouse users.
- **ActionMenu**: when a row has more actions than fit as buttons.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs

---

# Checkbox

Import: `import { Checkbox } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A checkbox with its label beside it, for yes/no choices and for picking several items from a list.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Unchecked" />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Checked" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Indeterminate" indeterminate />
    <Checkbox
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Contractors see it in their portal." />
    <Checkbox
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="I accept the terms"
        required
        error="Accept the terms to continue" />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Disabled" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>;
```

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A choice that takes effect when the form is submitted | `Checkbox` |
| A setting that takes effect immediately | `Switch` |
| One of a few options | `RadioGroup` or `SegmentedControl` |
| Several of many options | `MultiSelect`, or several checkboxes |
| A filter toggle in a toolbar | `Chip` |

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Checkbox label="Publish to ATM" onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### States

`onChange` receives `true` or `false`. Use `checked` to control it, or `defaultChecked` to leave the state to the checkbox. Checkbox takes the field props (`description`, `error`, `required`, `disabled`…) like the other inputs.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Unchecked" />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Checked" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Indeterminate" indeterminate />
    <Checkbox
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Contractors see it in their portal." />
    <Checkbox
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="I accept the terms"
        required
        error="Accept the terms to continue" />
    <Checkbox onChange={() => {}} label="Disabled" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>;
```

### Select all

`indeterminate` shows a dash: some of the items it stands for are checked. Clicking it calls `onChange(true)`.

```tsx
const SelectAll = args => {
    const [checked, setChecked] = useState<string[]>(['Drainage'])
    const all = checked.length === items.length

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
            <Checkbox
                label="All work types"
                checked={all}
                indeterminate={checked.length > 0 && !all}
                onChange={(next) => setChecked(next ? items : [])} />
            <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, paddingInlineStart: 28 }}>
                {items.map((item) => (
                  <Checkbox
                    key={item}
                    {...args}
                    label={item}
                    checked={checked.includes(item)}
                    onChange={(next) =>
                      setChecked((c) =>
                        next ? [...c, item] : c.filter((x) => x !== item),
                      )
                    }
                  />
                ))}
            </div>
        </div>
    );
};
```

### Sizes

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Checkbox key={size} {...args} size={size} label={`Size ${size}`} />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFCheckbox } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFCheckbox name="acceptTerms" label="I accept the terms" rules={{ required: 'Accept the terms to continue' }} />
```

The form value is a `boolean`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new checked state. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | `'on'` | What the control submits while checked. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` |  | Show a dash: part of a group is checked. |

In a native form, a checked checkbox submits `value` (`'on'` by default) under `name`.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-field.kit-field--inline` | The wrapper, with the label beside the box |
| `.kit-checkbox` | The box |
| `.kit-checkbox__indicator` | The check mark |
| `.kit-checkbox__dash` | The indeterminate dash |
| `[data-checked]`, `[data-indeterminate]` | State on the box (from ui-sdk) |

A checked box uses the `primary` and `primaryForeground` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Checkbox](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/checkbox), which follows the WAI-ARIA checkbox pattern. The label is linked to the box, so clicking the label toggles it. An indeterminate checkbox reports `aria-checked="mixed"`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space | Toggles the focused checkbox |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Phrase the label positively, so checked means yes: "Send me updates", not "Don't send me updates".
- Stack several checkboxes vertically, one per line.

**Don't**

- Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies the moment it's clicked. Use `Switch`.

## Related

- **Switch**, **RadioGroup**, **Chip**: other choice controls.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-checkbox--docs

---

# Chip

Import: `import { Chip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A pill that toggles on and off, for filters and tags. A checked chip shows a check mark.

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Filters = (args) => {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string[]>(['Overdue'])
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
      <fieldset
        aria-label="Filters"
        style={{
          display: 'flex',
          gap: 8,
          flexWrap: 'wrap',
          border: 0,
          margin: 0,
          padding: 0,
        }}
      >
        {filters.map((f) => (
          <Chip
            key={f}
            {...args}
            checked={active.includes(f)}
            onChange={(on) =>
              setActive((a) => (on ? [...a, f] : a.filter((x) => x !== f)))
            }
          >
            {f}
          </Chip>
        ))}
      </fieldset>
      <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Active: {active.join(', ') || 'none'}</p>
    </div>
  )
};
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Chip onChange={() => {}}>Overdue</Chip>;
```

## Examples

### Filters

Chips have no group of their own: keep the checked values in state and render one chip per option. Wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with an `aria-label` (or a `<legend>`) so screen readers know they belong together.

```tsx
const Filters = (args) => {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string[]>(['Overdue'])
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
      <fieldset
        aria-label="Filters"
        style={{
          display: 'flex',
          gap: 8,
          flexWrap: 'wrap',
          border: 0,
          margin: 0,
          padding: 0,
        }}
      >
        {filters.map((f) => (
          <Chip
            key={f}
            {...args}
            checked={active.includes(f)}
            onChange={(on) =>
              setActive((a) => (on ? [...a, f] : a.filter((x) => x !== f)))
            }
          >
            {f}
          </Chip>
        ))}
      </fieldset>
      <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Active: {active.join(', ') || 'none'}</p>
    </div>
  )
};
```

### States

`withoutIcon` hides the check mark.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
    <Chip onChange={() => {}}>Unchecked</Chip>
    <Chip onChange={() => {}} defaultChecked>Checked
              </Chip>
    <Chip onChange={() => {}} defaultChecked withoutIcon>No check mark
              </Chip>
    <Chip onChange={() => {}} disabled>Disabled
              </Chip>
</div>;
```

### Sizes

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Chip key={size} {...args} size={size} defaultChecked>
        Size {size}
      </Chip>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Use with react-hook-form

`RHFChip` binds one chip to a boolean field:

```tsx
import { RHFChip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFChip name="urgent">Urgent</RHFChip>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `withoutIcon` | `boolean` |  | Hide the check mark shown while checked. |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-chip` | The pill |
| `.kit-chip__icon` | The check mark |
| `[data-pressed]` | Present while checked (from ui-sdk) |

A checked chip uses the `primarySoft` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Toggle](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/toggle). Each chip is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space, Enter | Toggles the focused chip |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep chip labels to one or two words.
- Show the result of the filter straight away.

**Don't**

- Don't use chips for actions. Use `Button`.
- Don't use chips inside forms in place of checkboxes.

## Related

- **Checkbox**: for choices inside a form.
- **Badge**: a label that can't be toggled.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-chip--docs

---

# ColorInput and ColorPicker

Import: `import { ColorInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

`ColorInput` is a text field for a colour, with a swatch that opens a picker. `ColorPicker` is the same picker shown inline: a saturation area, a hue slider and optional swatches.

```tsx
import { ColorInput, ColorPicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <ColorInput
    label="Route colour"
    defaultValue="#1971c2"
    swatches={[
      '#e03131',
      '#f08c00',
      '#2f9e44',
      '#1971c2',
      '#7048e8',
      '#f2c45a',
    ]}
    onChange={() => {}}
    onChangeEnd={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Formats

The value is a CSS colour string in `format`: `hex` (default), `srgb` (`rgb()`), `hsl` or `oklch`. Typed colours in any CSS syntax are converted to it.

```tsx
const Formats = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    {(['hex', 'srgb', 'hsl', 'oklch'] as const).map((format) => (
      <ColorInput
        key={format}
        {...args}
        format={format}
        label={`format="${format}"`}
      />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### Transparency

`withAlpha` adds an alpha slider. Use a format that can hold alpha, like `srgb` or `oklch`.

```tsx
const WithAlpha = () => <ColorInput
    label="Overlay colour"
    defaultValue="#1971c2"
    swatches={[
      '#e03131',
      '#f08c00',
      '#2f9e44',
      '#1971c2',
      '#7048e8',
      '#f2c45a',
    ]}
    onChange={() => {}}
    onChangeEnd={() => {}}
    withAlpha
    format="srgb" />;
```

### Controlled

`onChange` runs as the colour changes, including while dragging. `onChangeEnd` runs once the drag is released or the edit is committed. Save in `onChangeEnd`.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [colour, setColour] = useState('#2f9e44')

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
            <ColorInput
                label="Route colour"
                defaultValue="#1971c2"
                swatches={[
                  '#e03131',
                  '#f08c00',
                  '#2f9e44',
                  '#1971c2',
                  '#7048e8',
                  '#f2c45a',
                ]}
                onChangeEnd={() => {}}
                value={colour}
                onChange={setColour} />
            <div
                style={{
                  height: 40,
                  borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
                  background: colour,
                }} />
        </div>
    );
};
```

### Inline picker

```tsx
const InlinePicker = () => (
  <ColorPicker
    aria-label="Route colour"
    defaultValue="#7048e8"
    swatches={swatches}
  />
);
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFColorInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFColorInput name="routeColour" label="Route colour" swatches={brandColours} />
```

## Props

### ColorInput

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | A CSS colour, written in `format`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called as the colour changes, including mid-drag. |
| `onChangeEnd` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called once a change ends: a drag released or an edit committed. |
| `format` | `enum` | `'hex'` |  |
| `swatches` | `string[]` |  | Preset colours to pick from. |
| `withAlpha` | `boolean` |  | Show an alpha slider. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |

### ColorPicker

See the props of `ColorPicker` on the docs page or in its TypeScript types.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-color` | The picker |
| `.kit-color--popover` | The picker inside ColorInput's popup |
| `.kit-color__area` | The saturation and brightness area |
| `.kit-color__slider` | The hue or alpha slider |
| `.kit-color__thumb` | A draggable handle |
| `.kit-color__swatches`, `.kit-color__swatch` | The preset colours |
| `.kit-color__preview` | The swatch in ColorInput's field |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Color Picker](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/color-picker). The area and sliders are sliders for assistive technology, and each swatch is a button named by its colour. Give a `ColorPicker` without a label an `aria-label`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | On the area or a slider, move the handle |
| Enter | In the text field, commits the typed colour |
| Escape | Closes ColorInput's popup |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Offer `swatches` for your brand or status colours, so people pick consistent colours.
- Check that text on the chosen colour is still readable.

**Don't**

- Don't use colour as the only way to tell things apart. Add a label or icon.

## Related

- **Tokens**: the theme's colours.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-colorinput--docs
