# FileInput

Import: `import { FileInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Picks or drops files, checks them against your limits, and lists what's chosen. It comes as a compact field with a Browse button, or a large dropzone.

```tsx
import { FileInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Cards = () => {
  const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([
    sampleFile('contract-signed.pdf', 482_000, 'application/pdf'),
    sampleFile('site-plan.xlsx', 96_000, 'application/vnd.ms-excel'),
  ])
  return (
    <FileInput
      label="Attachments"
      variant="dropzone"
      preview="cards"
      multiple
      value={files}
      onChange={setFiles}
      maxSize={100 * 1024 ** 2}
      placeholder="Drop your documents here"
      hint="Maximum upload file: 100 MB"
    />
  )
};
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <FileInput label="Contract (PDF)" accept=".pdf" onReject={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### One file or many

Without `multiple`, the value is a `File` or `null`. With `multiple`, it's a `File[]`. A file with the same name and size as one already chosen is never added twice.

```tsx
<FileInput label="Contract" accept=".pdf" onChange={(file) => setContract(file)} />
<FileInput label="Photos" multiple onChange={(files) => setPhotos(files)} />
```

### Dropzone

`variant="dropzone"` shows a large area to drop files on. `placeholder` is its main text and `hint` the smaller text under it.

```tsx
const Dropzone = () => <FileInput
    label="Site photos"
    accept="image/*"
    onReject={() => {}}
    variant="dropzone"
    multiple
    maxSize={5_000_000}
    description="JPG or PNG, up to 5 MB each" />;
```

### Cards

`preview="cards"` shows each file as a card with a thumbnail (or a document icon), name and size. Inside a dropzone the cards fill the area, which still takes drops. To show files that are already saved, create `File` objects and pass them as `value`.

```tsx
const Cards = () => {
  const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([
    sampleFile('contract-signed.pdf', 482_000, 'application/pdf'),
    sampleFile('site-plan.xlsx', 96_000, 'application/vnd.ms-excel'),
  ])
  return (
    <FileInput
      label="Attachments"
      variant="dropzone"
      preview="cards"
      multiple
      value={files}
      onChange={setFiles}
      maxSize={100 * 1024 ** 2}
      placeholder="Drop your documents here"
      hint="Maximum upload file: 100 MB"
    />
  )
};
```

### Limits and rejections

`accept`, `maxSize` (bytes) and `maxFiles` limit what's accepted. Files that fail are listed under the field and passed to `onReject` with every reason: `file-type`, `file-too-large`, `too-many-files` or `duplicate`. Set `showRejections={false}` to hide the message, or pass a function to word it yourself.

```tsx
const Limits = () => <FileInput
    label="Up to 2 images, 1 MB each"
    accept="image/*"
    onReject={() => {}}
    variant="dropzone"
    multiple
    maxSize={1_000_000}
    maxFiles={2} />;
```

### States

```tsx
const States = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <FileInput accept=".pdf" label="Required" required />
    <FileInput accept=".pdf" label="With error" error="Attach the contract" />
    <FileInput accept=".pdf" label="Disabled" disabled />
  </div>
);
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFFileInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFFileInput name="attachments" label="Attachments" multiple maxSize={10 * 1024 ** 2} />
```

The form value is a `File`, a `File[]` or `null`. Upload the files in your submit handler, for example with `FormData`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `accept` | `string \| readonly string[]` |  | Accepted types, like `"image/*"` or `[".pdf", "image/png"]`. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  | Largest file, in bytes. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` |  | Most files, with `multiple`. |
| `onReject` | `((rejected: FileRejectionInfo[]) => void)` |  | Called with files that failed `accept`, `maxSize`, `maxFiles` or the duplicate check. |
| `showRejections` | `boolean \| ((rejected: FileRejectionInfo[]) => ReactNode)` | `true` | Show a message under the field when files are rejected. Pass a function to word it yourself. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `'button'` | `button`: a compact field with a Browse button. `dropzone`: a large area to drop files on. |
| `preview` | `enum` | `'list'` | How chosen files show. `list`: name and size rows. `cards`: cards with an image thumbnail (or a document icon), name and size. With `cards` in a dropzone, the cards fill the dropzone, which still takes drops. |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` |  | Main text inside the dropzone, or beside the button. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | Smaller text under the dropzone's placeholder, like a size limit. |
| `buttonLabel` | `ReactNode` | `'Browse'` | Label of the browse button. |
| `onFileRemove` | `((file: File, index: number) => void)` |  | Called after the user removes a file. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `value` | `File \| File[] \| null` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `File \| File[] \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((files: File[]) => void) \| ((file: File \| null) => void)` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-file` | The wrapper |
| `.kit-file__trigger` | The Browse button field (`variant="button"`) |
| `.kit-file__dropzone` | The drop area (`variant="dropzone"`) |
| `.kit-file__placeholder`, `.kit-file__hint` | The dropzone's texts |
| `.kit-file__list` | The chosen files (`.kit-file__list--cards` for cards) |
| `.kit-file__item`, `.kit-file__card` | One file as a row or a card |
| `.kit-file__thumb` | A card's thumbnail (`--doc` for the document icon) |
| `.kit-file__name`, `.kit-file__size` | The file's name and size |
| `.kit-file__remove`, `.kit-file__card-remove` | The remove button |

The dropzone uses the `surface` token.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk File Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/file-input). Files can always be chosen with the keyboard through the system file dialog, so nobody has to drag. The chosen files are a list named "Chosen files". Each remove button is named after its file.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Say what's accepted and how big in `description` or `hint`: "PDF, up to 10 MB".
- Use `preview="cards"` for photos, so people can check they picked the right ones.

**Don't**

- Don't upload on drop without showing progress. Upload on submit, or show a loader per file.

## Related

- **ImagePreviewer**: shows an uploaded image full screen.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-fileinput--docs

---

# NumberInput

Import: `import { NumberInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A field for numbers. It parses what's typed, keeps the value between `min` and `max`, and formats it for display (`1,250,000.00`), while your value stays a plain `number`.

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Currency = () => <NumberInput
    label="Contract value"
    min={0}
    max={undefined}
    defaultValue={1250000}
    withControls={false}
    onChange={() => {}}
    onValueCommit={() => {}}
    prefix="RM"
    decimalScale={2}
    fixedDecimalScale />;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <NumberInput
    label="Lanes"
    min={1}
    max={8}
    defaultValue={2}
    withControls
    onChange={() => {}}
    onValueCommit={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Money

`prefix` and `suffix` show text beside the number. `decimalScale` sets the digits after the point, and `fixedDecimalScale` always shows them. Thousands are grouped unless you set `thousandSeparator={false}`.

```tsx
const Currency = () => <NumberInput
    label="Contract value"
    min={0}
    max={undefined}
    defaultValue={1250000}
    withControls={false}
    onChange={() => {}}
    onValueCommit={() => {}}
    prefix="RM"
    decimalScale={2}
    fixedDecimalScale />;
```

### Percentages and steps

`step` is how far the arrow keys and step buttons move the value. `withControls` shows the step buttons.

```tsx
const Percent = () => <NumberInput
    label="Progress"
    min={0}
    max={100}
    defaultValue={40}
    withControls
    onChange={() => {}}
    onValueCommit={() => {}}
    suffix="%"
    step={5} />;
```

### Other units

For anything the shorthands don't cover, pass `Intl.NumberFormat` options to `format`. They override `decimalScale`, `fixedDecimalScale` and `thousandSeparator`. `locale` defaults to the page's language.

```tsx
const Units = () => <NumberInput
    label="Road length"
    min={0}
    max={undefined}
    defaultValue={12.4}
    withControls={false}
    onChange={() => {}}
    onValueCommit={() => {}}
    format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
    step={0.1} />;
```

### Controlled

`onChange` receives a `number`, or `null` when the field is empty, as the user types or steps. `onValueCommit` runs once an edit is finished: on Enter, blur or a step. Use it to save, so you don't save on every key press.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<number | null>(3)

    return (
        <>
            <NumberInput
                label="Lanes"
                min={1}
                max={8}
                withControls
                onValueCommit={() => {}}
                defaultValue={undefined}
                value={value}
                onChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {value === null ? 'null' : value}({typeof value})
                        </p>
        </>
    );
};
```

The form submits the plain number (`1250000`), not the formatted text.

### States

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <NumberInput
        min={1}
        max={8}
        withControls
        onChange={() => {}}
        onValueCommit={() => {}}
        label="Required"
        required
        defaultValue={null} />
    <NumberInput
        min={1}
        max={8}
        defaultValue={2}
        withControls
        onChange={() => {}}
        onValueCommit={() => {}}
        label="With error"
        error="At most 8 lanes" />
    <NumberInput
        min={1}
        max={8}
        defaultValue={2}
        withControls
        onChange={() => {}}
        onValueCommit={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFNumberInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFNumberInput name="contractValue" label="Contract value" prefix="RM" decimalScale={2} rules={{ required: true, min: 0 }} />
```

The form value is a `number` or `null`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | The number, or `null` when empty. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: number \| null) => void)` |  | Called with the number as the user types or steps, `null` when empty. |
| `onValueCommit` | `((value: number \| null) => void)` |  | Called once an edit is committed: on Enter, blur or a step. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  |
| `min` | `number` |  |  |
| `max` | `number` |  |  |
| `step` | `number` | `1` |  |
| `decimalScale` | `number` |  | Digits after the decimal point. Shorthand for `format.maximumFractionDigits`. |
| `fixedDecimalScale` | `boolean` |  | Always show `decimalScale` digits, like `1.50`. |
| `thousandSeparator` | `boolean` | `true` | Group thousands, like `12,500`. |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | Text before the number, like `RM `. Shown beside the field. |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` |  | Text after the number, like `%`. |
| `format` | `NumberFormatOptions` |  | Full `Intl.NumberFormat` options; overrides the shorthands above. |
| `locale` | `string` | `the page's language` |  |
| `withControls` | `boolean` | `false` | Show step buttons. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

Uses the **TextInput** classes, plus:

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input__affix` | The prefix or suffix |
| `.kit-number__steppers` | The step buttons' column |
| `.kit-number__step` | One step button |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Number Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/number-input), which follows the keyboard model of the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern on a native text input, so normal text editing still works.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Steps by `step` |
| Shift + arrow, Page Up, Page Down | Steps by ten steps |
| Alt (Option) + arrow | Steps by a tenth of a step |
| Home, End | Goes to `min` or `max`, when set |
| Enter | Commits the typed text |

The step buttons stay out of the Tab order, because the arrow keys do the same thing.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for values people calculate with: money, quantities, lengths, percentages.
- Set `min` and `max` when the value has real limits.
- Show the unit with `prefix`, `suffix` or `format`, not only in the label.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for numbers that are really codes: phone numbers, IC numbers, postcodes. Use `TextInput` with `inputMode="numeric"`.
- Don't add `withControls` for large values like money. Nobody steps to RM 1,250,000.

## Related

- **TextInput**: for numeric codes.
- **DataTable**: `NumberCellEditor` edits numbers inside a table.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs

---

# PasswordInput

Import: `import { PasswordInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A password field with a button that shows or hides what's typed.

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <PasswordInput label="Password" />;
```

## Examples

### New password

Set `autoComplete="new-password"` on sign-up and change-password forms, so password managers offer to generate one. The default, `current-password`, is right for sign-in forms.

```tsx
const NewPassword = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState('')

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
            <PasswordInput
                label="Create a password"
                autoComplete="new-password"
                required
                value={value}
                onValueChange={setValue} />
            <ul
                aria-label="Password requirements"
                style={{ margin: 0, paddingInlineStart: 20, fontSize: 13 }}>
                {rules.map((rule) => (
                  <li key={rule.label}>
                    {rule.test(value) ? '✓ ' : '✗ '}
                    {rule.label}
                  </li>
                ))}
            </ul>
        </div>
    );
};
```

### States

PasswordInput takes the same field props as **TextInput**.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <PasswordInput label="With error" error="Wrong password" />
    <PasswordInput label="Disabled" disabled defaultValue="secret123" />
    <PasswordInput label="With icon" leftSection={<icons.CheckIcon />} />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFPasswordInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFPasswordInput name="password" label="Password" rules={{ required: true, minLength: 8 }} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` |  | The password, to control the field. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting password, when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new text after any change: typing, clearing or a form reset. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement, Element>` |  | The native change event of the inner `<input>`. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` |  | Called when the input loses focus. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown while the field is empty. |
| `autoComplete` | `(string & {}) \| "current-password" \| "new-password" \| "off"` | `'current-password'` | `current-password` for sign-in forms, `new-password` for sign-up and change-password forms, so password managers fill or generate correctly. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the field, before the text, like an icon. |

## Styling

Uses the **TextInput** classes. The show/hide button is `.kit-input__toggle`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Password Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/password-input). The field stays a native password input. The toggle is a toggle button with `aria-pressed` and keeps the same name whether the password is shown or hidden.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves from the input to the toggle |
| Space, Enter | On the toggle, shows or hides the password |
| Enter | In the input, submits the form (it never presses the toggle) |

Clicking the toggle with the mouse keeps the caret in the input.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- List the password rules up front, and show which are met as the user types.
- Let the browser autofill: always set `autoComplete`.

**Don't**

- Don't block pasting. It breaks password managers.
- Don't ask for the password twice. The show/hide toggle lets people check it.

## Related

- **TextInput**: shares the field props and styling.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-passwordinput--docs

---

# RadioGroup

Import: `import { RadioGroup } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Picks one of a few options, all visible at once. Pass the options as `data` and the group renders the radios.

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Horizontal = () => <RadioGroup
    label="Severity"
    data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
    defaultValue="Medium"
    onChange={() => {}}
    orientation="horizontal" />;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <RadioGroup
    label="Severity"
    data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
    defaultValue="Medium"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Layout

Radios stack vertically by default. `orientation="horizontal"` puts them in a row, for two to four short options.

```tsx
const Horizontal = () => <RadioGroup
    label="Severity"
    data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
    defaultValue="Medium"
    onChange={() => {}}
    orientation="horizontal" />;
```

### Options

`data` takes the same shapes as **Select**: strings, or `{ value, label, disabled }` objects.

```tsx
const OptionObjects = () => <RadioGroup
    label="Payment"
    data={[
      { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly claim' },
      { value: 'milestone', label: 'By milestone' },
      { value: 'lump', label: 'Lump sum', disabled: true },
    ]}
    defaultValue="monthly"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

### Controlled

`onChange` receives the chosen value.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>('High')

    return (
        <>
            <RadioGroup
                label="Severity"
                data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
                defaultValue="Medium"
                value={value}
                onChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {String(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

### States

The group takes the field props. `label` names the whole group, and `error` and `required` apply to it.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 24 }}>
    <RadioGroup
        data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With error"
        defaultValue={null}
        required
        error="Pick a severity" />
    <RadioGroup
        data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']}
        defaultValue="Medium"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFRadioGroup } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFRadioGroup name="severity" label="Severity" data={['Low', 'Medium', 'High']} rules={{ required: true }} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `data` (required) | `SelectData` |  | The choices. |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| null) => void)` |  |  |
| `orientation` | `enum` | `'vertical'` | Lay the radios out in a row. |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-radio-group` | The group |
| `.kit-radio-group__option` | One radio with its label |
| `.kit-radio` | The circle |
| `.kit-radio__indicator` | The dot |
| `[data-checked]` | On the chosen radio (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Radio](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/radio), which follows the WAI-ARIA radio group pattern. The group has the `radiogroup` role and is named by `label`. The whole group is one Tab stop.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves into the group, onto the chosen radio (or the first) |
| Arrow keys | Move to the next or previous radio and choose it |
| Space | Chooses the focused radio |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for two to five options that people should compare.
- Pick a sensible default when there is one.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for more than about five options. Use `Select`.
- Don't use a single radio. Use `Checkbox`.

## Related

- **SegmentedControl**: a more compact way to pick one of a few options.
- **Select**: for longer lists.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-radiogroup--docs

# SearchInput

Import: `import { SearchInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A text field for searching. It has a search icon and a clear button, and calls `onSearch` once the user stops typing, so you don't send a request on every key press.

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <SearchInput placeholder="Search packages" onSearch={() => {}} debounceMs={300} />;
```

## Examples

### Debounced search

`onSearch` runs `debounceMs` milliseconds (300 by default) after the last change, including a clear. Use it to filter a list or fetch results. `onValueChange` still runs on every change if you need the raw text.

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['packages', query], queryFn: () => api.search(query) })

<SearchInput placeholder="Search packages" onSearch={setQuery} />
```

### With a label

Without a `label`, the input is named "Search" for screen readers. Add a label when the search sits in a form or there's more than one on the page.

```tsx
const WithLabel = () => <SearchInput
    placeholder="Name or registration no."
    onSearch={() => {}}
    debounceMs={300}
    label="Find a contractor" />;
```

## Props

Takes every `TextInput` prop except `type`, plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears the text. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the input, before the text, like an icon. |
| `onSearch` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the text after the user pauses typing. |
| `debounceMs` | `number` | `300` | Pause before `onSearch`, in ms. |

`clearable` defaults to `true` and `leftSection` to the search icon. Pass your own to replace them.

## Styling

Uses the same classes as **TextInput**. The `<input>` has `type="search"`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/input). The input has `type="search"`, so screen readers announce it as a search field, and it gets the accessible name "Search" unless you give it a `label` or `aria-label`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Say what's being searched in the placeholder: "Search packages".
- Keep the debounce at 300ms or more for server requests.

**Don't**

- Don't add a separate Search button that does the same thing as typing.

## Related

- **TextInput**: the field it's built on.
- **Autocomplete**: when the user should pick from suggestions.
- **DataTable**: has its own quick-filter search in the toolbar.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-searchinput--docs

---

# SegmentedControl

Import: `import { SegmentedControl } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A row of options where exactly one is chosen, with an indicator that slides to the choice. Good for switching views or periods.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const SwitchViews = () => {
    const [view, setView] = useState('List')

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12, maxWidth: 420 }}>
            <SegmentedControl
                aria-label="View"
                data={['List', 'Map', 'Calendar']}
                defaultValue="List"
                value={view}
                onChange={setView} />
            <div
                style={{
                  padding: 16,
                  border: '1px dashed var(--ui-border)',
                  borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
                }}>
                {view}view of work orders
                        </div>
        </div>
    );
};
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <SegmentedControl
    aria-label="View"
    data={['List', 'Map', 'Calendar']}
    defaultValue="List"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Switch views

`onChange` receives the new value. There's always a value: the user can't unselect.

```tsx
const SwitchViews = () => {
    const [view, setView] = useState('List')

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12, maxWidth: 420 }}>
            <SegmentedControl
                aria-label="View"
                data={['List', 'Map', 'Calendar']}
                defaultValue="List"
                value={view}
                onChange={setView} />
            <div
                style={{
                  padding: 16,
                  border: '1px dashed var(--ui-border)',
                  borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
                }}>
                {view}view of work orders
                        </div>
        </div>
    );
};
```

### With a label

Inside a form, give it a `label` like any other field. On its own, give it an `aria-label`.

```tsx
const WithLabel = () => <SegmentedControl
    aria-label={undefined}
    data={['Day', 'Week', 'Month', 'Year']}
    defaultValue="Month"
    onChange={() => {}}
    label="Period" />;
```

### Full width and disabled options

```tsx
const FullWidth = () => <SegmentedControl
    aria-label="View"
    data={['List', 'Map', 'Calendar']}
    defaultValue="List"
    onChange={() => {}}
    fullWidth />;
```
```tsx
const DisabledOption = () => <SegmentedControl
    aria-label="View"
    data={[
      { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
      { value: 'map', label: 'Map' },
      { value: 'gantt', label: 'Gantt', disabled: true },
    ]}
    defaultValue="list"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFSegmentedControl } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFSegmentedControl name="period" label="Period" data={['Day', 'Week', 'Month']} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `data` (required) | `SelectData` |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  |  |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Stretch to the container's width. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-segmented` | The track |
| `.kit-segmented--full` | Added with `fullWidth` |
| `.kit-segmented__item` | One option |
| `.kit-segmented__indicator` | The sliding highlight |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Segmented Control](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/segmented-control). It works like a radio group: one Tab stop for the whole row, and the arrow keys move the choice.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves onto the chosen option |
| Arrow keys | Choose the next or previous option |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for two to five short options.
- Use it to change what's shown on the page, not to submit data.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for navigation between pages. Use `Tabs`.
- Don't put long labels in it. It doesn't wrap.

## Related

- **RadioGroup**: the same choice, laid out as a list.
- **Tabs**: for switching between panels of content.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-segmentedcontrol--docs
