# Switch

Import: `import { Switch } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

An on/off switch for settings that take effect straight away, like turning notifications on.

```tsx
import { Switch } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="Off" />
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="On" defaultChecked />
    <Switch
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Get an email when a work order changes." />
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="Disabled" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Switch label="Email notifications" onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### States

`onChange` receives `true` or `false`. Use `checked` or `defaultChecked`, as with Checkbox.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="Off" />
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="On" defaultChecked />
    <Switch
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Get an email when a work order changes." />
    <Switch onChange={() => {}} label="Disabled" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>;
```

### Label on top

By default the label sits beside the switch. `labelPosition="top"` puts it above, like a text field's label, so a switch lines up with the other fields in a form grid.

```tsx
const LabelOnTop = () => <Switch label="DLP status" onChange={() => {}} labelPosition="top" defaultChecked />;
```

### Sizes

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Switch key={size} {...args} size={size} label={`Size ${size}`} />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFSwitch } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFSwitch name="active" label="Active" />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new checked state. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | `'on'` | What the control submits while checked. |
| `labelPosition` | `enum` | `end` | Where the label sits: beside the switch, or above it like other fields. |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-switch` | The track |
| `.kit-switch__thumb` | The moving knob |
| `[data-checked]` | Present while on (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Switch](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/switch), which follows the WAI-ARIA switch pattern: the control has the `switch` role and reports `aria-checked`. The label names it, and clicking the label toggles it.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space, Enter | Toggles the switch |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use a switch when the change applies immediately, without a Save button.
- Label the setting, not the state: "Email notifications", not "On".

**Don't**

- Don't use a switch inside a form that needs submitting. Use `Checkbox`.

## Related

- **Checkbox**: for choices that apply on submit.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-switch--docs

---

# TextInput

Import: `import { TextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A single-line text field with a label, description and error. Every kit form control shares the same field props, so what you learn here applies to the others.

```tsx
import { TextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Sections = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Website"
        placeholder="example.com"
        leftSection={<span>https://</span>} />
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Search"
        placeholder="Search packages"
        leftSection={<icons.SearchIcon />}
        clearable
        defaultValue="Road upgrade" />
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Length"
        placeholder="0"
        rightSection={<span>km</span>} />
</div>;
```

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One line of text | `TextInput` |
| A search box with a debounced callback | `SearchInput` |
| A password | `PasswordInput` |
| A number, money or a percentage | `NumberInput` |
| Several lines | `Textarea` |

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <TextInput label="Package name" placeholder="PKG-001" onValueChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Field states

These props are the same on every kit input, select and picker:

- `label`, and `description` for helper text under the control.
- `error`: a message, or `true` to mark the field invalid without one.
- `required` makes the field natively required and adds an asterisk. `withAsterisk` adds only the asterisk.
- `disabled` and `readOnly`. A read-only field stays focusable and is submitted with the form. A disabled one is neither.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <TextInput
        placeholder="PKG-001"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="As written on the contract." />
    <TextInput placeholder="PKG-001" onValueChange={() => {}} label="Required" required />
    <TextInput
        placeholder="PKG-001"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="With error"
        error="Enter a package name" />
    <TextInput
        placeholder="PKG-001"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled
        defaultValue="PKG-014" />
    <TextInput
        placeholder="PKG-001"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Read-only"
        readOnly
        defaultValue="PKG-014" />
</div>;
```

### Sizes

`size` sets the height from the `--kit-h-*` tokens, the same scale as buttons.

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <TextInput key={size} {...args} size={size} label={`Size ${size}`} />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### Sections and clear button

`leftSection` and `rightSection` sit inside the field, before and after the text: an icon, a prefix like `https://` or a unit. `clearable` adds a button that empties the field and shows only while there's text.

```tsx
const Sections = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Website"
        placeholder="example.com"
        leftSection={<span>https://</span>} />
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Search"
        placeholder="Search packages"
        leftSection={<icons.SearchIcon />}
        clearable
        defaultValue="Road upgrade" />
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Length"
        placeholder="0"
        rightSection={<span>km</span>} />
</div>;
```

### Controlled

`onValueChange` receives the new text after any change: typing, clearing or a form reset. `onChange` is the native change event, as on a plain `<input>`. Use `defaultValue` instead of `value` to leave the state to the input.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState('Road upgrade section 4')

    return (
        <>
            <TextInput
                label="Package name"
                placeholder="PKG-001"
                clearable
                value={value}
                onValueChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {JSON.stringify(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

### Input types

`type` and any other native input attribute (`autoComplete`, `inputMode`, `pattern`, `maxLength`…) pass through to the `<input>`.

```tsx
const Types = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Email"
        type="email"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        autoComplete="email" />
    <TextInput
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Phone"
        type="tel"
        placeholder="012-345 6789"
        autoComplete="tel" />
    <TextInput onValueChange={() => {}} label="URL" type="url" placeholder="https://" />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFTextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFTextInput name="packageName" label="Package name" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

`RHFTextInput` takes the same props plus `name` and `rules`, and shows the field's error message for you. See **Forms with react-hook-form**.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement, Element>` |  | The native change event, as with a plain `<input>`. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | The new text, after any change: typing, clearing or a form reset. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the input, before the text, like an icon. |
| `rightSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the input, after the text. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears the text. |

The ref goes to the `<input>`.

## Styling

These classes are shared by every text-like field (TextInput, SearchInput, PasswordInput, NumberInput, Select…).

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-field` | `root` | The wrapper around label, control and messages |
| `.kit-field__label` | `label` | The label |
| `.kit-field__asterisk` | — | The required asterisk |
| `.kit-field__description` | `description` | The helper text |
| `.kit-field__error` | `error` | The error message |
| `.kit-input` | `control` | The box with the border |
| `.kit-input__control` | — | The `<input>` itself |
| `.kit-input__section` | — | The left or right section |
| `.kit-input__clear` | — | The clear button |
| `[data-size]`, `[data-kind]` | — | On `.kit-field`: the size, and which control it holds |
| `[data-invalid]`, `[data-disabled]` | — | Invalid and disabled state (from ui-sdk) |

Borders use the `input` token, the focus ring uses `ring` and `ringBorder`, and errors use `destructive`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/input) and [Field](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/field). The label names the input, the description and error describe it, and an invalid field gets `aria-invalid`. Clicking the label focuses the input. The input is a native `<input>`, so text editing, selection and autofill work as usual.

- Without a visible `label`, give the input an `aria-label`.
- The clear button is named "Clear".

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Always use a `label`. A placeholder isn't a label: it disappears as soon as someone types.
- Put format hints in `description`: "As written on the contract".
- Set `type` and `autoComplete` so phones show the right keyboard and browsers can autofill.

**Don't**

- Don't use `TextInput` for numbers people do maths with. Use `NumberInput`.
- Don't show an error before the user has had a chance to fill the field.

## Related

- **SearchInput**, **PasswordInput**, **NumberInput**, **Textarea**: specialised text fields.
- **Autocomplete**: free text with suggestions.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs

---

# Textarea

Import: `import { Textarea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A multi-line text field for remarks, descriptions and notes. It can grow with its text and show a character count.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Autosize = () => <Textarea
    label="Remarks"
    placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
    onValueChange={() => {}}
    autosize
    minRows={2}
    maxRows={6} />;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Textarea
    label="Remarks"
    placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
    onValueChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Grow with the text

`autosize` makes the field grow and shrink with its content between `minRows` (3 by default) and `maxRows`, then scroll.

```tsx
const Autosize = () => <Textarea
    label="Remarks"
    placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
    onValueChange={() => {}}
    autosize
    minRows={2}
    maxRows={6} />;
```

### Character count

`showCount` shows "used / max" under the field when `maxLength` is set. The browser stops input at the limit.

```tsx
const CharacterCount = () => <Textarea
    label="Remarks"
    placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
    onValueChange={() => {}}
    maxLength={280}
    showCount
    defaultValue="Night work only." />;
```

### States

Textarea takes the same field props as **TextInput**.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <Textarea
        placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Shown on the work order." />
    <Textarea
        placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="With error"
        error="Add a remark"
        required />
    <Textarea
        placeholder="Anything the contractor should know"
        onValueChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled
        defaultValue="Approved." />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFTextarea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFTextarea name="remarks" label="Remarks" autosize maxLength={500} showCount />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` |  | The text, to control the field. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting text, when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement, Element>` |  | The native change event, as with a plain `<textarea>`. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new text after any change. |
| `autosize` | `boolean` |  | Grow and shrink with the text, between `minRows` and `maxRows`. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `maxRows` | `number` |  |  |
| `showCount` | `boolean` |  | Show "used / max" under the field when `maxLength` is set. |

Native `<textarea>` attributes pass through. The ref goes to the `<textarea>`.

## Styling

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-textarea` | `control` | The `<textarea>` |
| `.kit-field__count` | — | The character count |

The label, description and error use the **TextInput** field classes.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Textarea](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/textarea). It stays a native `<textarea>`, so editing, selection and spell checking work as usual. Enter adds a new line and never submits the form.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Size the field to the expected length: `minRows={2}` for a short note, more for a description.
- Set `maxLength` when the server has a limit, and show the count.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for one-line values. Use `TextInput`.

## Related

- **TextInput**: one line of text.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs

---

# Autocomplete

Import: `import { Autocomplete } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A text field that suggests values as you type. Unlike **Select**, any text is a valid value: the suggestions only help fill it in.

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Autocomplete
    label="District"
    data={[
      'Gombak',
      'Hulu Langat',
      'Hulu Selangor',
      'Klang',
      'Kuala Langat',
      'Kuala Selangor',
      'Petaling',
      'Sabak Bernam',
      'Sepang',
    ]}
    placeholder="Type a district"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Free text

`onChange` receives the text, whether it was typed or picked from the suggestions.

```tsx
const FreeText = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState('Kajang')

    return (
        <>
            <Autocomplete
                label="District"
                data={[
                  'Gombak',
                  'Hulu Langat',
                  'Hulu Selangor',
                  'Klang',
                  'Kuala Langat',
                  'Kuala Selangor',
                  'Petaling',
                  'Sabak Bernam',
                  'Sepang',
                ]}
                placeholder="Type a district"
                value={value}
                onChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {JSON.stringify(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

### No match

`nothingFoundMessage` shows while nothing matches. Leave it out to show nothing.

```tsx
const NothingFound = () => <Autocomplete
    label="District"
    data={[
      'Gombak',
      'Hulu Langat',
      'Hulu Selangor',
      'Klang',
      'Kuala Langat',
      'Kuala Selangor',
      'Petaling',
      'Sabak Bernam',
      'Sepang',
    ]}
    placeholder="Type a district"
    onChange={() => {}}
    nothingFoundMessage="No matching district. You can still use it." />;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFAutocomplete } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFAutocomplete name="district" label="District" data={districts} />
```

The form value is a `string`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `data` | `SelectData` |  | Suggestions. The value is free text; suggestions only help fill it. |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  |  |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `nothingFoundMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | Text while no suggestion matches. Leave empty to show nothing. |
| `maxDropdownHeight` | `number` | `240` | Max height of the list, in px. |

## Styling

The field uses the **TextInput** classes and the suggestions use the **Select** list classes (`.kit-listbox*`).

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Autocomplete](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/autocomplete), which follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete. Focus stays in the input while the arrow keys move the highlight.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the suggestions and opens the list |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlight |
| Enter | Fills in the highlighted suggestion and closes the list, without submitting |
| Escape | Closes the list and keeps the text |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it when most answers come from a known list, but others are allowed.

**Don't**

- Don't use it when the value must come from the list. Use `Select` with `searchable`.

## Related

- **Select**: when only listed values are allowed.
- **SearchInput**: a search box without suggestions.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-combobox-autocomplete--docs

---

# InfiniteSelect

Import: `import { InfiniteSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A Select whose options come from a paged, searchable API. Give it one `loadOptions` function and it handles the rest: it waits for typing to pause, loads the next page as the list scrolls, cancels requests that a newer search made stale, and remembers the labels of chosen values. Add `multiple` for a MultiSelect.

```tsx
import { InfiniteSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <InfiniteSelect
    label="Contractor"
    placeholder="Search contractors"
    loadOptions={fetchContractors} />;
```

## Examples

### Loading options

`loadOptions` receives `{ search, page, signal }` and returns `{ options, hasMore }`. `page` starts at 0. Pass `signal` to `fetch`, so a stale request is cancelled. It works with any fetcher and has no data-library dependency.

```tsx
<InfiniteSelect
  label="Contractor"
  loadOptions={async ({ search, page, signal }) => {
    const res = await api.contractors({ search, page: page + 1, size: 20 }, { signal })
    return {
      options: res.data.map((c) => ({ value: c.uuid, label: c.name })),
      hasMore: res.meta.page < res.meta.last_page,
    }
  }}
/>
```

`debounceMs` (300 by default) sets how long to wait after typing before searching.

### Multiple

```tsx
const Multiple = () => (
  <InfiniteSelect
    multiple
    label="Contractors"
    placeholder="Add contractors"
    loadOptions={fetchContractors}
  />
);
```

### Editing a saved value

When a form opens with a saved value, its option may be on a page that hasn't loaded yet. Pass it in `initialOptions` so the field shows its label straight away.

```tsx
const EditSavedValue = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>('c-42')
  return (
    <>
      <InfiniteSelect
        label="Contractor"
        loadOptions={fetchContractors}
        value={value}
        onChange={setValue}
        initialOptions={[{ value: 'c-42', label: 'Contractor 42 Sdn Bhd' }]}
      />
      <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {String(value)}</p>
    </>
  )
};
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFInfiniteSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFInfiniteSelect name="contractorId" label="Contractor" loadOptions={loadContractors} />
```

## Props

Takes the props of **Select** (or **MultiSelect** with `multiple`), except `data` and the async props, which it manages. Plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loadOptions` (required) | `LoadOptions` |  | Fetches one page of options for a search. |
| `initialOptions` | `SelectOption[]` |  | Options for values already selected, so their labels show before their page loads, like when editing a saved record. |
| `debounceMs` | `number` | `300` | Wait this long after typing before searching, in ms. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Styling

Same as **Select**, or **MultiSelect** with `multiple`.

## Accessibility

Same as **Select** or **MultiSelect**. Reaching the last option with the keyboard loads the next page, and a status in the list tells screen readers while it loads.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for lists that are too long to load at once: contractors, users, assets.
- Return 20 or so options a page.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for short, fixed lists. Use `Select`.

## Related

- **Select** with the async props: if you'd rather manage paging yourself, for example with TanStack Query's `useInfiniteQuery`.
- **MultiSelect**: several values from a list you already have.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-combobox-infiniteselect--docs

---

# MultiSelect

Import: `import { MultiSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Picks several options. Chosen values show as removable chips in the field, and typing filters the list. It can create options from the typed text, and search and page through options on the server.

```tsx
import { MultiSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <MultiSelect
    label="States"
    data={states}
    placeholder="Add states"
    defaultValue={['Johor', 'Selangor']}
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Limit and clear

`maxValues` caps how many can be chosen: once reached, the other options are disabled. `clearable` adds a button that removes every value.

```tsx
const MaxValues = () => <MultiSelect
    label="States"
    data={states}
    placeholder="Add states"
    defaultValue={['Johor', 'Selangor']}
    onChange={() => {}}
    maxValues={3}
    clearable
    description="Up to 3 states" />;
```

### Create options

With `creatable`, the list offers the typed text as a new option. `onCreateOption` receives the text and returns the new option, or a Promise of it, for example after saving it on the server. The option is then selected. Add it to `data` as well, so it keeps its label.

```tsx
const Creatable = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>(['urgent'])
    const [tags, setTags] = useState([
      { value: 'urgent', label: 'Urgent' },
      { value: 'night-work', label: 'Night work' },
      { value: 'lane-closure', label: 'Lane closure' },
    ])

    return (
        <MultiSelect
            defaultValue={['Johor', 'Selangor']}
            label="Tags"
            placeholder="Add or create tags"
            data={tags}
            value={value}
            onChange={setValue}
            creatable
            onCreateOption={(query) => {
              const option = { value: query.toLowerCase(), label: query }
              setTags((t) => [...t, option])
              return option
            }} />
    );
};
```

```tsx
<MultiSelect
  label="Tags"
  data={tags}
  creatable
  onCreateOption={async (query) => {
    const tag = await api.createTag(query)
    return { value: tag.id, label: tag.name }
  }}
/>
```

### Groups

`data` takes the same shapes as **Select**, including groups.

```tsx
const Grouped = () => <MultiSelect
    label="Assets"
    data={[
      { group: 'Pavement', items: ['Flexible', 'Rigid'] },
      { group: 'Structures', items: ['Bridge', 'Culvert', 'Tunnel'] },
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick assets"
    defaultValue={[]}
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

### Server-side search and paging

MultiSelect has the same async props as Select: `onSearchChange`, `loading`, `hasMore` and `onLoadMore`, plus `getOptionLabel` for chosen values that aren't in the current page. See **Select** for an example, or use `InfiniteSelect` with `multiple`. `keepSearchOnSelect` keeps the typed text after each choice, so people can pick several matches in a row.

### States

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <MultiSelect
        data={states}
        placeholder="Add states"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Required"
        required
        defaultValue={[]}
        error="Pick at least one state" />
    <MultiSelect
        data={states}
        placeholder="Add states"
        defaultValue={['Johor', 'Selangor']}
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFMultiSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFMultiSelect name="states" label="States" data={states} rules={{ validate: (v) => v.length > 0 || 'Pick at least one' }} />
```

The form value is a `string[]`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `onSearchChange` | `((query: string) => void)` |  | Called with the search text as the user types. Pair it with `filter={false}` (set automatically) to search on the server. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Show a loading state in the list. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` |  | More options exist: `onLoadMore` runs when the list scrolls to the end. |
| `onLoadMore` | `(() => void)` |  | Load the next page. |
| `nothingFoundMessage` | `ReactNode` | `'Nothing found'` | Text while nothing matches. |
| `data` | `SelectData` |  |  |
| `value` | `string[]` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` |  |  |
| `onBlur` | `(() => void)` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `maxValues` | `number` |  | The most values that can be chosen. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears every value. |
| `creatable` | `boolean` |  | Offer to create an option from the search text. |
| `onCreateOption` | `((query: string) => SelectOption \| Promise<SelectOption \| null> \| null) \| undefined` |  | Turn the search text into a new option. Return the option (or a Promise of it) and it's selected. Required with `creatable`. |
| `getOptionLabel` | `((value: string) => string)` |  | Label for values not present in `data`, like async results. |
| `keepSearchOnSelect` | `boolean` |  | Keep the search text after choosing an option. |
| `maxDropdownHeight` | `number` | `280` | Max height of the list, in px. |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-multiselect` | The field box |
| `.kit-multiselect__chips` | The chips row |
| `.kit-chip-tag` | One chosen value |
| `.kit-chip-tag__remove` | A chip's remove button |
| `.kit-multiselect__input` | The search input |
| `.kit-listbox__create` | The "Create …" option |

The popup list uses the same `.kit-listbox*` classes as **Select**.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Combobox](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/combobox) with multiple selection. The input is a combobox named by the label. The chips are a toolbar named by the same label, and each remove button is named after its value.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the options and opens the list |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Opens the list, then moves the highlight |
| Enter | Chooses the highlighted option, or creates one |
| Escape | Closes the list |
| Backspace | In an empty input, removes the last chip |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Move between chips |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it when people need more than one value from a long list.
- Set `maxValues` when there's a real limit, and say so in `description`.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for fewer than about six options. Use checkboxes.
- Don't allow `creatable` unless new values are really welcome. It invites typos and duplicates.

## Related

- **Select**: one value.
- **InfiniteSelect**: the same with `multiple`, for large remote lists.
- **Chip**: filters as toggles.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-combobox-multiselect--docs

---

# Select

Import: `import { Select } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Picks one option from a list. Add `searchable` to filter the list, `clearable` to allow no value, and the async props to search and page through options on the server.

```tsx
import { Select } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Searchable = () => <Select
    label="State"
    data={[
      'Johor',
      'Kedah',
      'Kelantan',
      'Melaka',
      'Negeri Sembilan',
      'Pahang',
      'Perak',
      'Perlis',
      'Pulau Pinang',
      'Sabah',
      'Sarawak',
      'Selangor',
      'Terengganu',
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick a state"
    onChange={() => {}}
    searchable
    clearable />;
```

**Pick the right list component:**

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One value from a fixed list | `Select` |
| Several values, or values the user can create | `MultiSelect` |
| Free text with suggestions, where any text is allowed | `Autocomplete` |
| One value from a large remote list that loads page by page | `InfiniteSelect`, or `Select` with the async props (below) |
| Two to five options, all visible at once | `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` |

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Select
    label="State"
    data={[
      'Johor',
      'Kedah',
      'Kelantan',
      'Melaka',
      'Negeri Sembilan',
      'Pahang',
      'Perak',
      'Perlis',
      'Pulau Pinang',
      'Sabah',
      'Sarawak',
      'Selangor',
      'Terengganu',
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick a state"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Options

`data` takes three shapes, and you can mix them:

```tsx
// Strings: each one is both the value and the label.
data={['Draft', 'Published']}

// Objects: a separate value and label, and optionally disabled.
data={[{ value: 'draft', label: 'Draft' }, { value: 'archived', label: 'Archived', disabled: true }]}

// Groups: options under a heading.
data={[{ group: 'Pavement', items: ['Flexible', 'Rigid'] }]}
```

```tsx
const OptionObjects = () => <Select
    label="Status"
    data={[
      { value: 'draft', label: 'Draft' },
      { value: 'review', label: 'In review' },
      { value: 'published', label: 'Published' },
      { value: 'archived', label: 'Archived', disabled: true },
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick a status"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

### Groups

```tsx
const Grouped = () => <Select
    label="Asset"
    data={[
      { group: 'Pavement', items: ['Flexible', 'Rigid'] },
      {
        group: 'Structures',
        items: [
          'Bridge',
          'Culvert',
          { value: 'tunnel', label: 'Tunnel', disabled: true },
        ],
      },
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick an asset"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

### Controlled

Pass `value` and `onChange` to own the state. `onChange` receives the value, or `null` when cleared, plus the whole option object. Use `defaultValue` instead to let the Select keep its own state.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>('Selangor')

    return (
        <>
            <Select
                label="State"
                data={[
                  'Johor',
                  'Kedah',
                  'Kelantan',
                  'Melaka',
                  'Negeri Sembilan',
                  'Pahang',
                  'Perak',
                  'Perlis',
                  'Pulau Pinang',
                  'Sabah',
                  'Sarawak',
                  'Selangor',
                  'Terengganu',
                ]}
                placeholder="Pick a state"
                clearable
                value={value}
                onChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {String(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = useState<string | null>(null)

<Select
  label="Status"
  data={statuses}
  value={status}
  onChange={(value, option) => setStatus(value)}
/>
```

### Field states

Select takes the same field props as every kit input: `label`, `description`, `error`, `required`, `withAsterisk`, `disabled` and `readOnly`. A read-only Select stays focusable and submits its value. A disabled one does neither.

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <Select
        data={[
          'Johor',
          'Kedah',
          'Kelantan',
          'Melaka',
          'Negeri Sembilan',
          'Pahang',
          'Perak',
          'Perlis',
          'Pulau Pinang',
          'Sabah',
          'Sarawak',
          'Selangor',
          'Terengganu',
        ]}
        placeholder="Pick a state"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With description"
        description="Where the work takes place." />
    <Select
        data={[
          'Johor',
          'Kedah',
          'Kelantan',
          'Melaka',
          'Negeri Sembilan',
          'Pahang',
          'Perak',
          'Perlis',
          'Pulau Pinang',
          'Sabah',
          'Sarawak',
          'Selangor',
          'Terengganu',
        ]}
        placeholder="Pick a state"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Required"
        required />
    <Select
        data={[
          'Johor',
          'Kedah',
          'Kelantan',
          'Melaka',
          'Negeri Sembilan',
          'Pahang',
          'Perak',
          'Perlis',
          'Pulau Pinang',
          'Sabah',
          'Sarawak',
          'Selangor',
          'Terengganu',
        ]}
        placeholder="Pick a state"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="With error"
        error="Pick a state" />
    <Select
        data={[
          'Johor',
          'Kedah',
          'Kelantan',
          'Melaka',
          'Negeri Sembilan',
          'Pahang',
          'Perak',
          'Perlis',
          'Pulau Pinang',
          'Sabah',
          'Sarawak',
          'Selangor',
          'Terengganu',
        ]}
        placeholder="Pick a state"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled
        defaultValue="Johor" />
    <Select
        data={[
          'Johor',
          'Kedah',
          'Kelantan',
          'Melaka',
          'Negeri Sembilan',
          'Pahang',
          'Perak',
          'Perlis',
          'Pulau Pinang',
          'Sabah',
          'Sarawak',
          'Selangor',
          'Terengganu',
        ]}
        placeholder="Pick a state"
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Read-only"
        readOnly
        defaultValue="Johor" />
</div>;
```

### Sizes

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Select key={size} {...args} size={size} label={`Size ${size}`} />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### Left section

```tsx
const WithLeftSection = () => <Select
    label="State"
    data={[
      'Johor',
      'Kedah',
      'Kelantan',
      'Melaka',
      'Negeri Sembilan',
      'Pahang',
      'Perak',
      'Perlis',
      'Pulau Pinang',
      'Sabah',
      'Sarawak',
      'Selangor',
      'Terengganu',
    ]}
    placeholder="Pick a state"
    onChange={() => {}}
    leftSection={<icons.SearchIcon />} />;
```

### Server-side search and paging

For a list too big to load at once, search and page on the server:

- `onSearchChange` is called as the user types. Setting it turns off local filtering and shows the search field.
- `loading` shows a loader in the list.
- `hasMore` and `onLoadMore` load the next page when the list scrolls to the end.
- `getOptionLabel` gives the trigger a label for a selected value that isn't in the current page of `data`.

```tsx
const ServerSide = () => {
    const [search, setSearch] = useState('')
    const [page, setPage] = useState(0)
    const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
    const [options, setOptions] = useState<SelectOption[]>([])
    const matches = contractors.filter((c) =>
      c.label.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase()),
    )

    useEffect(() => {
      setLoading(true)
      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
        setOptions(matches.slice(0, (page + 1) * 10))
        setLoading(false)
      }, 400)
      return () => clearTimeout(timer)
    }, [search, page])

    return (
        <Select
            onChange={() => {}}
            label="Contractor"
            placeholder="Search contractors"
            data={options}
            loading={loading}
            onSearchChange={(query) => {
              setSearch(query)
              setPage(0)
            }}
            hasMore={options.length < matches.length}
            onLoadMore={() => setPage((p) => p + 1)} />
    );
};
```

```tsx
const [search, setSearch] = useState('')
const query = useInfiniteQuery({ queryKey: ['contractors', search], … })

<Select
  label="Contractor"
  data={query.data?.pages.flat().map((c) => ({ value: c.uuid, label: c.name }))}
  onSearchChange={setSearch}
  loading={query.isFetching}
  hasMore={query.hasNextPage}
  onLoadMore={query.fetchNextPage}
/>
```

If you'd rather pass a single `loadOptions` function and let the component handle paging, use `InfiniteSelect`.

## Use with react-hook-form

`RHFSelect` from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form` takes the same props plus `name`, and wires value, change, blur and the error message to the form.

```tsx
import { FormProvider, useForm } from 'react-hook-form'
import { RHFSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

const form = useForm({ defaultValues: { state: null } })

<FormProvider {...form}>
  <RHFSelect name="state" label="State" data={states} rules={{ required: true }} />
</FormProvider>
```

See **Forms with react-hook-form** for config-driven forms.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `onSearchChange` | `((query: string) => void)` |  | Called with the search text as the user types. Pair it with `filter={false}` (set automatically) to search on the server. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Show a loading state in the list. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` |  | More options exist: `onLoadMore` runs when the list scrolls to the end. |
| `onLoadMore` | `(() => void)` |  | Load the next page. |
| `nothingFoundMessage` | `ReactNode` | `'Nothing found'` | Text while nothing matches. |
| `data` | `SelectData` |  | The options. |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | The selected value, or `null` for none. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| null, option: SelectOption \| null) => void)` |  | Called with the new value, or `null` when cleared. |
| `onBlur` | `(() => void)` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `searchable` | `boolean` |  | Add a search field to the list. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears the selection. |
| `getOptionLabel` | `((value: string) => string)` |  | Label for a value not present in `data`, like an async result. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the trigger, before the value. |
| `maxDropdownHeight` | `number` | `280` | Max height of the list, in px. |

The ref goes to the trigger button.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-select` | The field box around the trigger |
| `.kit-select__trigger` | The button that opens the list |
| `.kit-select__value` | The selected label, or the placeholder |
| `.kit-select__chevron` | The arrow on the right |
| `.kit-input__clear` | The clear button (`clearable`) |
| `.kit-listbox` | The popup list |
| `.kit-listbox__search` | The search field in the list |
| `.kit-listbox__item` | One option |
| `.kit-listbox__group-label` | A group heading |
| `.kit-listbox__empty` | The "Nothing found" message |
| `[data-highlighted]`, `[data-selected]` | On the item under the keyboard or pointer, and on the chosen item (from ui-sdk) |

The `classNames` prop adds classes to the field parts: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error` and `control`. Selected options use the `primarySoft` token.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Select](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/select), which follows the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox pattern. The trigger has the `combobox` role and the list is a `listbox`. The `label` names the trigger, and the description and error describe it.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger, opens the list |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Moves through the options, skipping disabled ones |
| Home, End | Goes to the first or last option |
| Typing | Jumps to the next option that starts with the typed text |
| Enter | Chooses the option, closes the list and returns focus to the trigger |
| Escape | Closes without choosing and returns focus to the trigger |

If a Select has no visible `label`, give it an `aria-label`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Always give it a `label`. The placeholder disappears once there's a value.
- Add `searchable` when there are more than about 10 options.
- Use option objects with stable IDs as values, so renaming a label doesn't break saved data.

**Don't**

- Don't use Select for two or three options. Show them all with `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup`.
- Don't load thousands of options at once. Use the server-side props or `InfiniteSelect`.
- Don't use the placeholder as a label or for instructions. Use `description`.

## Related

- **MultiSelect**, **Autocomplete** and **InfiniteSelect**: the rest of the combobox family.
- **SegmentedControl** and **RadioGroup**: for a few options.
- **RHFSelect**: the react-hook-form version.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-combobox-select--docs

---

# DatePicker

Import: `import { DatePicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar. The value is always an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string, whatever the field shows.

```tsx
import { DatePicker, toDateString } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <DatePicker label="Start date" defaultValue="2026-11-17" clearable onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Values

`onChange` receives `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` when cleared. `value` and `defaultValue` also accept a `Date`, or any string `Date` can read, like the HTTP date format some APIs send. They are converted to the local calendar date.

```tsx
const ApiDates = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null)

    return (
        <>
            <DatePicker
                clearable
                label="From an API"
                defaultValue="Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:00:00 GMT"
                onChange={setValue} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>onChange value: {String(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

To convert a value yourself, use `toDateString(value)`.

### Min and max

`minDate` and `maxDate` limit which dates can be picked. Dates outside the range are disabled in the calendar.

```tsx
const MinAndMax = () => <DatePicker
    label="Due date"
    defaultValue={null}
    clearable
    onChange={() => {}}
    minDate="2026-11-01"
    maxDate="2026-12-31"
    description="November or December 2026" />;
```

### Written out

`displayFormat` takes `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options and shows the date written out, like "17 November 2026". The field then can't be typed in: pressing it opens the calendar. `locale` sets the language and defaults to the page's.

```tsx
const WrittenOut = () => <DatePicker
    label="Inspection date"
    defaultValue="2026-11-17"
    clearable
    onChange={() => {}}
    placeholder="Pick a date"
    locale="en-GB"
    displayFormat={{ day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }}
    leftSection={<icons.CalendarIcon />} />;
```

### States

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <DatePicker
        clearable
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Required"
        required
        defaultValue={null}
        error="Pick a start date" />
    <DatePicker
        defaultValue="2026-11-17"
        clearable
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled />
    <DatePicker
        defaultValue="2026-11-17"
        clearable
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Read-only"
        readOnly />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFDatePicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFDatePicker name="startDate" label="Start date" minDate="2026-01-01" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

The form value is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string or `null`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| Date \| null` |  | The date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null`. A `Date`, or any date string `Date` can read, is accepted and converted. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| Date \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| null) => void)` |  | Called with `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` when cleared. |
| `onBlur` | `(() => void)` |  |  |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date` |  | Earliest pickable date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date` |  | Latest pickable date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears the date. Hidden while disabled or read-only. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown while the field is empty. |
| `displayFormat` | `DateTimeFormatOptions` |  | Show the date written out, like `{ day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }` for "21 May 2026", instead of a typed field. The field then opens the calendar when pressed, and can't be typed in. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the field, before the date, like a calendar icon. |
| `locale` | `string` | `the page's language` |  |
| `triggerLabel` | `string` | `'Choose date'` | Label of the button that opens the calendar. |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-date` | The field box |
| `.kit-date__input` | The typed input |
| `.kit-date__display` | The written-out date (with `displayFormat`) |
| `.kit-date__trigger` | The calendar button |
| `.kit-popover.kit-calendar` | The calendar popup |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Date Picker](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/date-picker), which follows the WAI-ARIA date picker dialog pattern: a plain text input, a button that opens a dialog, and a grid of days inside it. Focus moves into the grid when it opens and back to the button when a date is picked.

| Key | Where | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter | Input | Commits the typed date |
| Alt + ArrowDown | Input | Opens the calendar |
| Enter, Space | Calendar button | Opens or closes the calendar |
| Arrow keys | Calendar | Move between days |
| Page Up, Page Down | Calendar | Previous or next month |
| Escape | Calendar | Closes it |

`triggerLabel` sets the calendar button's name ("Choose date" by default). Translate it for other languages.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Set `minDate` and `maxDate` when only some dates make sense.
- Use `displayFormat` when the date is usually picked, not typed, and reading it matters, like on a summary form.

**Don't**

- Don't format the value yourself before saving. Send the ISO string to the API.

## Related

- **MonthPicker**: when only the month matters.
- **TimeInput**: a time of day.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-dates-datepicker--docs

---

# MonthPicker

Import: `import { MonthPicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A month field for reports, claims and anything billed by the month. It opens a year switcher and a grid of months. The value is a `YYYY-MM` string.

```tsx
import { MonthPicker, toMonthString } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <MonthPicker label="Reporting month" defaultValue="2026-03" clearable onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Controlled

`onChange` receives `YYYY-MM`, or `null` when cleared. `value` also accepts a `Date`. `toMonthString(value)` converts a Date or ISO string for you.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [month, setMonth] = useState<string | null>('2026-03')

    return (
        <MonthPicker
            label="Reporting month"
            clearable
            value={month}
            onChange={setMonth}
            defaultValue={undefined}
            description={month ? `Value: ${month}` : 'No month picked'} />
    );
};
```

### Range and format

`minMonth` and `maxMonth` limit which months can be picked. `monthFormat` shows "March 2026" (`long`, default) or "Mar 2026" (`short`).

### States

```tsx
const States = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <MonthPicker
        clearable
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Required"
        required
        defaultValue={null}
        error="Pick a month" />
    <MonthPicker
        defaultValue="2026-03"
        clearable
        onChange={() => {}}
        label="Disabled"
        disabled />
</div>;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFMonthPicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFMonthPicker name="reportMonth" label="Reporting month" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| Date \| null` |  | The month as `YYYY-MM`, or `null`. A `Date` is accepted and converted. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| Date \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| null) => void)` |  | Called with `YYYY-MM`, or `null` when cleared. |
| `onBlur` | `(() => void)` |  |  |
| `minMonth` | `string \| Date` |  | Earliest pickable month, `YYYY-MM`. |
| `maxMonth` | `string \| Date` |  | Latest pickable month, `YYYY-MM`. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show a button that clears the month. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown while no month is picked. |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content inside the field, before the month, like a calendar icon. |
| `locale` | `string` | `the page's language` |  |
| `monthFormat` | `enum` | `'long'` | How the field shows the month: `long` is "March 2026", `short` "Mar 2026". |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-month__trigger` | The field, a button that opens the popup |
| `.kit-month__value` | The month shown in the field |
| `.kit-month__popup` | The popup |
| `.kit-month__header`, `.kit-month__year`, `.kit-month__nav` | The year switcher |
| `.kit-month__grid`, `.kit-month__cell` | The months |

## Accessibility

The kit builds this one on ui-sdk's popover. The field is a button named by its label that opens the popup, and focus moves to the chosen month (or the current one).

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | On the field, opens the popup. On a month, picks it |
| Arrow keys | Move between months |
| Page Up, Page Down | Previous or next year |
| Home, End | January or December |
| Escape | Closes the popup |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it whenever the day doesn't matter, rather than a DatePicker with the day ignored.

## Related

- **DatePicker**: a full date.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-dates-monthpicker--docs

# TimeInput

Import: `import { TimeInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A time-of-day field, typed segment by segment: hours, minutes and, on a 12-hour clock, AM or PM. The value is always 24-hour `HH:mm`.

```tsx
import { TimeInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <TimeInput label="Inspection time" defaultValue="09:30" onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Clocks

`hourCycle` shows a 12 or 24-hour clock, and defaults to the locale's. `withSeconds` adds a seconds segment.

```tsx
const Clocks = () => <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <TimeInput defaultValue="09:30" onChange={() => {}} label="24-hour" hourCycle={24} />
    <TimeInput defaultValue="09:30" onChange={() => {}} label="12-hour" hourCycle={12} />
    <TimeInput defaultValue="09:30" onChange={() => {}} label="With seconds" withSeconds />
</div>;
```

### Controlled

`onChange` receives `HH:mm` (or `HH:mm:ss` with seconds), or `null` while the time is incomplete or empty. That's true even when a 12-hour clock is shown.

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>('14:30')

    return (
        <>
            <TimeInput
                label="Inspection time"
                hourCycle={12}
                value={value}
                onChange={setValue}
                defaultValue={undefined} />
            <p style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>Value: {String(value)}</p>
        </>
    );
};
```

### Min and max

`min` and `max` take `HH:mm`. A time outside the range is marked invalid.

```tsx
const WorkingHours = () => <TimeInput
    label="Lane closure from"
    defaultValue="21:00"
    onChange={() => {}}
    min="22:00"
    max="23:59"
    description="Night work: from 22:00" />;
```

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFTimeInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFTimeInput name="inspectionTime" label="Inspection time" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | An error to show. A string or node shows that message; `true` marks the field invalid without a message; `false` or empty clears it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required: the browser blocks submit and the label shows an asterisk. |
| `withAsterisk` | `boolean` |  | Show the asterisk without making the control natively required. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` | Control height and text size. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<FieldPart, string>>` |  | Classes for each part: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `control`. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the control submits under. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | The time as `HH:mm` (24-hour), or `null`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| null) => void)` |  |  |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `withSeconds` | `boolean` |  | Show seconds as well. |
| `hourCycle` | `enum` | `the locale's` | Use a 12 or 24 hour clock. |
| `min` | `string` |  |  |
| `max` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

The box uses the **TextInput** classes. The segments are inside `.kit-time__input`, and each has `[data-type]` (`hour`, `minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod`) from ui-sdk.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Time Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/time-input). The field is a group named by its label, and each segment is a spinbutton named by its unit.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Digits | Fill the segment and move to the next |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Step the segment, wrapping around |
| Page Up, Page Down | Bigger steps |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Move between segments |
| Backspace | Empties the segment, then moves back |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Store and send the 24-hour value. Let the field show the user's clock.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for durations ("2 hours 30 minutes"). Use `NumberInput`.

## Related

- **DatePicker**: a date.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-dates-timeinput--docs
