# ActionMenu

Import: `import { ActionMenu } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A button that opens a list of actions: the "⋮" menu on a table row, an Export menu, an account menu. Pass the items as data. They can be grouped under headings and carry a second line of description.

```tsx
import { ActionMenu } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const RowActions = () => <div
    style={{
      display: 'flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: 8,
      padding: 12,
      border: '1px solid var(--ui-border)',
      borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
      maxWidth: 480,
    }}>
    <span style={{ flex: 1 }}>PKG-004 · Road upgrade section 4</span>
    <Button size="sm" variant="light">Open
              </Button>
    <ActionMenu
        items={[
          { label: 'Edit', icon: <icons.PlusIcon />, onClick: () => toast('Edit') },
          { label: 'Duplicate', onClick: () => toast('Duplicate') },
          { label: 'Archive', disabled: true },
          { type: 'separator' },
          { label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: () => toast.error('Deleted') },
        ]}
        side="bottom"
        aria-label="Actions for PKG-004"
        align="end" />
</div>;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <ActionMenu
    items={[
      { label: 'Edit', icon: <icons.PlusIcon />, onClick: () => toast('Edit') },
      { label: 'Duplicate', onClick: () => toast('Duplicate') },
      { label: 'Archive', disabled: true },
      { type: 'separator' },
      { label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: () => toast.error('Deleted') },
    ]}
    side="bottom"
    align="start" />;
```

## Examples

### Items

Each item is `{ label, onClick }`, plus optional `icon`, `description`, `disabled`, `danger` or `href` (which renders a link). Add `{ type: 'separator' }` for a line between items.

```tsx
<ActionMenu
  aria-label="Actions for PKG-004"
  items={[
    { label: 'Edit', icon: <PencilIcon />, onClick: edit },
    { label: 'Duplicate', onClick: duplicate },
    { type: 'separator' },
    { label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: () => modals.confirm({ … }) },
  ]}
/>
```

### Groups

`{ type: 'group', label, items }` puts items under a heading. Leave out `label` for an untitled group.

```tsx
const Grouped = () => <ActionMenu
    items={[
      {
        type: 'group',
        label: 'Personal settings',
        items: [
          {
            label: 'General',
            description: 'Language, time zone and profile.',
            onClick: () => toast('General'),
          },
          {
            label: 'Notifications',
            description: 'Email and in-app notifications.',
            disabled: true,
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        type: 'group',
        label: 'Admin settings',
        items: [
          {
            label: 'User management',
            description: 'Add users and manage access.',
            onClick: () => toast('User management'),
          },
        ],
      },
    ]}
    side="bottom"
    align="end"
    aria-label="Settings"
    width={340} />;
```

### Custom trigger

The trigger is a small, square `subtle` icon button showing a vertical three-dot icon, named "More actions" by default. Pass another icon as `trigger`, with an `aria-label` that names it.

```tsx
const CustomTrigger = () => <ActionMenu
    items={[
      { label: 'Excel (.xlsx)', onClick: () => toast('Excel') },
      { label: 'CSV', onClick: () => toast('CSV') },
      { label: 'PDF', onClick: () => toast('PDF') },
    ]}
    side="bottom"
    align="start"
    trigger={<icons.UploadIcon />}
    aria-label="Export" />;
```

### Header

`header` shows content above the items that isn't an action, like the signed-in user.

```tsx
const WithHeader = () => <ActionMenu
    items={[
      { label: 'Profile', href: '#profile' },
      { type: 'separator' },
      { label: 'Sign out', onClick: () => toast('Signed out') },
    ]}
    side="bottom"
    align="start"
    aria-label="Account"
    header={(<div>
      <strong>Aisyah Rahman</strong>
      <div style={{ fontSize: 12, opacity: 0.7 }}>Project engineer</div>
    </div>)} />;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `ActionMenuItem[]` |  |  |
| `trigger` | `ReactNode` | `a vertical three-dot icon` | The trigger's content. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `'More actions'` | Accessible name of the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger button. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the popup. |
| `header` | `ReactNode` |  | Content above the items that isn't an action, like the signed-in user's name. |
| `width` | `string \| number` | `fits the items` | Popup width, any CSS length. |
| `side` | `enum` | `bottom` | Which side of the trigger the popup opens on. |
| `align` | `enum` | `start` | How the popup lines up with the trigger. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button.kit-icon-button` | The trigger (`className` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover.kit-menu` | The popup (`contentClassName` adds to it) |
| `.kit-menu__header` | The header |
| `.kit-menu__group`, `.kit-menu__group-label` | A group and its heading |
| `.kit-menu__item` | One action (`[data-danger]` for danger items) |
| `.kit-menu__icon` | The item's icon |
| `.kit-menu__label`, `.kit-menu__description` | The item's two lines |
| `.kit-menu__separator` | A separator |
| `[data-highlighted]` | The item under the keyboard or pointer (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Menu](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/menu), which follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, and the items are `menuitem`s.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger, opens the menu on the first item |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Move between items, skipping disabled ones |
| Home, End | First or last item |
| Typing | Jumps to the next item starting with the typed text |
| Enter, Space | Runs the item and closes the menu |
| Escape | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger |

On a table row, name each trigger after its row ("Actions for PKG-004"), so screen-reader users can tell the menus apart.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep the row's main action as a visible button, and put the rest in the menu.
- Put destructive actions last, after a separator, with `danger`.

**Don't**

- Don't hide the only way to do something in a menu.
- Don't put more than about seven items in one menu. Group them, or rethink.

## Related

- **Popover**: for content that isn't a list of actions.
- **ConfirmDialog**: confirm a destructive action from the menu.
- **DataTable**: has row actions built in.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-overlays-actionmenu--docs

---

# Dialog

Import: `import { Dialog } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Opens a focused task over the page, like editing a record or filling in a short form. It has a title, an optional description, a body and a footer for actions. Focus moves into the dialog when it opens, stays inside while it's open, and returns to where it was when it closes.

The kit has three ways to open one:

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A dialog with your own content and state | `Dialog` |
| A yes/no question before an action | `ConfirmDialog` |
| Either of those from an event handler, with no state to manage | `modals.open()` / `modals.confirm()` |

```tsx
import { ConfirmDialog, Dialog, modals } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <DialogDemo
    opened={false}
    onClose={() => {}}
    title="Edit package"
    size="md"
    withCloseButton
    closeOnClickOutside
    closeOnEscape
    centered />;
```

## Examples

### Basic usage

`Dialog` is controlled: you keep `opened` in state and close it in `onClose`. `onClose` runs on Escape, a press on the backdrop, or the × button.

```tsx
const [opened, setOpened] = useState(false)
const close = () => setOpened(false)

<Button onClick={() => setOpened(true)}>Edit package</Button>
<Dialog
  opened={opened}
  onClose={close}
  title="Edit package"
  description="Changes apply to every linked work order."
  footer={
    <>
      <Button variant="default" onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <TextInput label="Package name" />
</Dialog>
```

### Composition

A Dialog is built from these parts, top to bottom. Every part except the body is optional.

| Part | Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header | `title`, `withCloseButton` | The title names the dialog for screen readers. The × button shows by default. |
| Description | `description` | Read out when the dialog opens. Text renders in a `<p>`, anything richer in a `<div>`. |
| Body | `children` | Scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. |
| Footer | `footer` | Actions, right-aligned. Put Cancel first and the primary action last. |

### Sizes

`size` takes a preset (`xs` 352px, `sm` 416px, `md` 512px, `lg` 720px, `xl` 960px, `full`), a number of pixels, or any CSS length. `fullScreen` fills the viewport.

```tsx
const Sizes = args => <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const).map((size) => (
      <DialogDemo
        key={size}
        {...args}
        size={size}
        title={`Size ${size}`}
        trigger={size}
      />
    ))}
    <DialogDemo
        opened={false}
        onClose={() => {}}
        withCloseButton
        closeOnClickOutside
        closeOnEscape
        centered
        size="min(90vw, 1000px)"
        title="Custom width"
        trigger="min(90vw, 1000px)" />
    <DialogDemo
        opened={false}
        onClose={() => {}}
        size="md"
        withCloseButton
        closeOnClickOutside
        closeOnEscape
        centered
        fullScreen
        title="Full screen"
        trigger="fullScreen" />
</div>;
```

### Required decisions

Turn off `withCloseButton`, `closeOnEscape` and `closeOnClickOutside` when the user must pick an action in the footer. Keep this rare: a dialog people can't dismiss feels like a trap.

```tsx
const MustChoose = () => <DialogDemo
    opened={false}
    onClose={() => {}}
    title="Accept the new terms"
    size="md"
    withCloseButton={false}
    closeOnClickOutside={false}
    closeOnEscape={false}
    centered
    description="You need to accept them to keep using the portal."><p style={{ margin: 0 }}>The terms changed on 1 November.</p></DialogDemo>;
```

### Confirm an action

`ConfirmDialog` asks a question and renders the Cancel and Confirm buttons for you. Return a Promise from `onConfirm` and the dialog stays open, with the confirm button pending, until it settles. It closes when the Promise resolves and stays open if it rejects, so you can show the error. Add `danger` for destructive actions.

```tsx
const ConfirmAction = () => {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpened(true)}>
        Delete route
      </Button>
      <ConfirmDialog
        opened={opened}
        onClose={() => setOpened(false)}
        title="Delete route?"
        description="Route R-12 and its 4 work orders will be removed. This can't be undone."
        confirmLabel="Delete"
        danger
        onConfirm={() => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1200))}
      />
    </>
  )
};
```

```tsx
<ConfirmDialog
  opened={opened}
  onClose={close}
  title="Delete route?"
  description="This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  danger
  onConfirm={() => api.deleteRoute(id)}
/>
```

### Open from anywhere

`modals.open()` and `modals.confirm()` open a dialog from any event handler, with no state or JSX of your own. They need `UIKitProvider` with `withModals` (on by default).

```tsx
const Imperative = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12 }}>
    <Button
      variant="default"
      onClick={() =>
        modals.open({
          title: 'Route details',
          size: 'lg',
          children: <p>Anything can go here.</p>,
        })
      }
    >
      modals.open
    </Button>
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        modals.confirm({
          title: 'Publish package?',
          description: 'It becomes visible to contractors.',
          confirmLabel: 'Publish',
          onConfirm: () => toast.success('Published'),
        })
      }
    >
      modals.confirm
    </Button>
  </div>
);
```

```tsx
modals.confirm({
  title: 'Publish package?',
  description: 'It becomes visible to contractors.',
  confirmLabel: 'Publish',
  onConfirm: () => api.publish(id),
})
```

For a dialog that holds a react-hook-form form, use `FormDialog` or `openFormDialog()` from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form`. See **Forms with react-hook-form**.

## Props

### Dialog

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opened` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether it's open. |
| `onClose` (required) | `() => void` |  | Called when the dialog asks to close: Escape, the backdrop, or the close button. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the title, read out when the dialog opens. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons along the bottom, usually Cancel and a primary action. |
| `size` | `number \| (string & {}) \| DialogSize` | `md` | Width preset, a number of pixels, or any CSS length like `'640px'` or `'min(90vw, 1200px)'`. |
| `withCloseButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the × button. |
| `closeIcon` | `ReactNode` |  | What the × button shows instead of the kit's × icon. |
| `closeOnClickOutside` | `boolean` | `true` | Close when the backdrop is pressed. |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | `true` | Close on Escape. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the dialog in the page while closed. |
| `centered` | `boolean` | `true` | Centre vertically. |
| `fullScreen` | `boolean` |  | Fill the viewport. |
| `onTransitionEnd` | `((opened: boolean) => void)` |  | Called once it has finished opening or closing, after any animation. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<DialogPart, string>>` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |

### ConfirmDialog

Takes every Dialog prop except `footer`, plus these:

See the props of `ConfirmDialog` on the docs page or in its TypeScript types.

## Styling

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-dialog__backdrop` | `backdrop` | The dimmed layer behind |
| `.kit-dialog` | `content` | The dialog box |
| `.kit-dialog__header` | `header` | Title and × button row |
| `.kit-dialog__title` | `title` | The title |
| `.kit-dialog__description` | — | The description |
| `.kit-dialog__body` | `body` | Your content |
| `.kit-dialog__footer` | `footer` | The actions row |
| `.kit-dialog [aria-label="Close"]` | `close` | The × button |

| Attribute or variable | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `--kit-dialog-width` | The resolved width from `size` |
| `[data-centered]` | Present when `centered` |
| `[data-fullscreen]` | Present when `fullScreen` |
| `[data-open]`, `[data-starting-style]`, `[data-ending-style]` | Open state and animation hooks (from ui-sdk) |

The box uses the `surfaceRaised` token. The backdrop is a fixed 50% dark tint; override `.kit-dialog__backdrop` to change it.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Dialog](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/dialog), which follows the WAI-ARIA modal dialog pattern. The dialog sets `aria-modal`, is labelled by its title, and is described by its description.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves through the dialog's controls, staying inside |
| Escape | Closes the topmost dialog and returns focus to the element that opened it (unless `closeOnEscape` is off) |

- Always give a dialog a `title`. Without one, screen readers announce an unnamed dialog.
- Opening by touch focuses the dialog itself, so no on-screen keyboard appears.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep dialogs for short, focused tasks. Use a page for anything long or multi-step.
- Make the title a clear question or task: "Delete route?", "Edit package".
- Name the confirm button after the action ("Delete", "Publish"), not "OK" or "Yes".

**Don't**

- Don't open a dialog from another dialog. Change the content of the open one instead.
- Don't use a dialog for messages that need no decision. Use a `toast`.
- Don't use `ConfirmDialog` for actions that can be undone. Do the action and offer Undo in a toast.

## Related

- **ConfirmDialog** and `modals`: shortcuts for common dialogs.
- **FormDialog**: a dialog with a react-hook-form form.
- **Popover**: for small content next to its trigger, without blocking the page.
- **Toast**: for messages that need no decision.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-overlays-dialog--docs

---

# Popover

Import: `import { Popover } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A button that opens a floating panel of any content beside it: a notification list, a filter form, extra details. Escape and a press outside close it, and focus returns to the button. It doesn't block the page the way a Dialog does.

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Popover
    aria-label="Notifications"
    trigger={<span aria-hidden>🔔</span>}
    title="Notifications"
    width={320}
    side="bottom"
    align="start"
    onOpenChange={() => {}}><p style={{ margin: 0 }}>You're all caught up.</p></Popover>;
```

## Examples

### Trigger and title

Popover renders its own trigger: a small, square `subtle` icon button. Pass an icon as `trigger`, not a `<Button>`, and name it with `aria-label`. `title` is a heading in the popup and also names it for screen readers. Without a title, use `contentLabel`.

### A form inside

Control it with `opened` and `onOpenChange` to close it from inside, for example on Apply.

```tsx
const FilterPanel = () => {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Popover
      aria-label="Filters"
      trigger={<icons.SearchIcon />}
      title="Filter work orders"
      width={300}
      opened={opened}
      onOpenChange={setOpened}
    >
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
        <TextInput label="Contractor" size="sm" />
        <Checkbox label="Overdue only" size="sm" />
        <Checkbox label="Night work" size="sm" />
        <Button size="sm" onClick={() => setOpened(false)}>
          Apply
        </Button>
      </div>
    </Popover>
  )
};
```

### Placement

`side` picks the side of the trigger to open on, and `align` how the popup lines up with it. It flips to the other side when there isn't room.

```tsx
const Placement = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignSelf: 'center' }}>
    {(['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left'] as const).map((side) => (
      <Popover
        key={side}
        {...args}
        side={side}
        align="center"
        aria-label={`Opens on the ${side}`}
        trigger={<span aria-hidden>{side[0].toUpperCase()}</span>}
        title={`side="${side}"`}
        width={200}
      >
        <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Opens on the {side}.</p>
      </Popover>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The trigger's content, like an icon. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger. Required when the trigger is icon-only. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | A heading at the top of the popup; also its accessible name. |
| `contentLabel` | `string` |  | Names the popup when there's no visible `title`. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The popup's content. |
| `opened` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpened` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onOpenChange` | `((opened: boolean) => void)` |  |  |
| `side` | `enum` | `bottom` | Which side of the trigger the popup opens on. |
| `align` | `enum` | `start` | How the popup lines up with the trigger. |
| `width` | `string \| number` | `fits the content` | Popup width, any CSS length. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger button. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the popup. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button.kit-icon-button` | The trigger (`className` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover.kit-popover-panel` | The popup (`contentClassName` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover-panel__title` | The title |

The popup uses the `surfaceRaised`, `radiusLg` and `shadowLg` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Popover](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/popover). The trigger is a button with `aria-expanded` and the popup is a dialog named by `title` or `contentLabel`. Focus moves into the popup when it opens.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger, opens or closes the popup |
| Tab | Moves through the popup's content |
| Escape | Closes it and returns focus to the trigger |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for content that relates to the trigger and can be dismissed without losing work.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a list of actions. Use `ActionMenu`, which has menu keyboard behaviour.
- Don't put a long form in it. Use a `Dialog`.
- Don't use it for a hint. Use `Tooltip`.

## Related

- **ActionMenu**: a list of actions from a button.
- **Tooltip**: a short hint on hover.
- **Dialog**: for tasks that need the user's full attention.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs

---

# Toast

Import: `import { Toaster } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Short messages that appear in a corner and go away on their own: "Package saved", "Upload failed". Call `toast()` from anywhere, including outside components, like in a mutation's `onSuccess`.

```tsx
import { toast } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Kinds = () => (
  <div style={row}>
    <Button variant="default" onClick={() => toast('Route archived')}>
      Default
    </Button>
    <Button variant="default" onClick={() => toast.success('Package saved')}>
      Success
    </Button>
    <Button
      variant="default"
      onClick={() =>
        toast.error('Upload failed', {
          description: 'The file is over 10 MB.',
        })
      }
    >
      Error
    </Button>
    <Button
      variant="default"
      onClick={() => toast.warning('Session expires in 5 minutes')}
    >
      Warning
    </Button>
    <Button
      variant="default"
      onClick={() => toast.info('New version available')}
    >
      Info
    </Button>
  </div>
);
```

`UIKitProvider` renders the `Toaster`, the place toasts appear, so `toast()` works with no setup.

## Examples

### Kinds

`toast(title)` shows a plain message. `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning` and `toast.info` add an icon and a colour. Each takes a second `options` argument with a `description`.

```tsx
toast.success('Package saved')
toast.error('Upload failed', { description: 'The file is over 10 MB.' })
```

### Loading, then the result

`toast.loading()` shows a spinner and stays until updated. It returns an id: call another `toast` with the same `id` to replace it with the result.

```tsx
const LoadingToResult = () => (
  <Button
    variant="default"
    onClick={() => {
      const id = toast.loading('Exporting report…')
      setTimeout(
        () => toast.success('Report ready', { id, duration: 4000 }),
        1500,
      )
    }}
  >
    Export report
  </Button>
);
```

```tsx
const id = toast.loading('Exporting report…')
try {
  await api.exportReport()
  toast.success('Report ready', { id })
} catch {
  toast.error('Export failed', { id })
}
```

### Action

`action` adds a button, like Undo.

```tsx
const WithAction = () => (
  <Button
    variant="default"
    onClick={() =>
      toast('Route archived', {
        action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => toast('Restored') },
      })
    }
  >
    Archive route
  </Button>
);
```

### Duration and dismissing

Toasts close after 4 seconds. Set `duration` in ms, or `Infinity` to keep one until it's dismissed. `toast.dismiss(id)` closes one, and `toast.dismiss()` closes them all. `onDismiss` runs when it closes.

```tsx
const Persistent = () => (
  <div style={row}>
    <Button
      variant="default"
      onClick={() =>
        toast.warning('Connection lost', {
          id: 'offline',
          duration: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
          description: 'Changes will sync when you are back online.',
        })
      }
    >
      Show until dismissed
    </Button>
    <Button variant="subtle" onClick={() => toast.dismiss('offline')}>
      Dismiss it
    </Button>
  </div>
);
```

## API

### toast(title, options?)

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | A second line under the title |
| `duration` | `number` | In ms. `Infinity` keeps it until dismissed. Default 4000 |
| `id` | `string` | Reuse an id to update a toast instead of adding another |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | A button in the toast |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | Runs when it closes |

Also `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning`, `toast.info`, `toast.loading` (same arguments, each returns the id) and `toast.dismiss(id?)`.

### Toaster

Render it yourself only if you set `withToaster={false}` on `UIKitProvider`, for example to change where toasts appear.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `enum` | `bottom` |  |
| `align` | `enum` | `end` |  |
| `maxVisible` | `number` | `3` |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-toaster` | The stack of toasts |
| `.kit-toast` | One toast |
| `.kit-toast__icon` | The icon (`[data-type]` is the kind: `success`, `error`…) |
| `.kit-toast__title`, `.kit-toast__description` | The text |
| `.kit-toast__close` | The close button |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Toast](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/toast). Toasts are announced by screen readers through a live region without moving focus. The timer pauses while the pointer is over a toast or focus is inside it, so people have time to read it and reach the action.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Confirm actions people just took: saved, deleted, sent.
- Keep the title short, and put details in `description`.
- Offer Undo instead of a confirmation dialog for actions that can be undone.

**Don't**

- Don't use a toast for errors people must fix in a form. Show them next to the field.
- Don't put the only copy of important information in a toast. It disappears.

## Related

- **ConfirmDialog**: for decisions before an action.
- **UIKitProvider**: renders the Toaster.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-overlays-toast--docs

---

# Tooltip

Import: `import { Tooltip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A short hint that shows when the pointer rests on an element or it gets keyboard focus. On touch screens, pressing the element toggles it.

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const IconButtons = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
    <Tooltip label="Refresh">
      <IconButton aria-label="Refresh">
        <icons.RefreshIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip label="Add package">
      <IconButton aria-label="Add package">
        <icons.PlusIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip label="More actions">
      <IconButton aria-label="More actions">
        <icons.DotsVerticalIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
  </div>
);
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Tooltip label="Export to PDF" side="top" align="center" delay={300}><Button variant="default">Export</Button></Tooltip>;
```

## Examples

### Icon buttons

The most common use: an icon-only button names itself with `aria-label`, and the tooltip shows that name to sighted mouse users. The child must accept a ref and props, like a button, a link or a kit component.

```tsx
const IconButtons = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
    <Tooltip label="Refresh">
      <IconButton aria-label="Refresh">
        <icons.RefreshIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip label="Add package">
      <IconButton aria-label="Add package">
        <icons.PlusIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip label="More actions">
      <IconButton aria-label="More actions">
        <icons.DotsVerticalIcon />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
  </div>
);
```

### Arrow and long text

`withArrow` draws an arrow at the trigger. Text wraps at `maxWidth` (20rem by default).

```tsx
const WithArrow = () => <Tooltip label="Export to PDF" side="top" align="center" delay={300} withArrow><Button variant="default">Export</Button></Tooltip>;
```
```tsx
const LongText = () => <Tooltip
    label="Exports every visible column for the current filter. Large tables can take a minute."
    side="top"
    align="center"
    delay={300}
    maxWidth={240}
    withArrow><Button variant="default">Export</Button></Tooltip>;
```

### Sides

```tsx
const Sides = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12 }}>
    {(['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left'] as const).map((side) => (
      <Tooltip key={side} {...args} side={side} label={`side="${side}"`}>
        <Button variant="default">{side}</Button>
      </Tooltip>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What the tooltip says. With no label, the child renders on its own. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactElement<Record<string, any>, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | The element the tooltip points at. It must accept a ref and props, like a button, a link or a kit component. |
| `side` | `enum` | `top` |  |
| `align` | `enum` | `center` |  |
| `withArrow` | `boolean` |  | Draw an arrow pointing at the trigger. |
| `maxWidth` | `string \| number` | `20rem` | Wrap long text at this width, any CSS length. |
| `delay` | `number` | `300` | Pause before opening, in ms. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Don't show the tooltip; the child still renders. |
| `type` | `enum` | `description` | `description` (default) adds the label to the trigger's description. `label` makes it the trigger's name, for icon-only buttons. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-tooltip` | The tooltip (`className` adds to it) |
| `.kit-tooltip__arrow` | The arrow |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Tooltip](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/tooltip). By default (`type="description"`) the label is added to the trigger's description, so screen readers read it after the trigger's name. With `type="label"` it becomes the trigger's name instead, for an icon button that has no `aria-label`.

- It opens on keyboard focus as well as hover, after `delay` (300ms).
- Escape closes it.
- Never put interactive content in a tooltip. It can't be reached with the keyboard.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep it to a few words: name the action, or add one fact.
- Give every icon-only button a tooltip.

**Don't**

- Don't hide important information in a tooltip. People on touch screens rarely find it.
- Don't add a tooltip that repeats a visible label.

## Related

- **IconButton**: the usual trigger.
- **Popover**: for longer or interactive content.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs

---

# Loader

Import: `import { Loader } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Shows that something is loading: three staggered dots, or a spinning ring.

```tsx
import { Loader } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Variants = () => <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 32, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    <Loader size="md" variant="dots" />
    <Loader size="md" variant="spinner" />
</div>;
```

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A short wait with no layout to show | `Loader` |
| The shape of content that's coming | `Skeleton` |
| To block a panel or form while it works | `LoadingOverlay` |
| A button that's working | `Button` with `loading`, or an async `onClick` |

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Loader variant="dots" size="md" />;
```

## Examples

### Sizes

`size` goes from `xs` to `xl`. `color` takes any CSS colour. It defaults to the `primary` token, and to the text colour inside a button.

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    {(['dots', 'spinner'] as const).map((variant) => (
      <div
        key={variant}
        style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 24, alignItems: 'center' }}
      >
        {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const).map((size) => (
          <Loader key={size} {...args} variant={variant} size={size} />
        ))}
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### In context

Pass `label={null}` when text nearby already says what's loading, so screen readers don't hear it twice.

```tsx
const InContext = () => (
  <div
    style={{
      display: 'grid',
      justifyItems: 'center',
      gap: 12,
      padding: 32,
      border: '1px dashed var(--ui-border)',
      borderRadius: 'var(--ui-radius)',
      maxWidth: 360,
    }}
  >
    <Loader label={null} />
    <span>Loading work orders…</span>
    <Button size="sm" loading>
      Buttons have their own
    </Button>
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `enum` | `dots` | `dots` is the staggered three-dot loader; `spinner` a ring. |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` |  |
| `color` | `string` |  | Colour: any CSS colour. Defaults to the primary foreground of the context. |
| `label` | `string \| null` | `Loading` | What screen readers hear. Pass `null` when something nearby already says it's loading, like a button label. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-loader` | The loader (`[data-variant]`, `[data-size]`) |
| `.kit-loader__dot` | One dot |
| `.kit-loader__ring` | The ring |

## Accessibility

The loader has `role="status"` and is named by `label` ("Loading" by default), so screen readers announce it. With `label={null}` it's hidden from assistive technology. The animation slows down for people who ask for reduced motion.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Say what's loading when the wait may be long: "Loading work orders…".

**Don't**

- Don't show a loader for waits under about 300ms. It flickers.
- Don't use a loader where the page layout is known. A `Skeleton` keeps the page from jumping.

## Related

- **Skeleton**, **LoadingOverlay**, **Button**.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-feedback-loader--docs

---

# LoadingOverlay

Import: `import { LoadingOverlay } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Covers its parent with a translucent layer and a loader, so the content can't be used while it updates. The parent needs `position: relative`.

```tsx
import { LoadingOverlay } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <div style={{ position: 'relative', maxWidth: 360 }}>
    <LoadingOverlay visible blur label="Loading" />
    <Card title="Package details">
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
            <TextInput label="Package name" defaultValue="Road upgrade section 4" />
            <TextInput label="Package no." defaultValue="PKG-004" />
        </div>
    </Card>
</div>;
```

## Examples

### While saving

```tsx
<div style={{ position: 'relative' }}>
  <LoadingOverlay visible={mutation.isPending} label="Saving" />
  <PackageForm />
</div>
```

```tsx
const WhileSaving = () => {
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  return (
    <div style={{ position: 'relative', maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <LoadingOverlay visible={saving} label="Saving" />
      <Card
        title="Package details"
        footer={
          <Button
            onClick={() => {
              setSaving(true)
              setTimeout(() => setSaving(false), 1500)
            }}
          >
            Save
          </Button>
        }
      >
        <TextInput
          label="Package name"
          defaultValue="Road upgrade section 4"
        />
      </Card>
    </div>
  )
};
```

`blur` (on by default) blurs the content underneath. Turn it off when people should still read the content while it refreshes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | What screen readers hear. |
| `blur` | `boolean` | `true` | Blur the content underneath. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-overlay` | The layer (`[data-blur]` when blurred) |

## Accessibility

The loader inside has `role="status"` and is named by `label` ("Loading" by default), so screen readers announce it. The layer blocks pointer presses, but not the keyboard: disable the form's controls too if editing must stop.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it to cover one panel, table or form, not the whole page.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for the first load. Use `Skeleton`, which shows the layout.

## Related

- **Loader**, **Skeleton**.
- **DataTable**: has its own loading state.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-feedback-loadingoverlay--docs

---

# Skeleton

Import: `import { Skeleton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A grey placeholder shape that stands in for content while it loads, so the page doesn't jump when the content arrives.

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const ListItem = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, maxWidth: 360 }}>
    {[1, 2, 3].map((n) => (
      <div key={n} style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
        <Skeleton circle height={40} />
        <div style={{ flex: 1, display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
          <Skeleton height={14} width="70%" />
          <Skeleton height={12} width="40%" />
        </div>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Skeleton height={20} width="60%" animate />;
```

## Examples

### Shapes

Set `width` and `height` (any CSS length, or pixels), `circle` for a circle of `height`, and `radius` for the corners. Build the same layout as the content that will load.

```tsx
const ListItem = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, maxWidth: 360 }}>
    {[1, 2, 3].map((n) => (
      <div key={n} style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
        <Skeleton circle height={40} />
        <div style={{ flex: 1, display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
          <Skeleton height={14} width="70%" />
          <Skeleton height={12} width="40%" />
        </div>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### Wrap the content

Wrap the real content and pass `visible`: while `true`, the skeleton shows at the content's size. Once `false`, the content shows.

```tsx
const WrapContent = () => {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12, maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <Button
        size="sm"
        variant="default"
        onClick={() => setLoading((l) => !l)}
      >
        {loading ? 'Finish loading' : 'Load again'}
      </Button>
      <Skeleton visible={loading}>
        <Card title="Contract value" description="Including variations">
          RM 1,250,000.00
        </Card>
      </Skeleton>
    </div>
  )
};
```

```tsx
<Skeleton visible={query.isLoading}>
  <ContractSummary contract={query.data} />
</Skeleton>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `string \| number` |  |  |
| `height` | `string \| number` |  |  |
| `circle` | `boolean` |  | A circle of `height`. |
| `radius` | `string \| number` | `the theme radius` | Corner radius, any CSS length. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Animate the shimmer. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the skeleton instead of `children` while true; show `children` once false. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-skeleton` | The shape (`[data-animate]` while shimmering) |
| `.kit-skeleton__ghost` | The hidden content inside, when wrapping |

The shape uses the `muted` token.

## Accessibility

Skeletons are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`). Tell assistive technology that the region is loading another way, for example `aria-busy` on the container.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Match the real layout closely: same number of lines, same avatar size.

**Don't**

- Don't use skeletons for content that loads in under 300ms.

## Related

- **Loader**, **LoadingOverlay**.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-feedback-skeleton--docs

# Avatar

Import: `import { Avatar } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A person's picture, with their initials while it loads, if it fails, or when there's no picture.

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Initials = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    <Avatar name="Aisyah Rahman" />
    <Avatar name="Lim Wei Jie" />
    <Avatar name="Muthu" />
    <Avatar src="/missing.png" name="Broken Image" />
    <Avatar />
  </div>
);
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Avatar src={portrait(200)} name="Aisyah Rahman" size="md" radius="full" />;
```

## Examples

### Initials and fallback

`name` gives the initials (up to two letters) and the image's alt text. Without a name, `fallback` shows instead, or a blank circle.

```tsx
const Initials = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    <Avatar name="Aisyah Rahman" />
    <Avatar name="Lim Wei Jie" />
    <Avatar name="Muthu" />
    <Avatar src="/missing.png" name="Broken Image" />
    <Avatar />
  </div>
);
```

### Sizes and shape

`size` takes a preset (`xs` 20px to `xl` 64px) or a number of pixels. `radius="md"` makes it a rounded square, for organisations rather than people.

```tsx
const Sizes = args => <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Avatar key={size} {...args} size={size} />
    ))}
    <Avatar src={portrait(200)} name="Aisyah Rahman" radius="full" size={80} />
</div>;
```
```tsx
const Square = () => <Avatar src={portrait(200)} name="Aisyah Rahman" size="lg" radius="md" />;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `alt` | `string` |  | Alt text for the image. Defaults to `name`. |
| `name` | `string` |  | A person's name: its initials show while the image loads or if it fails. |
| `size` | `number \| Size \| "xl"` | `md` | Preset or pixels. |
| `radius` | `enum` | `full` |  |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown instead of initials when there's no name. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-avatar` | The avatar (`[data-radius]`) |
| `.kit-avatar__image` | The image |
| `.kit-avatar__fallback` | The initials or fallback |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Avatar](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/avatar). The image's alt text is `alt`, or `name`. When the name is already written next to the avatar, pass `alt=""` so screen readers don't read it twice.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Always pass `name`, so there's a fallback.

**Don't**

- Don't use an avatar as the only way to identify someone. Show their name nearby.

## Related

- **ActionMenu**: an account menu with the avatar as its trigger.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-avatar--docs

# Badge

Import: `import { Badge } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A short label for a status, a category or a count.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Statuses = () => {
  const status = {
    Draft: 'neutral',
    'In review': 'info',
    Approved: 'success',
    Overdue: 'warning',
    Rejected: 'danger',
  } as const
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      {Object.entries(status).map(([label, color]) => (
        <Badge key={label} color={color} variant="dot">
          {label}
        </Badge>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
};
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Badge color="success" variant="light" size="sm">Published</Badge>;
```

## Examples

### Colours and variants

Six colours (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`) in four variants: `light` (tinted, default), `filled`, `outline` and `dot` (a coloured dot beside plain text).

```tsx
const ColorsAndVariants = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
    {variants.map((variant) => (
      <div
        key={variant}
        style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}
      >
        {colors.map((color) => (
          <Badge key={color} {...args} variant={variant} color={color}>
            {color}
          </Badge>
        ))}
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

### Statuses

Map each status to a colour once and reuse the map, so a status looks the same on every page.

```tsx
const Statuses = () => {
  const status = {
    Draft: 'neutral',
    'In review': 'info',
    Approved: 'success',
    Overdue: 'warning',
    Rejected: 'danger',
  } as const
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      {Object.entries(status).map(([label, color]) => (
        <Badge key={label} color={color} variant="dot">
          {label}
        </Badge>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
};
```

```tsx
const statusColor = { draft: 'neutral', review: 'info', approved: 'success', rejected: 'danger' } as const

<Badge color={statusColor[pkg.status]} variant="dot">{statusLabel[pkg.status]}</Badge>
```

### Sizes, icons and counts

```tsx
const Sizes = (args) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center' }}>
    {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const).map((size) => (
      <Badge key={size} {...args} size={size}>
        Size {size}
      </Badge>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```
```tsx
const WithIconAndCount = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
    <Badge color="success" leftSection={<icons.CheckIcon />}>
      Verified
    </Badge>
    <Badge color="primary" variant="filled">
      12
    </Badge>
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `enum` | `light` | `light`: tinted. `filled`: solid. `outline`: bordered. `dot`: a coloured dot and text. |
| `size` | `enum` | `sm` |  |
| `leftSection` | `ReactNode` |  |  |

Other `<span>` attributes pass through.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-badge` | The badge (`[data-color]`, `[data-variant]`, `[data-size]`) |
| `.kit-badge__dot` | The dot (`variant="dot"`) |
| `.kit-badge__section` | The left section |

Colours come from the `success`, `warning`, `info`, `destructive` and `primary` tokens.

## Accessibility

A badge is plain text. Don't rely on its colour alone to carry meaning: the text must say the status. For a count, add context for screen readers, like `aria-label="12 unread"`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep it to one or two words.
- Use the same colour for the same meaning across the app.

**Don't**

- Don't make badges clickable. Use `Chip` or `Button`.

## Related

- **Chip**: a label that toggles.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-badge--docs

# Card

Import: `import { Card } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A surface that groups related content, with an optional header (title, description, actions) and footer.

```tsx
import { Card } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const WithActionsAndFooter = () => <Card
    title="Contract"
    description="Key dates and value"
    padding="md"
    withBorder
    actions={(<>
      <Badge color="success">Active</Badge>
      <ActionMenu
        aria-label="Contract actions"
        align="end"
        items={[{ label: 'Edit' }, { label: 'Download PDF' }]}
      />
    </>)}
    footer={(<div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'flex-end', gap: 8 }}>
      <Button variant="default" size="sm">
        View history
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm">Open contract</Button>
    </div>)}>(<dl
      style={{
        margin: 0,
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr',
        gap: '6px 16px',
      }}
    >
      <dt>Value</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>RM 1,250,000.00</dd>
      <dt>Start</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>1 Dec 2026</dd>
      <dt>End</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>30 Nov 2027</dd>
    </dl>)</Card>;
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Card
    title="Contract"
    description="Key dates and value"
    padding="md"
    withBorder>(<dl
      style={{
        margin: 0,
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr',
        gap: '6px 16px',
      }}
    >
      <dt>Value</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>RM 1,250,000.00</dd>
      <dt>Start</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>1 Dec 2026</dd>
      <dt>End</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>30 Nov 2027</dd>
    </dl>)</Card>;
```

## Examples

### Header and footer

`title` and `description` make the header. `actions` sit at its top right: buttons, a badge or an `ActionMenu`. `footer` runs along the bottom.

```tsx
const WithActionsAndFooter = () => <Card
    title="Contract"
    description="Key dates and value"
    padding="md"
    withBorder
    actions={(<>
      <Badge color="success">Active</Badge>
      <ActionMenu
        aria-label="Contract actions"
        align="end"
        items={[{ label: 'Edit' }, { label: 'Download PDF' }]}
      />
    </>)}
    footer={(<div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'flex-end', gap: 8 }}>
      <Button variant="default" size="sm">
        View history
      </Button>
      <Button size="sm">Open contract</Button>
    </div>)}>(<dl
      style={{
        margin: 0,
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr',
        gap: '6px 16px',
      }}
    >
      <dt>Value</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>RM 1,250,000.00</dd>
      <dt>Start</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>1 Dec 2026</dd>
      <dt>End</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>30 Nov 2027</dd>
    </dl>)</Card>;
```

### Plain surface

Leave out the header for a plain box. `padding` goes from `none` to `lg`, and `withBorder={false}` removes the border.

```tsx
const Plain = () => <Card title={undefined} description={undefined} padding="lg" withBorder>(<dl
      style={{
        margin: 0,
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr',
        gap: '6px 16px',
      }}
    >
      <dt>Value</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>RM 1,250,000.00</dd>
      <dt>Start</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>1 Dec 2026</dd>
      <dt>End</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>30 Nov 2027</dd>
    </dl>)</Card>;
```

### Page sections

`component` renders a `section`, `article` or `aside` instead of a `div`. The title then labels the element, so it appears as a named region for screen readers.

```tsx
const AsSection = () => <Card
    title="Contract summary"
    description="Key dates and value"
    padding="md"
    withBorder
    component="section">(<dl
      style={{
        margin: 0,
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr',
        gap: '6px 16px',
      }}
    >
      <dt>Value</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>RM 1,250,000.00</dd>
      <dt>Start</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>1 Dec 2026</dd>
      <dt>End</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>30 Nov 2027</dd>
    </dl>)</Card>;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons or a menu at the top right. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Content along the bottom. |
| `padding` | `enum` | `md` | Inner padding. |
| `withBorder` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw a border. |
| `component` | `enum` | `div` | Render as another element, like `section` or `article`. |

Other HTML attributes pass through.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-card` | The card (`[data-padding]`, `[data-border]`) |
| `.kit-card__header` | The header row |
| `.kit-card__title`, `.kit-card__description` | The header text |
| `.kit-card__actions` | The actions |
| `.kit-card__body` | The content |
| `.kit-card__footer` | The footer |

The card uses the `surfaceRaised`, `border` and `radiusLg` tokens.

## Accessibility

A `div` card is just a container. With `component="section"` (or `article`, `aside`) and a `title`, the element is labelled by the title, so screen-reader users can jump to it.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use cards to separate independent chunks: a summary, a related list, a chart.

**Don't**

- Don't nest cards inside cards.
- Don't make a whole card clickable and also put buttons in it.

## Related

- **EmptyState**: what a card shows when it has nothing yet.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs

---

# EmptyState

Import: `import { EmptyState } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

What to show where a list or page has nothing yet: say what's missing and how to fix it.

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <EmptyState
    title="No packages yet"
    description="Packages you create show up here."
    action={<Button leftSection={<icons.PlusIcon />}>Add package</Button>} />;
```

## Examples

### No results

After a search or filter, say why it's empty and offer a way back, like clearing the filters. `icon` replaces the default inbox icon.

```tsx
const NoResults = () => <EmptyState
    title="No matching work orders"
    description="Try another search or clear the filters."
    action={<Button variant="default">Clear filters</Button>}
    icon={<icons.SearchIcon />} />;
```

### Title only

```tsx
const TitleOnly = () => <EmptyState title="Nothing to review" description={undefined} action={undefined} />;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | `an inbox icon` |  |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | A button or link to recover, like "Add package". |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-empty` | The wrapper |
| `.kit-empty__icon` | The icon |
| `.kit-empty__title`, `.kit-empty__description` | The text |
| `.kit-empty__action` | The action |

## Accessibility

The icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers. The title and description are plain text, so they're read in order.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Tell people what will appear here and give them the action that creates it.
- Tell "nothing yet" apart from "nothing matches": they need different actions.

**Don't**

- Don't show an empty state while data is still loading. Use `Skeleton`.

## Related

- **DataTable**: shows an empty state when there are no rows.
- **Skeleton**: while loading.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-emptystate--docs

# ImagePreviewer

Import: `import { ImagePreviewer } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A thumbnail that opens the image full screen, with zoom. Use it for site photos and other uploaded images.

```tsx
import { ImagePreviewer } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Gallery = () => (
  <div
    style={{
      display: 'grid',
      gap: 16,
      gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fill, 200px)',
    }}
  >
    {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((n) => (
      <ImagePreviewer
        key={n}
        src={photo(n)}
        alt={`Site photo ${n}`}
        label={`IMG_20${n}1.jpg`}
        meta="12 Nov 2026"
        fileSize={245_000 * n}
      />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Playground

```tsx
const Playground = () => <ImagePreviewer
    src={photo(1, 'Pothole at KM 12')}
    alt="Pothole at KM 12"
    label="IMG_2041.jpg"
    meta="12 Nov 2026"
    fileSize={245_000}
    width={240}
    height={160} />;
```

## Examples

### Gallery

`label` and `meta` caption the thumbnail, like the file name and upload date. `fileSize` (bytes) shows in the viewer's header. The thumbnail fills its container's width by default and is 160px tall: set `width` and `height` to change it.

```tsx
const Gallery = () => (
  <div
    style={{
      display: 'grid',
      gap: 16,
      gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fill, 200px)',
    }}
  >
    {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((n) => (
      <ImagePreviewer
        key={n}
        src={photo(n)}
        alt={`Site photo ${n}`}
        label={`IMG_20${n}1.jpg`}
        meta="12 Nov 2026"
        fileSize={245_000 * n}
      />
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `alt` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | A caption under the thumbnail, like the file name. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | Secondary caption, like the upload date. |
| `fileSize` | `number` |  | Shown in the viewer header. |
| `width` | `string \| number` | `100%` | Thumbnail width, any CSS length. |
| `height` | `string \| number` | `160` | Thumbnail height. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-image-preview` | The thumbnail and caption |
| `.kit-image-preview__thumb` | The thumbnail button |
| `.kit-image-preview__label`, `.kit-image-preview__meta` | The caption |
| `.kit-viewer` | The full-screen viewer |
| `.kit-viewer__bar`, `.kit-viewer__title`, `.kit-viewer__size` | The viewer's header |
| `.kit-viewer__tools` | Zoom and close buttons |
| `.kit-viewer__stage` | The image area |

## Accessibility

The thumbnail is a button named "Open" plus the image's `alt`. The viewer is a modal dialog built on [ui-sdk Dialog](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/dialog): focus moves in, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the thumbnail. The Zoom in, Zoom out and Close buttons are named.

Always write a real `alt` that describes the photo: "Pothole at KM 12", not "IMG_2041".

## Related

- **FileInput**: `preview="cards"` shows thumbnails while uploading.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-imagepreviewer--docs

# ScrollArea

Import: `import { ScrollArea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A scrollable box with slim scrollbars that match the theme. Scrolling stays native, so touchpads, wheels and keyboards work as usual.

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <ScrollArea height={240} type="hover" aria-label="Notifications">(<ul style={{ margin: 0, padding: 0, listStyle: 'none' }}>
      {notifications.map((n) => (
        <li
          key={n.id}
          style={{
            padding: '10px 12px',
            borderBottom: '1px solid var(--ui-border)',
          }}
        >
          {n.text}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>)</ScrollArea>;
```

## Examples

### Height

`height` fixes the box's height. `maxHeight` lets it grow with the content up to that height, then scroll.

```tsx
const MaxHeight = () => <ScrollArea
    height={undefined}
    type="always"
    aria-label="Notifications"
    maxHeight={200}
    offsetScrollbars>(<ul style={{ margin: 0, padding: 0, listStyle: 'none' }}>
      {notifications.map((n) => (
        <li
          key={n.id}
          style={{
            padding: '10px 12px',
            borderBottom: '1px solid var(--ui-border)',
          }}
        >
          {n.text}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>)</ScrollArea>;
```

### When scrollbars show

`type` sets when the scrollbars appear: on `hover` (default), `always`, while scrolling (`scroll`), or when the content overflows (`auto`). `offsetScrollbars` keeps space for the scrollbar so content doesn't sit under it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `height` | `string \| number` |  | Fixed height, any CSS length. |
| `maxHeight` | `string \| number` |  | Grow with the content up to this height, then scroll. |
| `type` | `enum` | `hover` | When scrollbars show. |
| `offsetScrollbars` | `boolean` |  | Keep space for the scrollbar so content doesn't sit under it. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Name the region when it holds meaningful content. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-scroll` | The box (`[data-offset]`) |
| `.kit-scroll__viewport` | The scrolling element |
| `.kit-scroll__content` | Your content |
| `.kit-scroll__bar`, `.kit-scroll__thumb` | A scrollbar and its handle |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Scroll Area](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/scroll-area). When the area holds meaningful content, give it an `aria-label`: the scrolling element then becomes a named region that screen-reader users can find.

## Usage guidelines

**Don't**

- Don't put scroll areas inside scroll areas.
- Don't make the main page content scroll inside a box. Let the page scroll.

## Related

- **Dialog**: its body already scrolls when content is tall.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-scrollarea--docs

---

# Timeline

Import: `import { Timeline } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

A vertical list of events: an activity log, an audit trail, or a workflow's stages. It comes plain, or as cards in SWIFTO's style, with stages alternating left and right.

```tsx
import { Timeline, type TimelineEvent } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Activity = () => <Timeline
    events={[
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Package submitted',
        actor: 'Aisyah Rahman',
        dateTime: '2026-11-10T09:12',
        time: '10 Nov, 9:12 AM',
        status: 'success' as const,
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        title: 'Returned for changes',
        actor: 'Lim Wei Jie',
        description: 'Bill of quantities is missing the drainage items.',
        dateTime: '2026-11-11T14:32',
        time: '11 Nov, 2:32 PM',
        status: 'warning' as const,
      },
      {
        id: '3',
        title: 'Resubmitted',
        actor: 'Aisyah Rahman',
        dateTime: '2026-11-12T10:05',
        time: '12 Nov, 10:05 AM',
        status: 'info' as const,
        metadata: [
          { label: 'Version', value: '2' },
          { label: 'Files', value: '3 attachments' },
        ],
      },
      { id: '4', title: 'Awaiting approval', status: 'pending' as const },
    ]}
    variant="activity"
    aria-label="Package history" />;
```

## Examples

### Events

Each event needs an `id` and a `title`. Add any of:

- `actor`: who did it, beside the title.
- `dateTime` (machine-readable, for the `<time>` element) and `time` (what's shown).
- `description`, and `metadata` as label/value pairs.
- `status` to colour the marker: `success`, `error`, `pending`, `info`, `warning` or `neutral`.
- `icon` inside the marker.
- For workflows: `department` and `stage` (shown after the actor as "Aina, Planning & Verification"), `reason` (like a rejection reason) and `sentFrom` (`{ name, department?, stage? }`, shown as a "Sent from" block).
- `date`, shown with `time`.

```tsx
<Timeline
  aria-label="Package history"
  events={history.map((h) => ({
    id: h.id,
    title: h.action,
    actor: h.user.name,
    dateTime: h.createdAt,
    time: formatDateTime(h.createdAt),
    status: h.action === 'Rejected' ? 'error' : 'success',
  }))}
/>
```

### Stages

`variant="status"` is roomier, for a workflow's stages rather than a dense log.

```tsx
const Stages = () => <Timeline
    events={[
      {
        id: 'a',
        title: 'Drafted',
        status: 'success',
        icon: <icons.CheckIcon />,
        time: '3 Nov',
      },
      {
        id: 'b',
        title: 'Engineer review',
        status: 'success',
        icon: <icons.CheckIcon />,
        time: '5 Nov',
      },
      {
        id: 'c',
        title: 'Finance review',
        status: 'pending',
        description: 'With Finance since 6 Nov.',
      },
      { id: 'd', title: 'Director approval', status: 'neutral' },
    ]}
    variant="status"
    aria-label="Approval stages" />;
```

### Cards, alternating left and right

`appearance="card"` puts each event in a bordered card coloured by its status. With `variant="status"` the markers grow and show a status icon (a tick, a cross, a clock…), and the time shows as a pill. `alternating` adds SWIFTO's zigzag: a centred line, with events alternating left and right and the time on the opposite side.

```tsx
const AlternatingCards = () => <Timeline
    events={[
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Work order created',
        actor: 'Afiq Rahman',
        department: 'Planning Office',
        stage: 'Planning',
        description: 'Initial creation of the work order.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-22T12:09',
        time: '22 Mar 2026, 12:09',
        status: 'success',
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        title: 'Submitted for verification',
        actor: 'Nadia Farhana',
        department: 'Engineering',
        stage: 'Submission',
        description: 'Details reviewed and forwarded to verification.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-23T09:30',
        time: '23 Mar 2026, 09:30',
        status: 'success',
        sentFrom: { name: 'Afiq Rahman', stage: 'Planning' },
      },
      {
        id: '3',
        title: 'Work order rejected',
        actor: 'Nurin Izzati',
        department: 'Approvals Committee',
        stage: 'Approval',
        reason: 'Rejected due to missing cost breakdown and unclear scope.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-24T15:02',
        time: '24 Mar 2026, 15:02',
        status: 'error',
        sentFrom: { name: 'Rafidah Noor', stage: 'Verification' },
      },
      {
        id: '4',
        title: 'Awaiting resubmission',
        actor: 'Afiq Rahman',
        department: 'Planning Office',
        status: 'pending',
        time: 'Pending',
      },
    ]}
    variant="status"
    aria-label="Work order history"
    appearance="card"
    alternating />;
```

```tsx
<Timeline
  variant="status"
  appearance="card"
  alternating
  aria-label="Work order history"
  events={history.map((h) => ({
    id: h.uuid,
    title: h.action,
    actor: h.user.name,
    department: h.user.department,
    stage: h.stage,
    reason: h.remarks,
    sentFrom: h.from ? { name: h.from.name, stage: h.from.stage } : undefined,
    dateTime: h.created_at,
    time: formatDateTime(h.created_at),
    status: h.action === 'Rejected' ? 'error' : 'success',
  }))}
/>
```

The colours come from the theme. A finished stage (`success`) and the time pill use `primary`, so with `swiftoTheme` they're SWIFTO's gold, and with the neutral theme they're blue. Errors use `destructive` and pending stages use `warning`. It works in dark mode like everything else.

When the timeline is narrower than 40rem, the zigzag falls back to one column, so it still fits a side panel or a phone. You can also leave `alternating` off:

```tsx
const StageCards = () => <Timeline
    events={[
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Work order created',
        actor: 'Afiq Rahman',
        department: 'Planning Office',
        stage: 'Planning',
        description: 'Initial creation of the work order.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-22T12:09',
        time: '22 Mar 2026, 12:09',
        status: 'success',
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        title: 'Submitted for verification',
        actor: 'Nadia Farhana',
        department: 'Engineering',
        stage: 'Submission',
        description: 'Details reviewed and forwarded to verification.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-23T09:30',
        time: '23 Mar 2026, 09:30',
        status: 'success',
        sentFrom: { name: 'Afiq Rahman', stage: 'Planning' },
      },
      {
        id: '3',
        title: 'Work order rejected',
        actor: 'Nurin Izzati',
        department: 'Approvals Committee',
        stage: 'Approval',
        reason: 'Rejected due to missing cost breakdown and unclear scope.',
        dateTime: '2026-03-24T15:02',
        time: '24 Mar 2026, 15:02',
        status: 'error',
        sentFrom: { name: 'Rafidah Noor', stage: 'Verification' },
      },
      {
        id: '4',
        title: 'Awaiting resubmission',
        actor: 'Afiq Rahman',
        department: 'Planning Office',
        status: 'pending',
        time: 'Pending',
      },
    ]}
    variant="status"
    aria-label="Work order history"
    appearance="card"
    alternating={false} />;
```

### Activity cards

With `variant="activity"`, cards get a dot with a soft ring, a dashed line, and a row with the `date` and `time` beside calendar and clock icons.

```tsx
const ActivityCards = () => <Timeline
    events={[
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Inspection completed',
        actor: 'Lim Wei Jie',
        description: 'Pothole at KM 12 measured and photographed.',
        date: '12 Nov 2026',
        time: '10:05 AM',
        dateTime: '2026-11-12T10:05',
        status: 'success',
        metadata: [
          { label: 'Route', value: 'R-12' },
          { label: 'Photos', value: '3' },
        ],
      },
      {
        id: '2',
        title: 'Contractor notified',
        description: 'Notice of defect sent to the contractor.',
        date: '12 Nov 2026',
        time: '11:40 AM',
        dateTime: '2026-11-12T11:40',
        status: 'info',
      },
      {
        id: '3',
        title: 'Repair overdue',
        description: 'No response within 48 hours.',
        date: '14 Nov 2026',
        time: '11:40 AM',
        dateTime: '2026-11-14T11:40',
        status: 'warning',
      },
    ]}
    variant="activity"
    aria-label="Activity log"
    appearance="card" />;
```

### Empty

```tsx
const Empty = () => <Timeline
    events={[]}
    variant="activity"
    aria-label="Package history"
    emptyMessage="No activity yet." />;
```

### Custom rendering

`renderIcon(event)` replaces an event's marker content, and `renderContent(event)` replaces its body (with cards, the title and card too). Your event type can carry extra fields: `Timeline` is generic over it.

`sentFromLabel` translates the "Sent from" label.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `events` (required) | `T[]` |  |  |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `'Timeline'` | Accessible name of the list. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `activity` | `activity`: dense, time first. `status`: roomier, for workflow stages. |
| `appearance` | `enum` | `plain` | `plain`: text beside small markers. `card`: each event in a bordered card coloured by its status. With `variant="status"`, card adds large markers with a status icon and shows the time as a pill; with `activity`, a ringed dot, a dashed line and a date and time row. |
| `alternating` | `boolean` | `false` | With `variant="status"`: a centred line with events alternating left and right, the time on the opposite side. Falls back to one column when the timeline is narrower than 40rem. |
| `sentFromLabel` | `ReactNode` | `Sent from` | Label of the `sentFrom` block, for translation. |
| `renderIcon` | `((event: T) => ReactNode)` |  | Replace an event's marker content. |
| `renderContent` | `((event: T) => ReactNode)` |  | Replace an event's body (title, time, description, metadata). |
| `emptyMessage` | `ReactNode` | `No activity yet` | Text while there are no events. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-timeline` | The list (`[data-variant]`, `[data-appearance]`, `[data-alternating]`) |
| `.kit-timeline__item` | One event |
| `.kit-timeline__marker` | The dot (`[data-status]`) |
| `.kit-timeline__connector` | The line between markers |
| `.kit-timeline__title`, `.kit-timeline__actor`, `.kit-timeline__time` | The heading |
| `.kit-timeline__description` | The description |
| `.kit-timeline__meta`, `.kit-timeline__meta-row` | The metadata |
| `.kit-timeline__reason` | The reason |
| `.kit-timeline__sent-from`, `.kit-timeline__sent-from-label` | The "Sent from" block |
| `.kit-timeline__card` | A card (`[data-status]`), with `appearance="card"` |
| `.kit-timeline__people` | The actor line in a card |
| `.kit-timeline__stamp`, `.kit-timeline__pill` | The time pill, with cards and `variant="status"` |
| `.kit-timeline__when`, `.kit-timeline__when-part` | The date and time row, with cards and `variant="activity"` |

The marker size is the CSS variable `--kit-tl-size` on `.kit-timeline`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Timeline](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/timeline). It's a list named by `aria-label` ("Timeline" by default), and the arrow keys move between events. Times use `<time dateTime>`, so assistive technology gets an exact value. Status colours are decorative: say the status in the title too.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Put the newest event first in an activity log, and the first stage first in a workflow.
- Name the timeline with `aria-label` when there's more than one on a page.

## Related

- **Badge**: a single status.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-data-display-timeline--docs
