# Accordion

Import: `import { Accordion } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Sections that expand and collapse under their headings, like an FAQ or optional form sections.

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Accordion
    items={[
      {
        value: 'submit',
        title: 'How do I submit a package?',
        content:
          'Open the package, check every tab is complete, then press Submit.',
      },
      {
        value: 'edit',
        title: 'Can I edit a package after submitting?',
        content:
          'Only while it is in review. Ask the reviewer to return it to you.',
      },
      {
        value: 'claims',
        title: 'When are claims paid?',
        content: 'Approved claims are paid at the end of the following month.',
      },
      {
        value: 'archived',
        title: 'Archived packages',
        content: '…',
        disabled: true,
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue={['submit']}
    multiple={false}
    variant="default"
    headingLevel={3}
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Items

Each item is `{ value, title, content }`, plus optional `icon` and `disabled`. `defaultValue` (or `value` with `onChange`) is the list of open items.

```tsx
<Accordion items={faqs.map((f) => ({ value: f.id, title: f.question, content: f.answer }))} />
```

### Separated

`variant="separated"` puts each item in its own card.

```tsx
const Separated = () => <Accordion
    items={[
      {
        value: 'submit',
        title: 'How do I submit a package?',
        content:
          'Open the package, check every tab is complete, then press Submit.',
      },
      {
        value: 'edit',
        title: 'Can I edit a package after submitting?',
        content:
          'Only while it is in review. Ask the reviewer to return it to you.',
      },
      {
        value: 'claims',
        title: 'When are claims paid?',
        content: 'Approved claims are paid at the end of the following month.',
      },
      {
        value: 'archived',
        title: 'Archived packages',
        content: '…',
        disabled: true,
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue={['submit']}
    multiple={false}
    variant="separated"
    headingLevel={3}
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

### Several open

Only one item is open at a time unless you set `multiple`.

```tsx
const Multiple = () => <Accordion
    items={[
      {
        value: 'submit',
        title: 'How do I submit a package?',
        content:
          'Open the package, check every tab is complete, then press Submit.',
      },
      {
        value: 'edit',
        title: 'Can I edit a package after submitting?',
        content:
          'Only while it is in review. Ask the reviewer to return it to you.',
      },
      {
        value: 'claims',
        title: 'When are claims paid?',
        content: 'Approved claims are paid at the end of the following month.',
      },
      {
        value: 'archived',
        title: 'Archived packages',
        content: '…',
        disabled: true,
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue={['submit', 'claims']}
    multiple
    variant="default"
    headingLevel={3}
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `AccordionItemData[]` |  |  |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | Open items. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` |  |  |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow several open at once. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `default` | `separated`: each item in its own card. |
| `headingLevel` | `enum` | `3` | The heading level of each title, for the page outline. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<AccordionPart, string>>` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-accordion` | `root` | The list |
| `.kit-accordion__item` | `item` | One section |
| `.kit-accordion__trigger` | `trigger` | The heading button |
| `.kit-accordion__chevron` | — | The arrow |
| `.kit-accordion__panel` | `panel` | The content |
| `[data-open]` | — | On an open item (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Accordion](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/accordion), which follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern. Each title is a button inside a heading, with `aria-expanded`. Set `headingLevel` (3 by default) so the headings fit the page outline.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | Opens or closes the focused item |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move between item headings |
| Home, End | First or last heading |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Write titles that say what's inside, so people can scan them.

**Don't**

- Don't hide information everyone needs inside an accordion.

## Related

- **Tabs**: one panel at a time, with the labels in a row.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-navigation-accordion--docs

---

# AppShell

Import: `import { AppShell } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

The page frame: a header, a sidebar, the main area and a footer. The sidebar can be full, a narrow rail or hidden, and below a breakpoint it becomes a drawer from the left. The kit handles the layout and behaviour; your app supplies the logo, the menu and the header, and keeps its own look.

```tsx
import { AppShell, useAppShell } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <SampleShell
    layout="sidebar"
    defaultSidebarState="full"
    collapsedState="mini"
    breakpoint="md"
    swipeToOpen={false}
    onSidebarStateChange={() => {}}
    onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}>{null}</SampleShell>;
```

## Examples

### Sidebar beside the header

The default, `layout="sidebar"`: the sidebar runs the full height on the left, with the header, main area and footer beside it.

```tsx
<AppShell>
  <AppShell.Header>
    <AppShell.MenuButton />
    <AppShell.SidebarToggle />
    <PageTitle />
  </AppShell.Header>
  <AppShell.Sidebar>
    <Navigation />
  </AppShell.Sidebar>
  <AppShell.Main>{children}</AppShell.Main>
  <AppShell.Footer>© 2026 OWL.AI</AppShell.Footer>
</AppShell>
```

### Header across the top

`layout="header"` puts the header and footer across the whole page, with the sidebar between them.

```tsx
const HeaderLayout = () => <SampleShell
    layout="header"
    defaultSidebarState="full"
    collapsedState="hidden"
    breakpoint="md"
    swipeToOpen={false}
    onSidebarStateChange={() => {}}
    onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}>{null}</SampleShell>;
```

### The mini rail

In the mini state the sidebar is `sidebarWidth.mini` wide (64px by default). Read `useAppShell().sidebarState` in your navigation to show icons only, with tooltips.

```tsx
const Mini = () => <SampleShell
    layout="sidebar"
    defaultSidebarState="mini"
    collapsedState="mini"
    breakpoint="md"
    swipeToOpen={false}
    onSidebarStateChange={() => {}}
    onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}>{null}</SampleShell>;
```

### Saving the state

Pass `sidebarState` and `onSidebarStateChange` to control it, and keep it wherever your app keeps settings. The kit doesn't save anything itself.

```tsx
const [state, setState] = useLocalStorage<AppShellSidebarState>('nav-state', 'full')

<AppShell sidebarState={state} onSidebarStateChange={setState}>…</AppShell>
```

```tsx
const Controlled = () => {
    const [state, setState] = useState<AppShellSidebarState>('full')

    return (
        <div>
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, padding: 12 }}>
                {(['full', 'mini', 'hidden'] as const).map((s) => (
                  <Button
                    key={s}
                    size="sm"
                    variant={state === s ? 'filled' : 'default'}
                    onClick={() => setState(s)}
                  >
                    {s}
                  </Button>
                ))}
            </div>
            <SampleShell
                layout="sidebar"
                defaultSidebarState="full"
                collapsedState="mini"
                breakpoint="md"
                swipeToOpen={false}
                onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}
                sidebarState={state}
                onSidebarStateChange={setState}>{null}</SampleShell>
        </div>
    );
};
```

### The toggle

`AppShell.SidebarToggle` switches between full and `collapsedState` (`"mini"`, or `"hidden"`). It sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and its name says what it will do: "Collapse sidebar" or "Expand sidebar". Pass `icon` to show your own icon.

```tsx
const Toggle = () => <SampleShell
    layout="sidebar"
    defaultSidebarState="full"
    collapsedState="mini"
    breakpoint={false}
    swipeToOpen={false}
    onSidebarStateChange={() => {}}
    onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}>{null}</SampleShell>;
```

### Compact screens

Below `breakpoint` (`"md"`, 62em, by default) the sidebar's children render in a drawer from the left instead. `AppShell.MenuButton` opens it, and it shows only on these screens; `SidebarToggle` hides. Inside the drawer, `useAppShell()` reads `sidebarState: "full"` and `inDrawer: true`. Call `closeMobile()` when a link is followed. `swipeToOpen` also opens it with a swipe from the left edge. `breakpoint={false}` keeps the sidebar beside the page at every width.

```tsx
const Compact = () => <SampleShell
    layout="sidebar"
    defaultSidebarState="full"
    collapsedState="mini"
    breakpoint="lg"
    swipeToOpen
    onSidebarStateChange={() => {}}
    onMobileOpenedChange={() => {}}>{null}</SampleShell>;
```

## Composition

| Part | Renders | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AppShell` | `div.kit-shell` | The state, and the parts below |
| `AppShell.Header` | `<header>` | Title, menu button, toggle, user menu |
| `AppShell.Sidebar` | `<nav aria-label="Main">`, or a drawer | Your navigation |
| `AppShell.Main` | `<main>` | The page; it scrolls on its own |
| `AppShell.Footer` | `<footer>` | Copyright, version |
| `AppShell.SidebarToggle` | `<button>` | Full ⇄ collapsed, beside the page only |
| `AppShell.MenuButton` | `<button>` | Opens the drawer, compact screens only |

`useAppShell()` returns `sidebarState`, `setSidebarState`, `toggleSidebar`, `compact`, `mobileOpened`, `openMobile`, `closeMobile`, `inDrawer` and `sidebarId`. Use it anywhere inside the shell.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | `Header`, `Sidebar`, `Main` and `Footer` parts, in any order. |
| `layout` | `enum` | `'sidebar'` | Where the sidebar sits. |
| `sidebarState` | `enum` |  | The sidebar's state. Pass it with `onSidebarStateChange` to control it, for example to save it. |
| `defaultSidebarState` | `enum` | `'full'` | The state it starts in, when uncontrolled. |
| `onSidebarStateChange` | `((state: AppShellSidebarState) => void)` |  | Called when the sidebar's state changes. |
| `collapsedState` | `enum` | `'mini'` | What `SidebarToggle` collapses the sidebar to. |
| `sidebarWidth` | `{ full?: string \| number; mini?: string \| number; } \| undefined` | `{ full: 300, mini: 64 }` | The sidebar's width when full and when mini: pixels or any CSS length. |
| `breakpoint` | `false \| AppShellBreakpoint` | `'md'` | Below this width the sidebar becomes a drawer that `MenuButton` opens. `false` keeps it beside the page at every width. |
| `mobileOpened` | `boolean` |  | Whether the drawer is open. Pass it with `onMobileOpenedChange` to control it. |
| `onMobileOpenedChange` | `((opened: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the drawer opens or closes. |
| `swipeToOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | On compact screens, a swipe from the left edge opens the drawer. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  |  |

## Styling

The layout is CSS grid, switched by media queries, so the page doesn't jump while it loads. Set these on `.kit-shell` (or with `style`):

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--kit-shell-bg` | `--kit-surface` | The page background |
| `--kit-shell-sidebar-bg` | transparent | The sidebar and drawer background |
| `--kit-shell-sidebar-full` | `300px` | Width when full (or `sidebarWidth.full`) |
| `--kit-shell-sidebar-mini` | `64px` | Width when mini (or `sidebarWidth.mini`) |
| `--kit-shell-drawer-width` | `min(20rem, 85vw)` | The drawer's width |
| `--kit-shell-transition` | `200ms` | How fast the width changes; `0ms` with reduced motion |

Attributes to style against: `data-layout`, `data-sidebar-state` (on the root and the sidebar), `data-compact` on the root, and `data-in-drawer` on the sidebar inside the drawer. Classes: `kit-shell`, `kit-shell__header`, `__sidebar`, `__main`, `__footer`, `__drawer`, `__backdrop`, `__toggle`, `__menu-button`.

The kit adds no padding, borders or cards: put your app's look on the parts with `className`.

## Accessibility

The drawer is built on [ui-sdk Drawer](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/drawer).

- The parts are landmarks: `banner`, `navigation` (named "Main"; change it with `aria-label`), `main` and `contentinfo`.
- Hidden, the sidebar stays in the page at zero width but out of reach of the keyboard and screen readers.
- The drawer is modal: focus moves in and stays there, the page behind is inert, and focus returns to the menu button when it closes. Its heading, "Menu" by default (`drawerTitle`), is read out when it opens.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the toggle | Switches the sidebar between full and collapsed |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> on the menu button | Opens the drawer |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the drawer, staying inside it |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the drawer |

## Usage guidelines

- **Do** keep your menu, logo and header in your app and pass them in as children.
- **Do** close the drawer when a link is followed (`closeMobile()`).
- **Don't** pad or round the shell's parts in the kit's CSS; style them in your app.
- **Don't** save the sidebar state inside the kit; control it and save it yourself.

## Related

- [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs) for sections within a page.
- [ActionMenu](?path=/docs/components-overlays-actionmenu--docs) for header menus.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-navigation-appshell--docs

---

# Breadcrumb

Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Shows where the current page sits in the app, with links back up the trail.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Breadcrumb
    items={[
      { label: 'Home', href: '#home' },
      { label: 'Packages', href: '#packages' },
      { label: 'Selangor', href: '#selangor' },
      { label: 'PKG-004' },
    ]} />;
```

## Examples

### Items

Each item is `{ label, href }`, with an optional `icon`. The last item is the current page and doesn't link.

### Your router's links

By default items render as `<a>`. Pass your router's link as `linkComponent` so navigation stays client-side. It receives `href`, `className` and `children`.

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link'

<Breadcrumb
  linkComponent={Link}
  items={[{ label: 'Packages', href: '/packages' }, { label: 'PKG-004' }]}
/>
```

```tsx
const WithRouterLink = () => <Breadcrumb
    items={[
      { label: 'Home', href: '#home' },
      { label: 'Packages', href: '#packages' },
      { label: 'Selangor', href: '#selangor' },
      { label: 'PKG-004' },
    ]}
    linkComponent={RouterLink} />;
```

### Long trails

`maxItems` collapses the middle items into an ellipsis when there are more than that many.

```tsx
const Collapsed = () => <Breadcrumb
    items={[
      { label: 'Home', href: '#home' },
      { label: 'Packages', href: '#packages' },
      { label: 'Selangor', href: '#selangor' },
      { label: 'Petaling', href: '#petaling' },
      { label: 'PKG-004', href: '#pkg-004' },
      { label: 'Route R-12' },
    ]}
    maxItems={3} />;
```

### Separator

```tsx
const CustomSeparator = () => <Breadcrumb
    items={[
      { label: 'Home', href: '#home' },
      { label: 'Packages', href: '#packages' },
      { label: 'Selangor', href: '#selangor' },
      { label: 'PKG-004' },
    ]}
    separator="/" />;
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `BreadcrumbItem[]` |  |  |
| `linkComponent` | `ComponentType<BreadcrumbLinkProps>` | `an `<a>`` | The link component, so the app's router handles navigation, like Next.js's `Link`. |
| `separator` | `ReactNode` | `a chevron` |  |
| `maxItems` | `number` |  | Collapse the middle items when there are more than this many. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `'Breadcrumb'` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-breadcrumb` | The `<nav>` |
| `.kit-breadcrumb__list`, `.kit-breadcrumb__item` | The list and one item |
| `.kit-breadcrumb__link` | A link |
| `.kit-breadcrumb__current` | The current page |
| `.kit-breadcrumb__separator` | A separator |
| `.kit-breadcrumb__gap` | The collapsed ellipsis |

## Accessibility

It's a `<nav>` named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`), holding an ordered list. The current page has `aria-current="page"`. Separators and the ellipsis are hidden from screen readers.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Put it at the top of detail pages, above the page title.

**Don't**

- Don't use it as the main navigation. It's a secondary aid.

## Related

- **Tabs**: navigation within one page.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-navigation-breadcrumb--docs

# Pagination

Import: `import { Pagination } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Page buttons with previous and next, for lists and tables split into pages.

```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Pagination total={12} defaultPage={3} siblings={1} boundaries={1} onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Controlled

`total` is the number of pages. `page` and `onChange` use page numbers starting at 1.

```tsx
const Controlled = args => {
    const [page, setPage] = useState(5)

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
            <Pagination
                total={12}
                siblings={1}
                boundaries={1}
                defaultPage={undefined}
                page={page}
                onChange={setPage} />
            <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Page {page}of {args.total}
            </p>
        </div>
    );
};
```

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['packages', page], queryFn: () => api.packages({ page }) })

<Pagination total={query.data?.meta.last_page ?? 1} page={page} onChange={setPage} />
```

### Siblings and boundaries

`siblings` is how many pages show either side of the current one, and `boundaries` how many always show at each end. Gaps show as an ellipsis.

```tsx
const SiblingsAndBoundaries = () => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
    <Pagination total={30} defaultPage={15} />
    <Pagination total={30} defaultPage={15} siblings={2} />
    <Pagination total={30} defaultPage={15} boundaries={2} />
  </div>
);
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `total` (required) | `number` |  | Number of pages. |
| `page` | `number` |  | The current page, starting at 1. |
| `defaultPage` | `number` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((page: number) => void)` |  | Called with the new page, starting at 1. |
| `siblings` | `number` | `1` | Pages shown either side of the current one. |
| `boundaries` | `number` | `1` | Pages always shown at each end. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `'Pagination'` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-pagination` | The `<nav>` |
| `.kit-pagination__list` | The list of pages |
| `.kit-pagination__link` | A page button (`[aria-current]` on the current page) |
| `.kit-pagination__control` | Previous and next |
| `.kit-pagination__ellipsis` | A gap |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Pagination](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/pagination). It's a `<nav>` named "Pagination" (change it with `aria-label` when there's more than one). The current page has `aria-current="page"`, and the arrows are named "Previous page" and "Next page".

## Related

- **DataTable**: has pagination built in.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs

# Tabs

Import: `import { Tabs } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Switches between panels of related content on the same page, like a record's Summary, Routes and Documents.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <Tabs
    aria-label="Package"
    tabs={[
      {
        value: 'summary',
        label: 'Summary',
        content: panel('Package summary, dates and value.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'routes',
        label: 'Routes',
        rightSection: <Badge size="xs">12</Badge>,
        content: panel('The 12 routes in this package.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'documents',
        label: 'Documents',
        content: panel('Contract, drawings and BQ.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'audit',
        label: 'Audit log',
        disabled: true,
        content: panel('Audit log'),
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue="summary"
    variant="line"
    orientation="horizontal"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```

## Examples

### Tabs as data

Each tab is `{ value, label, content }`, plus optional `icon`, `rightSection` (like a count) and `disabled`. Use `defaultValue` to pick the first tab, or `value` and `onChange` to control it, for example to keep the tab in the URL.

```tsx
<Tabs
  aria-label="Package"
  value={searchParams.get('tab') ?? 'summary'}
  onChange={(tab) => setSearchParams({ tab })}
  tabs={[
    { value: 'summary', label: 'Summary', content: <Summary /> },
    { value: 'routes', label: 'Routes', rightSection: <Badge>12</Badge>, content: <Routes /> },
  ]}
/>
```

### Variants and orientation

`variant="pills"` fills the selected tab. `orientation="vertical"` stacks the tabs on the left. `grow` stretches them across the list.

```tsx
const Pills = () => <Tabs
    aria-label="Package"
    tabs={[
      {
        value: 'summary',
        label: 'Summary',
        content: panel('Package summary, dates and value.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'routes',
        label: 'Routes',
        rightSection: <Badge size="xs">12</Badge>,
        content: panel('The 12 routes in this package.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'documents',
        label: 'Documents',
        content: panel('Contract, drawings and BQ.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'audit',
        label: 'Audit log',
        disabled: true,
        content: panel('Audit log'),
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue="summary"
    variant="pills"
    orientation="horizontal"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```
```tsx
const Vertical = () => <Tabs
    aria-label="Package"
    tabs={[
      {
        value: 'summary',
        label: 'Summary',
        content: panel('Package summary, dates and value.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'routes',
        label: 'Routes',
        rightSection: <Badge size="xs">12</Badge>,
        content: panel('The 12 routes in this package.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'documents',
        label: 'Documents',
        content: panel('Contract, drawings and BQ.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'audit',
        label: 'Audit log',
        disabled: true,
        content: panel('Audit log'),
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue="summary"
    variant="line"
    orientation="vertical"
    onChange={() => {}} />;
```
```tsx
const Grow = () => <Tabs
    aria-label="Package"
    tabs={[
      {
        value: 'summary',
        label: 'Summary',
        content: panel('Package summary, dates and value.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'routes',
        label: 'Routes',
        rightSection: <Badge size="xs">12</Badge>,
        content: panel('The 12 routes in this package.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'documents',
        label: 'Documents',
        content: panel('Contract, drawings and BQ.'),
      },
      {
        value: 'audit',
        label: 'Audit log',
        disabled: true,
        content: panel('Audit log'),
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue="summary"
    variant="line"
    orientation="horizontal"
    onChange={() => {}}
    grow />;
```

### Icons and a list action

`listRightSection` puts content at the end of the tab list, like a New button.

```tsx
const WithIconsAndAction = () => <Tabs
    aria-label="Package"
    tabs={[
      {
        value: 'list',
        label: 'List',
        icon: <icons.FileTextIcon />,
        content: panel('List view'),
      },
      {
        value: 'calendar',
        label: 'Calendar',
        icon: <icons.CalendarIcon />,
        content: panel('Calendar view'),
      },
    ]}
    defaultValue="list"
    variant="line"
    orientation="horizontal"
    onChange={() => {}}
    listRightSection={(<Button size="xs" leftSection={<icons.PlusIcon />}>New
            </Button>)} />;
```

### Tabs that only switch state

Leave out `content` and render what the tabs control yourself.

```tsx
const StateOnly = () => {
    const [view, setView] = useState('open')

    return (
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12 }}>
            <Tabs
                defaultValue="summary"
                orientation="horizontal"
                aria-label="Work orders"
                variant="pills"
                value={view}
                onChange={setView}
                tabs={[
                  { value: 'open', label: 'Open' },
                  { value: 'closed', label: 'Closed' },
                  { value: 'all', label: 'All' },
                ]} />
            <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Showing {view}work orders.</p>
        </div>
    );
};
```

Hidden panels unmount by default. Set `keepMounted` to keep their state, like a half-filled form, when switching.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` (required) | `TabItem[]` |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  |  |
| `variant` | `enum` | `line` | `line`: an underline under the selected tab. `pills`: a filled pill. |
| `orientation` | `enum` | `horizontal` |  |
| `grow` | `boolean` |  | Stretch the tabs across the list. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` |  | Keep hidden panels mounted, so their state survives switching. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the tab list. |
| `listRightSection` | `ReactNode` |  | Content at the end of the tab list, like a button. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<TabsPart, string>>` |  |  |

## Styling

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-tabs` | `root` | The wrapper (`[data-variant]`, `[data-orientation]`) |
| `.kit-tabs__list` | `list` | The tab list (`--grow` with `grow`) |
| `.kit-tabs__tab` | `tab` | One tab |
| `.kit-tabs__indicator` | — | The underline or pill that moves to the selected tab |
| `.kit-tabs__panel` | `panel` | A panel |
| `[data-selected]` | — | On the selected tab (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Tabs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/tabs), which follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern. The list is a `tablist` named by `aria-label`, and each panel is labelled by its tab. The tab list is one Tab stop.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight (ArrowUp, ArrowDown when vertical) | Move to the next or previous tab and show it |
| Home, End | First or last tab |
| Tab | Moves from the tab list into the panel |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep labels short, and the number of tabs under about six.
- Name the tab list with `aria-label`.

**Don't**

- Don't use tabs for steps that must be done in order. Use a stepper or separate pages.
- Don't use tabs to navigate between pages of the app.

## Related

- **SegmentedControl**: switch a view without separate panels.
- **Accordion**: when several sections can be open at once.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs

# ColorSchemeToggle

Import: `import { ColorSchemeToggle } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

An icon button that switches the app between light and dark. It shows a moon in light mode and a sun in dark mode.

```tsx
import { ColorSchemeToggle, useColorScheme } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
```

```tsx
const Playground = () => <ColorSchemeToggle />;
```

Pressing it here changes the whole docs page, just as it would in an app.

## Examples

### useColorScheme

For your own controls, like a Light / Dark / System setting, use the hook. It works anywhere under `UIKitProvider`.

```tsx
const WithHook = () => <SchemeReadout />;
```

```tsx
const { setting, colorScheme, setColorScheme, toggleColorScheme } = useColorScheme()
// setting: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto' (what the user chose)
// colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark' (in effect, after resolving 'auto')
```

The choice is saved in localStorage unless `UIKitProvider` has `persistColorScheme={false}`. Switching sets `color-scheme`, a `data-theme` attribute and a `dark` class on `<html>`, so app CSS and Tailwind's `dark:` variant follow it too.

## Props

Takes the **IconButton** props except `onClick` and `children`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `enum` | `'md'` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Styles, or a function of the part's state that returns them. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `'filled'` |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and blocks presses. A Promise returned from `onClick` does this on its own. |
| `type` | `enum` |  | What a native button does in a form: `"submit"` submits it and `"reset"` resets it. Ignored when the button renders as something else. @defaultValue "button" |
| `render` | `RenderProp<ButtonState>` |  | Renders your own element: one that receives the part's props, or a function of the props and the state. |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Keeps a disabled button in the tab order with `aria-disabled` instead of the native attribute, so it can hold focus while it becomes disabled and host a tooltip that says why. Presses still do nothing. @defaultValue false |
| `pendingAnnouncement` | `string` |  | What screen readers hear once the button has been pending for a second, so a slow action doesn't pass in silence. Set it in the page's language. An empty string says nothing. @defaultValue "Loading" |
| `debug` | `boolean` |  | Logs every state change with its reason to the console, in development builds. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |

## Accessibility

It's an `IconButton` named "Switch to dark mode" or "Switch to light mode", so the name says what pressing it will do. Pass `aria-label` to translate it.

## Related

- **UIKitProvider**: sets the starting scheme.
- **Theming**: how colours are defined for both schemes.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-theming-colorschemetoggle--docs

---

# DataTable

Import: `import { DataTable } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/table'`

A data grid built on AG Grid Community, with a toolbar (title, search, buttons, refresh), row actions, number formatting, and client-side or server-side pagination. It follows the kit's theme, dark mode included.

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/table'
```

`ag-grid-community` and `ag-grid-react` are optional peer dependencies of the kit. Install them in apps that use the `/table` entry.

```tsx
const ClientSide = () => <DataTable
    data={Array.from({ length: 57 }, (_, i) => ({
      uuid: `pkg-${i + 1}`,
      package_no: `PKG-${String(i + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`,
      name: `Road upgrade section ${i + 1}`,
      state: ['Selangor', 'Johor', 'Perak', 'Pahang'][i % 4],
      contract_amount: 150000 + i * 23750.5,
      progress_percentage: (i * 7) % 101,
      length_km: 2 + (i % 9) * 1.5,
      status: statuses[i % 4],
    }))}
    columns={[
      { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
      { field: 'name', headerName: 'Name', minWidth: 220 },
      { field: 'state', headerName: 'State' },
      {
        field: 'contract_amount',
        headerName: 'Contract Amount',
        type: 'currency',
      },
      {
        field: 'progress_percentage',
        headerName: 'Progress',
        type: 'percentage',
      },
      { field: 'length_km', headerName: 'Length (km)', type: 'number' },
    ]}
    title="Packages"
    buttons={[
      {
        label: 'Add package',
        icon: <icons.PlusIcon />,
        onClick: () => toast('Add package'),
      },
    ]}
    refresh={{ onClick: () => {} }}
    rowActions={({ rowData }) => ({
      options: { type: 'tripleDot' },
      items: [
        { label: 'Open', onClick: () => toast(`Open ${rowData.package_no}`) },
        { label: 'Duplicate' },
        { label: 'Delete', danger: true },
      ],
    })}
    tableSettings={{ getRowId: (p) => p.data.uuid }} />;
```

## Examples

### Basic usage

`data` is the rows and `columns` is a list of AG Grid column definitions. Give rows a stable id with `tableSettings.getRowId`.

```tsx
type Pkg = { uuid: string; package_no: string; name: string; contract_amount: number }

<DataTable<Pkg>
  title="Packages"
  data={packages}
  columns={[
    { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
    { field: 'name', headerName: 'Name', minWidth: 220 },
    { field: 'contract_amount', headerName: 'Contract Amount', type: 'currency' },
  ]}
  buttons={[{ label: 'Add package', icon: <PlusIcon />, onClick: openCreate }]}
  refresh={{ onClick: () => refetch(), isFetching }}
  tableSettings={{ getRowId: (p) => p.data.uuid }}
/>
```

### Toolbar

- `title` on the left.
- A search box (`hasFilters`, on by default) that filters every column on the client, or calls `onSearchChange` on the server.
- `buttons` on the right. Each is `{ label, onClick, icon, variant, disabled }`, or `{ type: 'custom', component }` for your own.
- `refresh`, a button that spins while `isFetching`, and `hasReport`, a print button.
- `createRowBtn`, a button under the grid for adding a row.

### Number formatting

Set `type` on a column to format it: `currency` (Malaysian ringgit by default), `percentage` or `number`. Set `numberFormatting` in `tableSettings` to change the locale or currency.

With `tableSettings.autoFormatColumns`, columns named like amounts, percentages or counts are formatted without a `type`, as SWIFTO did.

```tsx
const AutoFormattedColumns = () => <DataTable
    data={rows.slice(0, 10)}
    columns={[
      { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
      { field: 'contract_amount', headerName: 'Contract Amount' },
      { field: 'progress_percentage', headerName: 'Progress %' },
      { field: 'length_km', headerName: 'Length km' },
    ]}
    title="Auto-formatted (SWIFTO behaviour)"
    hasFilters={false}
    tableSettings={{
      autoFormatColumns: true,
      pagination: false,
      tableContainerMaxHeight: false,
      height: 420,
    }} />;
```

### Row actions

`rowActions` returns, for each row, the items and how to show them: `type: 'tripleDot'` for a ⋮ menu, or `type: 'icon'` for one icon button per action. They sit in a column pinned to the right.

```tsx
const IconActions = () => <DataTable
    data={rows.slice(0, 8)}
    columns={[
      { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
      { field: 'status', headerName: 'Status' },
    ]}
    hasFilters={false}
    rowActions={() => ({
      options: { type: 'icon' },
      items: [
        { label: 'Refresh row', icon: <icons.RefreshIcon /> },
        { label: 'Remove', icon: <icons.CloseIcon />, danger: true },
      ],
    })}
    tableSettings={{ pagination: false, height: 380 }} />;
```

```tsx
rowActions={({ rowData }) => ({
  options: { type: 'tripleDot' },
  items: [
    { label: 'Open', onClick: () => navigate(`/packages/${rowData.uuid}`) },
    { label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: () => confirmDelete(rowData) },
  ],
})}
```

### Server-side paging and search

With `serverSide: true`, the table shows `data` as the current page and asks you for others:

- `totalRows`: the total on the server.
- `currentPage` and `onPageChange`: pages start at **0** here (unlike `Pagination`, which starts at 1).
- `onSearchChange`: the search text, debounced by `searchDebounceMs` (500 by default).

```tsx
const ServerSide = () => {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(0)
  const [search, setSearch] = useState('')
  const filtered = useMemo(
    () =>
      rows.filter((r) => r.name.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())),
    [search],
  )
  return (
    <DataTable<Pkg>
      title="Server-side paging"
      data={filtered.slice(page * 10, page * 10 + 10)}
      columns={[
        { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
        { field: 'name', headerName: 'Name' },
        { field: 'contract_amount', headerName: 'Amount', type: 'currency' },
      ]}
      tableSettings={{
        serverSide: true,
        paginationPageSize: 10,
        totalRows: filtered.length,
        currentPage: page,
        onPageChange: setPage,
        onSearchChange: (value) => {
          setSearch(value)
          setPage(0)
        },
      }}
    />
  )
};
```

### Selection and totals

`rowSelection` (`'single'`, `'multiple'`, or AG Grid's options) adds checkboxes, and `onSelectionChanged` reports them. `pinnedBottomRowData` pins rows to the bottom, for totals.

```tsx
const SelectionAndTotals = () => <DataTable
    data={rows.slice(0, 6)}
    columns={[
      { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
      { field: 'contract_amount', headerName: 'Amount', type: 'currency' },
    ]}
    title="Selection and pinned totals"
    hasFilters={false}
    tableSettings={{
      rowSelection: { mode: 'multiRow' },
      pagination: false,
      height: 360,
      pinnedBottomRowData: [
        {
          package_no: 'Total',
          contract_amount: rows
            .slice(0, 6)
            .reduce((s, r) => s + r.contract_amount, 0),
        } as Pkg,
      ],
    }} />;
```

### Size

By default the grid is capped at 62% of the viewport height (`tableContainerMaxHeight`). Set `height` for a fixed height, or turn off `pagination` to show every row.

### Anything else

`gridRef` gives you the AG Grid API (`gridRef.current.api`). `tableSettings.gridOptions` passes any other AG Grid option, last, so it wins. For cell editing, see `editType`, `onCellValueChanged`, and the `NumberCellEditor` and `TextCellEditor` from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/table`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` (required) | `TData[]` |  | The rows. |
| `columns` (required) | `(ColDef<TData, any> \| ColGroupDef<TData>)[]` |  | AG Grid column definitions. Set `type: 'currency' \| 'percentage' \| 'number'` to format a column. |
| `gridRef` | `RefObject<AgGridReact<TData> \| null>` |  | A ref to the AgGridReact instance, for `gridRef.current.api`. |
| `rowActions` | `((args: { rowData: TData; rowIndex: number; }) => RowActionConfig \| null)` |  | Actions for each row, shown in a pinned column on the right. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `buttons` | `ToolbarButton[] \| (() => ToolbarButton[])` |  | Buttons at the right of the toolbar. |
| `refresh` | `{ onClick: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void; isFetching?: boolean; isLoading?: boolean; } \| undefined` |  | A refresh button; it spins while `isFetching`. |
| `hasReport` | `{ onClick: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void; }` |  | A report/print button. |
| `hasFilters` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the search box. |
| `withDivider` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw a line under the toolbar. |
| `createRowBtn` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void; leftSection?: ReactNode; className?: string; } \| null` |  | A button under the grid, for adding a row. |
| `tableSettings` | `DataTableSettings<TData>` |  |  |
| `theme` | `Theme` | `the kit theme, following the app's CSS variables` | The grid theme. |
| `renderIcon` | `((name: string, className?: string) => ReactNode)` |  | Turns string icons in row actions into nodes, like an Iconify name. |
| `labels` | `DataTableLabels` |  | Text for the built-in UI, for translation. |
| `icons` | `DataTableIcons` |  | Replace the built-in icons: the toolbar's refresh and report buttons, and the row menu trigger. |
| `classNames` | `Partial<Record<DataTablePart, string>>` |  | Classes for parts of the toolbar. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### tableSettings

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pagination` | `true` | Split rows into pages |
| `paginationPageSize` | `20` | Rows a page |
| `tableContainerMaxHeight` | `true` | Cap the grid at 62% of the viewport height |
| `height` | — | Fixed grid height, any CSS length. Overrides the cap |
| `getRowId` | — | Stable row ids, so updates keep selection and scroll |
| `rowSelection`, `onSelectionChanged` | `false` | Row selection |
| `enableSorting` / `enableFiltering` | `true` / `false` | Column sorting and AG Grid column filters |
| `showRowNumbers` | `true` | A "No." column with the row number |
| `rowHeight`, `headerHeight` | `45` | Heights in px |
| `serverSide`, `totalRows`, `currentPage`, `onPageChange` | — | Server-side paging (pages start at 0) |
| `onSearchChange`, `searchDebounceMs`, `initialSearchValue` | — / `500` | Search |
| `pinnedBottomRowData` | — | Rows pinned to the bottom |
| `autoFormatColumns`, `numberFormatting` | — | Number formatting |
| `editType`, `singleClickEdit`, `onCellValueChanged`… | — | Editing |
| `gridOptions` | — | Any other AG Grid option |

## Theming and styling

The grid uses an AG Grid theme built from the kit's CSS variables, so it follows the app's theme and colour scheme. Use `createAgGridTheme()` for your own variant, or pass AG Grid's own `theme`. The tokens `tableHeader`, `tableHeaderForeground` and `tableRowHover` style the header and row hover.

`classNames` adds classes to the toolbar's parts, and `className` to the wrapper.

## Translation

`labels` replaces the built-in text: `search`, `clearSearch`, `refresh`, `report`, `rowNumber`, `rowActions`, and `records`, a function that writes the record summary ("Record 1 to 20 out of 57" by default).

## Accessibility

AG Grid provides grid keyboard navigation (arrow keys between cells, Enter to edit) and ARIA grid roles. The kit's toolbar controls are named: the search box is "Search list", and the refresh and print buttons are named after what they do. Row action menus are named with `labels.rowActions`.

```tsx
const SearchFilters = () => <DataTable
    data={Array.from({ length: 57 }, (_, i) => ({
      uuid: `pkg-${i + 1}`,
      package_no: `PKG-${String(i + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`,
      name: `Road upgrade section ${i + 1}`,
      state: ['Selangor', 'Johor', 'Perak', 'Pahang'][i % 4],
      contract_amount: 150000 + i * 23750.5,
      progress_percentage: (i * 7) % 101,
      length_km: 2 + (i % 9) * 1.5,
      status: statuses[i % 4],
    }))}
    columns={[
      { field: 'package_no', headerName: 'Package No.' },
      { field: 'name', headerName: 'Name', minWidth: 220 },
    ]}
    title="Packages"
    tableSettings={{ getRowId: (p) => p.data.uuid, height: 360 }} />;
```

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep the row's main action obvious: make the key column a link, or put Open first in the row actions.
- Use server-side paging for more than a few thousand rows.

**Don't**

- Don't show more than about eight columns. Hide the rest or put them on the detail page.

## Related

- **Pagination**: for lists that aren't tables.
- **EmptyState**: for a table with no rows yet.
- **ActionMenu**: the row ⋮ menu.

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/components-table-datatable--docs

# FormFields

Import: `import { FormFields } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`

Renders a form from a config: each entry becomes the matching RHF field.
Must sit inside `<FormProvider>`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` (required) | `FormFieldsConfig` |  |  |
| `columns` | `number` | `1` | Columns at the top level. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Web page: https://adhamaa.github.io/C-UI-KIT-docs/?path=/docs/form-react-hook-form
